# PRD: Predict Data Readiness Preflight and Backfill

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.
> Historical repo snapshot: [`dev-plans/prd-predict-data-readiness-preflight-and-backfill.md`](https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/blob/27665e649dbda4b2567ddeb157d2c54c2ea8710e/dev-plans/prd-predict-data-readiness-preflight-and-backfill.md) at [`27665e649dbd`](https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/commit/27665e649dbda4b2567ddeb157d2c54c2ea8710e).
> Migration note: repo-local PRD files are historical only after GitHub-only PRD migration; update this issue body instead of editing repo markdown snapshots.

---

---
title: Predict Data Readiness Preflight and Backfill
slug: predict-data-readiness-preflight-and-backfill
created: 2026-05-01
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-01T15:02:38Z
status: done
series: predict
---

# PRD: Predict Data Readiness Preflight and Backfill

**Status:** Done; final verifier bug-check approved
**Planning purpose:** immediate Predict reliability implementation slice
**Primary area:** Model Training / Predict
**Priority:** before broader configuration interoperability work

## 1. Problem

Predict job creation can fail because the selected exchange, symbol, timeframe, or data range does not have enough stored candles for model training. The backend correctly rejects these jobs, but the user only learns after clicking Train, and until the recent silent-failure fix this could appear as no action at all.

Observed case:

- `hyperliquid:BTC:15m`
- 525 candles available
- 8,000 candles required

The product should not let users discover this through a failed training submit. Predict should preflight data readiness before training and offer an obvious backfill path when data is missing.

## 2. Product goal

Before a Predict job is submitted, the create modal should show whether the selected market has enough training data. If not, it should explain the gap and offer a button to backfill the required candles.

A user should be able to move from “not enough data” to “ready to train” without leaving the Predict create flow.

## 3. Strategic boundary

Predict remains Model Training-owned.

This PRD does not move Predict into Strategy Discovery and does not touch Adversarial Debate, Discovery method ownership, or Strategy Discovery handoff semantics.

## 4. In scope

- Predict create-modal data readiness preflight
- canonical backend readiness response for selected exchange, symbol, timeframe, and data range
- clear “not enough data / backfill needed” state in the modal
- disabled Train action while required data is missing
- Backfill Candles button in the modal for any user who can create Predict jobs
- backend bounds and rate limits for user-started backfills
- backfill scope selection with minimum required candles, maximum available or allowed history, and custom candle count between minimum and maximum
- backfill request that downloads the relevant historical candles for the selected Predict training context
- progress/status display for the started backfill job
- auto-polling while the modal is open, plus manual Refresh and Retry controls
- refresh/recheck after backfill completes
- preservation of backend submit-time validation as a safety net
- targeted tests for sufficient data, insufficient data, backfill start, and backend error fallback

## 5. Out of scope

- changing Predict model algorithms
- changing ensemble composition search
- changing Model Training import/evaluation/writeback behavior
- changing PRD 08 Backtest Evaluation scope
- Strategy Discovery or Adversarial Debate changes
- automatically starting model training after backfill completes
- privileged/admin-only backfill gating in the first slice
- broad data-feed admin redesign
- unbounded historical downloads outside backend limits
- backfilling every symbol/timeframe by default

## 6. User stories

### US-001: Preflight data before training
As a Predict user, I want the create modal to check candle readiness for my selected exchange, symbol, timeframe, and range before I submit training.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The modal checks readiness when opened and when exchange, symbol, timeframe, or data range changes.
- [ ] The UI shows candles available, minimum required, first timestamp, and last timestamp when available.
- [ ] The UI distinguishes ready, checking, insufficient, backfilling, failed, and unknown states.
- [ ] The check uses backend training-readiness rules rather than duplicating unrelated frontend-only thresholds.

### US-002: Explain insufficient data clearly
As a Predict user, I want missing data to be explained before I click Train.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] If data is insufficient, the primary message says “Not enough data to train.”
- [ ] The details show available candles and required candles.
- [ ] The Train button is disabled while required data is missing.
- [ ] If the backend still rejects submit, the modal displays the backend error inline.

### US-003: Start the right backfill from the modal
As a Predict user, I want one button that downloads the relevant candles for the selected training context.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The modal shows a Backfill Candles action when data is insufficient.
- [ ] The action is available to any user who can create Predict jobs, subject to backend bounds and rate limits.
- [ ] The action starts historical download for the selected exchange, symbol, and timeframe.
- [ ] The user can choose minimum required candles, maximum available or allowed history, or a custom candle count between those bounds.
- [ ] The minimum option is enough to satisfy Predict readiness for the selected training context.
- [ ] The maximum option respects backend/provider limits and explains if larger history is unavailable.
- [ ] Custom candle count validation prevents requests below the minimum or above the maximum.

### US-004: Track backfill progress and recheck readiness
As a Predict user, I want to know whether the backfill is running and when training is ready.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] After backfill starts, the modal shows the download job status.
- [ ] Backfill progress is tied to the exchange, symbol, timeframe, range, and candle-count selection that started the job.
- [ ] Changing the selected training context resets readiness/backfill state for the new context instead of reusing stale job status.
- [ ] The modal auto-polls while open until completion or failure.
- [ ] The modal also provides manual Refresh and Retry controls.
- [ ] Completion triggers a readiness recheck for the same context that started the backfill.
- [ ] When readiness becomes sufficient, the modal re-enables Train and shows “Data ready for training.”
- [ ] Failed backfill shows an actionable error and allows retry.
- [ ] Training does not auto-start after backfill completes.

### US-005: Provide an operator fallback script
As an operator, I want a direct script or command path for backfilling Predict training data outside the UI.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A documented backend command can backfill one exchange/symbol/timeframe for Predict training.
- [ ] The command uses the same lookback/minimum-candle logic as the UI path.
- [ ] The command reports candles downloaded and final readiness.
- [ ] The command avoids hardcoded product names and supports Hyperliquid/Binance-style symbol differences.

### US-006: Keep backend validation authoritative
As a developer, I want the backend to remain the source of truth so a stale frontend preflight cannot submit invalid training jobs.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Job creation still rejects insufficient data.
- [ ] Preflight and submit-time validation share thresholds or a common readiness helper.
- [ ] Range-specific readiness is checked for custom date ranges and lookback ranges.
- [ ] Tests cover total-count insufficiency and requested-range insufficiency.

## 7. Functional requirements

- FR-1: Predict create flow must call a backend readiness endpoint before training submit.
- FR-2: Readiness response must include `status`, `count`, `min_required`, `first_timestamp`, `last_timestamp`, and a user-facing reason when not ready.
- FR-3: Readiness must account for selected data range, not only total candle count.
- FR-4: Insufficient readiness must show a Backfill Candles action.
- FR-5: Backfill action must expose minimum required, maximum available or allowed, and custom candle-count choices.
- FR-6: Backfill action must start or reuse a historical download job for the selected market context.
- FR-7: Backend must enforce request bounds and rate limits for user-started backfills.
- FR-8: Backfill progress must be visible enough for the user to know whether to wait, retry, or change inputs.
- FR-9: Backfill progress must auto-poll while the modal is open and support manual refresh.
- FR-10: Readiness and backfill state must be keyed by selected training context to prevent stale status from enabling Train.
- FR-11: Backend job creation must continue to reject insufficient data even if preflight is skipped or stale.
- FR-12: Existing Predict create errors must remain visible inline.

## 8. UX requirements

Primary states should use concise copy:

- Ready: “Data ready for training.”
- Checking: “Checking training data…”
- Insufficient: “Not enough data to train.”
- Backfill available: “Backfill candles for this market.”
- Backfill scope: “Choose how much history to download.”
- Backfilling: “Downloading historical candles…”
- Backfill failed: “Backfill failed. Retry or choose another market.”

The primary surface should show the next action first. Deeper details such as timestamps, job IDs, and raw errors can sit below the primary message. After successful backfill and readiness recheck, Train is re-enabled; the user must still click Train explicitly.

## 9. Technical notes for shaping

Existing surfaces that may be reused or extended:

- `GET /api/v1/datafeed/{exchange}/ohlcv/count`
- `POST /api/v1/collectors/{exchange}/historical-download`
- `GET /api/v1/collectors/{exchange}/historical-download/{job_id}`
- Predict create backend validation in `backend/app/api/routers/guided_loop.py`
- Predict default lookback values in `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/schemas/ensembleSchema.ts`

CEO preference: add a canonical Predict readiness helper/endpoint rather than spreading threshold logic across the frontend.

## 10. Quality gates

Expected gates should be finalized during implementation review and may include:

- `pnpm --dir frontend typecheck`
- targeted frontend tests for Predict create-modal readiness states
- targeted frontend tests for Backfill Candles action, context changes during backfill, and backend-error fallback
- targeted backend tests for Predict readiness and submit-time insufficient-data rejection
- targeted backend tests for historical download request creation if a new endpoint/helper is added
- `git diff --check`

## 11. CEO decisions resolved

1. Backfill Candles is available to any user who can create Predict jobs, with backend bounds and rate limits.
2. Train is hard-disabled while readiness is insufficient; backend submit-time validation remains authoritative.
3. Backfill scope offers minimum required candles, maximum available or allowed history, and custom candle count between minimum and maximum.
4. The modal auto-polls backfill progress while open and also provides manual Refresh and Retry controls.
5. Successful backfill re-enables Train after readiness recheck; training does not auto-start.
6. This PRD is the immediate Predict reliability slice before broader configuration interoperability work.

## 12. Implementation shaping notes

- “Maximum available history” should be interpreted as the maximum the backend can safely request for the selected exchange, symbol, and timeframe under provider and platform limits.
- If true provider maximum is not knowable before a request, the backend should return the configured/requestable maximum and explain unavailable larger history in the UI.
- The custom candle-count field should be numeric, bounded, and validated before submission.

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.
> Historical repo snapshot: [`dev-plans/prd-hyperliquid-historical-data-bootstrap.md`](https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/blob/27665e649dbda4b2567ddeb157d2c54c2ea8710e/dev-plans/prd-hyperliquid-historical-data-bootstrap.md) at [`27665e649dbd`](https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/commit/27665e649dbda4b2567ddeb157d2c54c2ea8710e).
> Migration note: repo-local PRD files are historical only after GitHub-only PRD migration; update this issue body instead of editing repo markdown snapshots.

# PRD: Hyperliquid Historical Data Bootstrap

**Status:** CEO approved
**Planning purpose:** follow-on data-infrastructure slice after Predict readiness/backfill
**Primary area:** Datafeed / Model Training / Predict
**Priority:** high, because Hyperliquid native candle history cannot satisfy common Predict training windows for lower timeframes

## 1. Problem

Predict readiness now correctly identifies when our local OHLCV database lacks enough candles. For Hyperliquid, the native candle API only returns a recent-history window of roughly 5,000 candles. That is not enough for common Predict training contexts such as `BTC 15m`, where Predict requires around 8,000 candles.

A one-off TikTape integration can backfill a selected Predict context, but this still leaves us dependent on ad hoc user-triggered backfills and a live third-party subscription whenever deeper history is needed.

We need to bootstrap a durable Hyperliquid historical OHLCV dataset into our own database, across all TikTape-supported Hyperliquid assets and the key trading timeframes, then use our existing datafeed adapter system to keep the dataset fresh.

## 2. Product goal

Seed our canonical OHLCV database with full available Hyperliquid history across TikTape-supported assets and key timeframes, so Predict and other systems can train from our own data without runtime dependency on a third-party historical provider.

## 3. Strategic decision

Use TikTape as a temporary historical seed source, not as the long-term serving layer.

Our database remains canonical. Predict, backtests, dashboards, and readiness checks must read from our existing OHLCV storage. After seeding, TikTape may remain configured for a stabilization period, but only for explicit operator repair/backfill commands. The Hyperliquid datafeed adapter should own ongoing freshness, and TikTape should not become a normal runtime dependency.

## 4. CEO decisions resolved

1. V1 target universe is all TikTape-supported Hyperliquid assets, even if they are not yet configured in our adapter.
2. Bootstrap attempts full available TikTape history, bounded only by provider, storage, and operational safeguards.
3. V1 checkpointing uses durable local JSON artifacts under `backend/data/reports`, plus idempotent DB upserts.
4. First implementation slice is a BTC smoke seed for `15m` and `1h`, followed by Predict readiness verification.
5. V1 operator surface is CLI only; admin UI is deferred.
6. After the seed is complete and validated, keep the TikTape key for at least a 30-day stabilization period as an explicit repair/backfill fallback, then remove it only after native freshness verification passes.
7. Full all-asset seeding requires a dry-run/storage estimate report and explicit operator approval before execution.
8. V1 default concurrency is `3`, with operator override for slower or faster environments.

## 5. In scope

- TikTape-backed bulk historical seed command for Hyperliquid OHLCV data
- asset discovery for all TikTape-supported Hyperliquid assets
- timeframe coverage for `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `1h`, `4h`, and `1d`
- full available history download where provider and storage limits allow
- conversion from TikTape candle rows into our existing OHLCV schema
- idempotent upsert into the canonical `ohlcv_data` table
- checkpoint/resume support per symbol/timeframe using local JSON artifacts
- dry-run and verify-only modes
- gap detection/reporting after bootstrap
- bounded concurrency and rate-limit controls, defaulting to `3` concurrent symbol/timeframe downloads
- operational progress output suitable for long-running jobs
- secret-safe configuration via backend environment variables
- integration with existing Predict readiness checks after data lands
- post-seed freshness handoff to the native Hyperliquid datafeed adapter
- report of any seeded assets that are not yet covered by native freshness configuration

## 6. Out of scope

- replacing the existing datafeed adapter system
- making Predict train directly from TikTape
- building our own full historical exchange-data vendor in this slice
- changing Predict training algorithms or thresholds
- changing OHLCV table identity semantics unless implementation discovers a hard blocker
- seeding non-Hyperliquid exchanges
- tick/trade/orderbook historical ingestion
- admin UI for seed management in v1
- automated subscription management or billing workflows
- keeping TikTape as an always-on automatic runtime fallback after the bulk seed is validated

## 7. User stories

### US-001: Bulk seed Hyperliquid history
As an operator, I want a command that downloads deep Hyperliquid OHLCV history into our DB so Predict has enough local training data.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The command can seed Hyperliquid OHLCV from TikTape.
- [ ] The command supports `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `1h`, `4h`, and `1d`.
- [ ] The command can discover all TikTape-supported Hyperliquid assets.
- [ ] The command supports explicit `--symbols` for smoke tests and targeted reruns.
- [ ] Each candle is stored in our canonical OHLCV table with exchange `hyperliquid`.

### US-002: Resume safely after interruption
As an operator, I want the seed job to resume without duplicating or corrupting data.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Progress is checkpointed per symbol/timeframe in a local JSON artifact under `backend/data/reports`.
- [ ] Re-running the command skips or upserts existing candles safely.
- [ ] Partial failures are reported without losing successful symbol/timeframe work.
- [ ] The command can retry failed symbol/timeframe pairs.

### US-003: Keep Predict independent from TikTape
As a product owner, I want TikTape used only for seeding so training does not depend on a third-party historical provider.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Predict readiness reads only from our DB.
- [ ] Predict training reads only from our DB.
- [ ] TikTape API is not called during normal Predict job creation except when an explicit seed/backfill command is run.
- [ ] During the stabilization period, the TikTape key may remain configured for explicit operator repair/backfill.
- [ ] Disabling the TikTape key after stabilization does not break Predict readiness for seeded contexts.

### US-004: Verify data completeness
As an operator, I want a verification report so I know which assets/timeframes are ready for Predict.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Verification reports candle count, first timestamp, last timestamp, and gap count per symbol/timeframe.
- [ ] Verification identifies symbol/timeframe pairs below Predict minimums.
- [ ] Verification can run independently of downloading.
- [ ] Reports are saved to a durable artifact path.

### US-005: Protect secrets and provider limits
As a developer, I want the integration to be safe to operate without leaking API keys or overwhelming providers.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] API key is read from `TIKTAPE_API_KEY` or `HYPERLIQUID_HISTORICAL_API_KEY`.
- [ ] API key is never logged, committed, or returned in API responses.
- [ ] The command supports configurable concurrency.
- [ ] The command respects provider request limits and backs off on rate-limit or transient failures.

### US-006: Hand off freshness to our adapter
As an operator, I want seeded assets to remain fresh after TikTape is disabled.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The final report lists which seeded assets/timeframes are covered by native freshness configuration.
- [ ] The final report lists seeded assets/timeframes that require adapter configuration before TikTape is disabled.
- [ ] The bootstrap process does not silently assume native freshness for assets not configured in our adapter.

## 8. Functional requirements

- FR-1: Provide an operator CLI, tentatively `python -m app.cli.bootstrap_hyperliquid_history`.
- FR-2: CLI must support `--symbols`, `--all-tiktape-assets`, `--timeframes`, `--start`, `--end`, `--resume`, `--dry-run`, `--verify-only`, `--concurrency`, and `--report-path`.
- FR-3: CLI default timeframes must be `1m 5m 15m 1h 4h 1d`.
- FR-3a: CLI default concurrency must be `3`.
- FR-4: CLI default asset target should be all TikTape-supported Hyperliquid assets when discovery is available; if discovery is unavailable, it must fail with a clear message or require explicit `--symbols`.
- FR-5: Asset discovery must use a TikTape coverage endpoint if available; otherwise, it must support a repo-visible/provider-exported asset list as an operator input.
- FR-6: TikTape response rows must be normalized from `[timestamp_ms, open, high, low, close, volume]` into our internal candle representation.
- FR-7: Storage must use existing OHLCV upsert logic so repeated runs are idempotent.
- FR-8: Download pagination must use provider-supported `startTime`, `endTime`, and `limit` parameters.
- FR-9: Seed jobs must record per-symbol/timeframe progress and last successful timestamp in a local checkpoint artifact.
- FR-10: Verification must compare stored ranges against expected timeframe cadence and report gaps.
- FR-11: The existing Hyperliquid adapter must remain responsible for ongoing freshness after bootstrap.
- FR-12: Predict readiness must require no changes to consume seeded data because data lands in canonical storage.
- FR-13: Bootstrap output must include a freshness-coverage report comparing seeded symbols/timeframes against current native adapter configuration.
- FR-14: Full all-asset bootstrap must require a dry-run report before execution, including estimated symbol/timeframe count and storage-risk warning.
- FR-15: Full all-asset bootstrap must require explicit operator confirmation unless an intentional `--yes` flag is supplied.

## 9. Compatibility with current database

TikTape candles are compatible with our current internal OHLCV model after normalization:

| TikTape field | Internal field |
| --- | --- |
| `coin` request param | `symbol` |
| fixed source | `exchange = hyperliquid` |
| `interval` request param | `timeframe` |
| row `[0] timestamp_ms` | `timestamp` datetime |
| row `[1]` | `open` |
| row `[2]` | `high` |
| row `[3]` | `low` |
| row `[4]` | `close` |
| row `[5]` | `volume` |

The command should call the same bulk upsert path used by historical downloads so existing readers do not need special TikTape logic.

## 10. UX / operator experience

Example BTC smoke seed:

```bash
python -m app.cli.bootstrap_hyperliquid_history \
  --symbols BTC \
  --timeframes 15m 1h \
  --resume \
  --report-path backend/data/reports/hyperliquid-history-bootstrap-btc.json
```

Example full discovery dry run:

```bash
python -m app.cli.bootstrap_hyperliquid_history \
  --all-tiktape-assets \
  --timeframes 1m 5m 15m 1h 4h 1d \
  --dry-run
```

Example full seed:

```bash
python -m app.cli.bootstrap_hyperliquid_history \
  --all-tiktape-assets \
  --timeframes 1m 5m 15m 1h 4h 1d \
  --resume \
  --concurrency 3 \
  --report-path backend/data/reports/hyperliquid-history-bootstrap.json
```

Full all-asset seed should only run after reviewing the dry-run report. Automation may pass `--yes` only when the operator has intentionally accepted the estimated scope.

Example verification:

```bash
python -m app.cli.bootstrap_hyperliquid_history \
  --all-tiktape-assets \
  --timeframes 1m 5m 15m 1h 4h 1d \
  --verify-only \
  --report-path backend/data/reports/hyperliquid-history-bootstrap-verify.json
```

Operator output should include:

- total symbols/timeframes planned
- current symbol/timeframe
- downloaded candle count
- inserted/upserted candle count
- first/last timestamps
- retry status
- final readiness summary
- freshness-coverage summary

## 11. Non-functional requirements

- Performance: support long-running bootstrap without blocking API startup or normal app usage.
- Reliability: resume after process crash or network failure.
- Security: API keys only via environment variables; redact provider credentials from logs.
- Observability: structured logs per symbol/timeframe and final report artifact.
- Data quality: detect gaps, duplicate timestamps, malformed OHLC values, and non-monotonic data.
- Maintainability: keep TikTape behind a provider abstraction so it can be replaced later.
- Operational safety: default concurrency is `3`; full all-asset runs require a dry-run/storage estimate before execution.

## 12. Failure modes

- Missing API key: command exits with actionable setup message.
- Provider 401/403: command stops and reports credential failure without logging key.
- Provider DNS/network failure: command retries with backoff, then records symbol/timeframe failure.
- Provider rate limit: command backs off and continues.
- Provider discovery unavailable: command requires explicit asset list or a checked-in/exported coverage artifact.
- Partial provider coverage: command stores available rows and reports coverage gap.
- DB write failure: command stops current symbol/timeframe and preserves checkpoint before failure where possible.
- Interruption: rerun with `--resume` continues from checkpoint.
- Native adapter overlap: upsert prevents duplicate canonical candles.
- Seeded asset not configured for freshness: final report flags it before TikTape key is removed.

## 13. Rollout plan

### Phase 1: BTC smoke seed
- Symbols: `BTC`
- Timeframes: `15m`, `1h`
- Goal: prove provider request, normalization, DB upsert, checkpointing, and Predict readiness.

### Phase 2: Major assets seed
- Symbols: `BTC`, `ETH`, `SOL`
- Timeframes: all six target timeframes
- Goal: validate longer runtime, checkpointing, and gap reporting.

### Phase 3: All TikTape-supported Hyperliquid assets
- Symbols: all assets discovered from TikTape or provided by a coverage artifact
- Timeframes: all six target timeframes
- Prerequisite: dry-run/storage estimate reviewed and explicitly approved
- Goal: produce durable training-ready Hyperliquid dataset.

### Phase 4: Freshness handoff and stabilization
- Confirm native adapter freshness coverage for seeded assets.
- Update adapter configuration or produce explicit exceptions.
- Keep the TikTape key available for at least 30 days for explicit operator repair/backfill only.
- Disable TikTape only after the stabilization window and a passing freshness report.
- Document how to re-enable TikTape only for explicit future repair/backfill.

## 14. Test strategy

- Unit: TikTape row normalization into internal candle objects.
- Unit: pagination window calculation.
- Unit: checkpoint read/write and resume decisions.
- Unit: secret redaction in error messages.
- Unit: provider coverage parsing or explicit asset-list loading.
- Integration: seed a small mocked symbol/timeframe into test DB and verify upserted OHLCV rows.
- Integration: rerun same seed and verify idempotency.
- Integration: verification report detects missing ranges.
- Integration: freshness-coverage report identifies symbols absent from adapter config.
- Manual QA: run BTC `15m` and `1h` seed on preview and verify Predict readiness turns ready.

## 15. Success metrics

- BTC is Predict-ready for `15m` and `1h` after Phase 1.
- BTC, ETH, and SOL are Predict-ready for all six target timeframes after Phase 2 where sufficient provider history exists.
- All TikTape-supported target assets have populated `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `1h`, `4h`, and `1d` ranges after Phase 3, or are explicitly listed as unavailable/incomplete.
- Predict readiness uses seeded data without direct TikTape calls.
- Re-running the bootstrap command does not create duplicate candles.
- Final report clearly lists any unavailable, incomplete, or not-freshness-covered symbol/timeframe pairs.
- TikTape key can be kept temporarily for explicit repair/backfill and later disabled without breaking Predict readiness for seeded contexts.

## 16. Remaining implementation questions

1. Does TikTape expose a machine-readable coverage endpoint for all supported Hyperliquid assets?
2. If TikTape does not expose coverage discovery, what exported asset-list artifact should operators provide?
3. Can the existing native adapter keep all TikTape-supported assets fresh, or do we need explicit exceptions for long-tail assets?
4. What storage threshold should trigger a warning before full `1m` history is seeded across all assets?

## 17. CEO recommendation

Approve this as a separate data-infrastructure PRD. Do not expand the current Predict readiness PRD further. The current PRD should keep the on-demand backfill path; this follow-on PRD should create the durable historical dataset that removes normal runtime dependence on TikTape.

# Strategy Configuration Contract Program

**Status:** Approved program overview
**Updated:** 2026-04-23
**Folder:** `dev-plans/`

This folder groups the PRDs and planning documents for the strategy-configuration boundary between **Strategy Discovery** and **Model Training**.

The core product use case is broader than adversarial debate alone: any future **strategy** or **signal** created in Strategy Discovery should be portable into Model Training through one canonical configuration boundary.

## Program end state

This program is complete when:
- Strategy Discovery can export one canonical, versioned configuration package.
- Model Training can import that package without manual remapping or origin-specific file rules.
- The same package boundary supports both strategy-origin and signal-origin producers.
- Producer-specific evidence remains inspectable without changing the canonical import contract.
- Selective trait import is explicit, meaning Model Training can include only the traits or components it accepts and clearly show what was stripped.

## Locked product decisions

1. **Product/UI naming is institutional by default** on adversarial debate config and handoff surfaces.
2. **`GenomeSpec` remains allowed only in explicit backend/code examples or compatibility notes** where the technical artifact name matters.
3. **V1 optimizes for a practical boundary:**
   - shared configuration contract
   - adversarial debate as the first producer implementation
   - source-agnostic package rules for future producers
   - Strategy Discovery export/handoff
   - Model Training import
   - selective trait stripping/import, with clear visibility into included versus stripped traits or components
4. **Model Training → Strategy Discovery write-back matters, but comes after import works.**
5. **Backtest interoperability and cross-system learning are deferred until the contract boundary is stable.**
6. **The canonical package is versioned from day one, with explicit compatibility expectations and no silent import breakage across revisions.**

## Non-goals for this program

This program does not:
- redesign all product terminology across the platform
- merge Strategy Discovery and Model Training into one codebase or workflow
- solve backtest interoperability in v1
- require full bidirectional parity before export and import are stable

# PRD: Strategy Configuration Contract

**Status:** Approved parent PRD / scope guard
**Date:** 2026-04-23
**Type:** Program PRD
**Folder:** `dev-plans/`

## Overview

Evonome needs a stable, product-truthful configuration boundary between **Strategy Discovery** and **Model Training**.

Today only **adversarial debate** exposes a meaningful configuration output and handoff surface. That is the first producer we need to standardize, but it is not the end-state definition of the boundary.

The intended product use case is broader:
- any **strategy** created in Strategy Discovery should be portable into Model Training
- any **signal** created in Strategy Discovery should also be portable into Model Training for optimization, retraining, composition, or downstream use
- Model Training should consume one canonical package shape rather than origin-specific file conventions
- future Strategy Discovery producers should target the same boundary without inventing their own handoff model

Today that boundary is too loose. Strategy Discovery can generate promising outputs, but the handoff into Model Training is not formal enough to support reliable import, selective refinement, later write-back, or long-term expansion into more discovery methods.

This PRD is the parent artifact for a multi-PRD program that defines, validates, and hardens that boundary before broader feature expansion continues.

This parent PRD is an umbrella scope-and-sequencing artifact. It governs the program, but executable implementation detail lives in the child PRDs.

## Why this matters now

This is a platform boundary, not a cosmetic feature.

If the boundary remains vague:
- new discovery methods will emit inconsistent artifacts
- Model Training imports will be brittle or manual
- later write-back and lineage will be hard to trust
- new backtest paths and strategy types will multiply contract drift

If the boundary is standardized first:
- adversarial debate gets a trustworthy config section and handoff surface
- Model Training receives a stable import package
- later discovery methods can target the same contract
- future signal and strategy producers can plug into the same package model
- validation becomes repeatable instead of ad hoc

## Core product use case

At this moment the system only has a real config-output setup in adversarial debate. This program should treat that as **producer #1**, not as a permanent special case.

The target state is:
- every Strategy Discovery producer emits the same canonical importable boundary
- producer-specific evidence can exist, but it is secondary to the canonical package
- Model Training consumes the canonical package rather than adversarial-debate-specific files
- future signal and strategy creation methods can become portable without redefining the boundary

## Locked product decisions

### 1. Institutional naming is the default in product/UI config surfaces

The config section and handoff surfaces in adversarial debate must default to institutional naming.

Product/UI labels should use terms such as:
- `Configuration Handoff`
- `Strategy Configuration`
- `Version History`
- `Paper Trading`
- `Live Trading`
- `Knowledge Base`

Evolutionary labels like `Genesis`, `genome`, `organism`, `colony`, `Terrarium`, and `Ecosystem` should not appear in the visible config section unless a separate terminology-mode surface explicitly opts into that display language.

### 2. Technical/code examples may still use `GenomeSpec`

The PRD keeps `GenomeSpec` as an allowed technical term only where it is truly required:
- backend/code examples
- compatibility references
- migration notes

This is a compatibility concession, not a product-facing naming decision.

### 3. V1 is practical, not maximal

The first approved delivery slice should cover:
- the shared configuration contract
- adversarial debate as the first producer implementation
- source-agnostic package rules for future producers
- Strategy Discovery export/handoff
- Model Training import
- selective trait strip/include behavior

### 4. Reverse write-back is important but comes after import works

Model Training → Strategy Discovery write-back should remain in this program, but it should be sequenced after the import path is working and validated.

### 5. Backtest interoperability and cross-system learning are follow-on work

They matter strategically, but they should not block the first contract boundary from being defined and shipped safely.

## Program goals

- Define one stable strategy-configuration contract that both sections can understand.
- Make the adversarial debate config/handoff surface readable, explicit, and institutionally named.
- Treat adversarial debate as the first producer of a source-agnostic boundary, not the only producer.
- Allow Strategy Discovery to emit an import-ready configuration package.
- Allow Model Training to import that package with selective trait handling.
- Ensure the contract can cover both future **strategy-origin** and **signal-origin** producers without redesign.
- Preserve clean lineage for later write-back and version history.
- Build enough validation harness so future methods can target the same boundary safely.

## V1 scope

V1 covers:
- contract foundation and naming rules
- source-agnostic package rules for all future Strategy Discovery producers
- adversarial debate as the first implemented producer
- Strategy Discovery configuration export/handoff
- Model Training configuration import
- selective trait strip/include behavior
- readiness states and validation rules for importability

## Phase 2 scope

Phase 2 covers:
- Model Training → Strategy Discovery write-back
- version-history and lineage rules for returned traits/configuration
- non-destructive update flow and overwrite protection

## Deferred scope

Deferred until the boundary is stable:
- shared backtest adapter / evaluation interoperability
- cross-system Knowledge Base learning
- additional producer implementations beyond adversarial debate; the implementations are deferred, but the contract must remain source-agnostic from day one
- portfolio/deployment refinement beyond what is needed to validate the contract

## Child PRD map

Child labels describe the sequence under this parent PRD. File numbers describe the canonical review order in `dev-plans/`.

Mapping:
- 2A = file `03`
- 2B = file `04`
- 2C = file `05`
- 2D = file `06`
- 2E = file `07`
- 2F = file `08`
- 2G = file `09`

### 2A / File 03 — Foundation
Defines:
- product/UI naming rules
- canonical contract sections
- field ownership and source-of-truth mapping
- the minimum v1 schema boundary

### 2B / File 04 — Strategy Discovery export and handoff
Defines:
- adversarial debate config/handoff surfaces
- exportable configuration package shape
- import-readiness criteria
- blocked/missing-state handling

### 2C / File 05 — Model Training import
Defines:
- import flow into Model Training
- selective trait strip/include behavior
- provenance handling
- import validation and failure modes

### 2D / File 06 — Write-back and version history
Defines:
- write-back flow from Model Training into Strategy Discovery
- change preview and confirmation rules
- lineage/version-history behavior

### 2E / File 07 — Compatibility and validation
Defines:
- fixture strategy
- compatibility matrix
- naming regressions
- round-trip validation
- branch-level gates between PRDs

### 2F / File 08 — Backtest evaluation interoperability
Deferred follow-on for shared evaluation pathways.

### 2G / File 09 — Cross-system Knowledge Base learning
Deferred follow-on for discovery/memory learning across sections.

## Implementation gate

Approval of this parent PRD does not authorize engineering to build directly from `02` alone.

Rules:
- this parent PRD is an umbrella artifact, not an implementation slice
- implementation starts with `2A / File 03 — dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-contract-foundation.md`
- no implementation for `2B` or later starts until `2A` is reviewed, approved, and locally validated
- later child PRDs proceed in sequence with validation gates between slices

## Non-goals

This program does **not** aim to:
- merge Strategy Discovery and Model Training into one codebase
- replace the existing Model Training workflow model
- build every future discovery method now
- redesign all historical naming across the product at once
- require full bidirectional parity in the first slice

## Success criteria by phase

### V1 success
- Strategy Discovery can produce a stable configuration handoff package.
- The adversarial debate config section uses institutional naming by default.
- The package shape is explicitly documented as reusable for future signal and strategy producers.
- Supporting evidence remains inspectable but clearly secondary to the canonical import package.
- Model Training can import that package into an experiment.
- Selective trait strip/include behavior works cleanly.
- No existing Model Training flow is degraded.

### Phase 2 success
- Model Training can write enhanced configuration back into Strategy Discovery.
- Returned changes preserve clear lineage and version history.
- Write-back is non-destructive and operator-reviewed.

### Deferred/future success
- configuration packages can be evaluated through multiple backtest pathways with shared metrics truth
- discoveries and refinements can move through the Knowledge Base without contract drift

## Validation posture

This program is intended to be developed on one branch if desired, but only with strong internal checkpoints.

Rules:
- checkpoint commit after each PRD slice
- focused validation before moving to the next PRD
- branch-level validation record updated after each checkpoint
- no “we’ll fix it in the next PRD” carryover for unresolved contract bugs

See:
- `dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-contract-program-plan.md`
- `dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-contract-validation-plan.md`

## Approval condition for implementation handoff

Do not hand this full program into implementation as one undifferentiated task.

Approval of `02` means the umbrella scope is accepted. It does not authorize direct implementation from the parent PRD alone.

Implementation should begin with `2A / File 03 — dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-contract-foundation.md` and then follow the child PRDs in sequence, with validation gates between them.

This parent PRD is ready to function as the umbrella artifact once the child PRDs and supporting program-plan and validation docs are accepted as the working structure.

# PRD: Backtest Evaluation Interoperability

**Status:** Approved for first-slice implementation
**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Folder:** `dev-plans/`
**Parent:** `dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-contract.md`
**Dependencies:**
- `dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-contract-foundation.md`
- `dev-plans/prd-strategy-discovery-configuration-export-and-handoff.md`
- `dev-plans/prd-model-training-configuration-import.md`
- `dev-plans/prd-strategy-configuration-compatibility-and-validation.md`

## Problem

The merged 03–07 boundary lets Strategy Discovery export a canonical package and lets Model Training import and write back that package.

What is still missing is a trustworthy evaluation bridge.

Today, an imported experiment preserves the source package and provenance, but the operator does not have one productized way to:
- inspect whether the imported package can be evaluated again,
- rerun the source strategy through an approved evaluation adapter,
- compare rerun metrics against the source-version metrics,
- keep the metrics truth attached to the imported experiment.

That gap makes the contract usable for transfer and lineage, but still weak for evaluation interoperability.

## First-slice goal

Implement the first interoperable evaluation slice for **strategy-origin packages**:
- start from an imported Model Training experiment,
- resolve the source Discovery project and source version,
- run a controlled **shell backtest adapter** for that source version,
- normalize the rerun output into one canonical metrics truth,
- compare the rerun metrics to the stored source-version metrics,
- keep the evaluation record attached to the imported experiment.

This first slice is intentionally narrow.

It proves the shared evaluation contract without requiring immediate parity across every engine or immediate wiring into the generic `/api/v1/backtests` job system.

## Why this slice first

This is the smallest implementation that proves the important thing:
- the strategy-configuration contract can move from Discovery to Training and still drive a repeatable evaluation path with shared metrics truth.

It also matches the existing repo reality:
- Discovery versions already persist immutable `strategy.yaml`, `metrics.json`, and `config_snapshot.yaml` artifacts.
- Discovery evolution already supports a shell-based backtest runner driven by strategy artifacts plus environment variables.
- Training experiments already preserve `source_project`, `source_version`, package kind, market context, and import decisions.

## Product goals

- Give imported experiments an explicit `Backtest Evaluation` action.
- Keep the first slice restricted to `strategy` packages.
- Treat shell evaluation as a first-class adapter mode, not an ad hoc hidden script.
- Normalize rerun metrics into the same canonical metric family used by Discovery versioning.
- Surface source-versus-rerun deltas clearly.
- Persist evaluation history on the imported experiment.

## In scope for the first slice

- evaluation preview for imported experiments
- strategy-package gating
- source project / source version resolution
- shell backtest adapter selection
- rerun execution using source-version strategy artifacts plus version config snapshot
- normalized metric record
- source-versus-rerun delta record
- Training-side modal entry point and review surface
- repo-visible tests for preview, blocked states, and successful evaluation persistence

## Out of scope for the first slice

- signal-package evaluation
- generic `/api/v1/backtests` job creation from imported experiments
- long-running queued evaluation jobs
- reworking every Discovery backtest command
- full browser dashboards for evaluation history
- Monte Carlo, WFO, or paper-trading follow-ons
- PRD 09 cross-system knowledge-base work

## Adapter policy

### Supported now
- `strategy` packages with a resolvable `source_project` and `source_version`
- a Discovery version artifact containing strategy state and metrics
- a resolvable shell backtest command from version config snapshot or project config

### Blocked now
- `signal` packages
- missing source version
- missing source project
- missing Discovery version artifact
- missing shell backtest command
- missing or invalid market context

Blocked packages must remain inspectable.

## User stories

### US-001: Preview whether an imported experiment can be evaluated
As an operator, I want to preview evaluation readiness for an imported experiment so I know whether the source package can be rerun safely.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The system exposes an evaluation preview endpoint for imported experiments.
- [ ] The preview shows source project, source version, package kind, market context, and adapter mode.
- [ ] The preview returns `ready` or `blocked` with structured reasons.
- [ ] Blocked states remain inspectable.

### US-002: Run a shell backtest adapter for the imported source version
As an operator, I want to rerun the imported source strategy through a controlled shell adapter so I can verify evaluation interoperability.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The system can load the source Discovery version artifact.
- [ ] The system can resolve backtest command, timeout, and working directory.
- [ ] The system writes a runtime strategy artifact for the rerun.
- [ ] The system executes the shell adapter and parses either JSON results or stdout metrics.

### US-003: Preserve one metrics truth
As a product owner, I want rerun metrics normalized into the same canonical metric family so different evaluation paths can still be compared honestly.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Rerun output is normalized into canonical metrics.
- [ ] Source-version metrics are loaded from immutable version artifacts.
- [ ] The evaluation record stores source metrics, rerun metrics, and deltas.
- [ ] The record is attached to the imported experiment.

### US-004: Training operators can access the evaluation flow without leaving the experiment menu
As a Training operator, I want to launch evaluation from the experiment menu so the Discovery → Training contract remains visible and actionable.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Imported experiments expose a `Backtest Evaluation` action in the workflow experiment selector.
- [ ] The modal shows preview readiness before execution.
- [ ] The modal shows normalized rerun metrics after success.
- [ ] Blocked packages cannot run but still explain why.

## Functional requirements

- FR-1: The platform must provide an evaluation preview for imported experiments.
- FR-2: The preview must require an imported experiment with `configuration_import` metadata.
- FR-3: The first slice must support `strategy` packages only.
- FR-4: Unsupported package kinds must fail with explicit structured reasons.
- FR-5: The preview must resolve `source_project`, `source_version`, and market context from the import record.
- FR-6: The preview must resolve the source Discovery version artifact from immutable version storage.
- FR-7: The first adapter mode must be `shell_backtest`.
- FR-8: The adapter must derive command, timeout, and working directory from source-version config snapshot or project config.
- FR-9: Evaluation execution must materialize a runtime strategy artifact for the rerun.
- FR-10: Evaluation execution must parse either JSON results or stdout metrics.
- FR-11: Rerun output must be normalized into the canonical Discovery metric family.
- FR-12: The evaluation record must preserve source metrics, rerun metrics, and metric deltas.
- FR-13: The evaluation record must be persisted in repo-visible experiment workspace storage.
- FR-14: The latest evaluation summary must be attached to the imported experiment.
- FR-15: The Training workflow experiment selector must expose a `Backtest Evaluation` action for imported experiments.
- FR-16: The evaluation modal must show preview readiness, blocked reasons, and rerun results.
- FR-17: The first slice must not require generic `/api/v1/backtests` job wiring.

## Quality gates

- a ready imported `strategy` package can produce an evaluation preview
- a ready imported `strategy` package can persist a completed evaluation record
- a blocked or unsupported package remains inspectable and does not run
- source-version metrics and rerun metrics are both visible in the persisted record
- Training UI exposes the action only where it is relevant
- focused backend and frontend tests cover preview, run, and blocked-state behavior

## Implementation notes

- Use the existing Discovery version store as the source of immutable strategy and metrics artifacts.
- Reuse the existing shell-runner conventions already used by Discovery evolution:
  - `AUTORESEARCH_PROJECT_DIR`
  - `AUTORESEARCH_STRATEGY_PATH`
  - `AUTORESEARCH_RESULTS_PATH`
  - `AUTORESEARCH_BASELINE_VERSION`
- Normalize rerun metrics into the canonical metric family before comparing them to source-version metrics.
- Keep the first slice simple: synchronous execution plus persisted record is acceptable.

## Non-goals after approval

Approval of this PRD authorizes only the first slice above.

It does not authorize:
- signal-package evaluation
- generic queued evaluation orchestration
- API backtest job unification
- Monte Carlo follow-ons
- PRD 09 work

- implementation_gate: released by human and completed; final verifier bug-check passed 2026-05-31

## 1. Problem

Training now has stable source-truth seams for Discovery-origin strategy/configuration packages, Training imports, Training evaluations, Training write-backs, artifact lineage summaries, and chart overlay availability. Operators still need a way to inspect lifecycle evidence across these seams without manually reconstructing what happened to a package after Discovery export.

The risk is overreach: Discovery also has signal, pattern, debate, and future method artifacts that are not yet stable first-class Training source contracts. If the Knowledge Evidence Ledger indexes or promotes those unstable artifacts as if they were authoritative, it can harden wrong assumptions and treat raw memory or unsupported records as validated knowledge.

## 2. First-slice goal

Build a **read-only Knowledge Evidence Ledger for stable strategy/configuration lifecycle evidence only**.

The first slice must let operators search and inspect source-owned lifecycle records for canonical Discovery strategy/configuration packages and Training-owned import/evaluation/write-back evidence. It must preserve provenance, distinguish indexed summaries from source-owned truth, and fail closed for missing, stale, conflicting, or unsupported records.

The first slice must not implement broad Discovery artifact ingestion, recommendation automation, memory injection, form prefill, or source-record mutation.

## 3. Strategic principle

The ledger indexes evidence; it does not become the evidence source of truth.

The source-truth flow remains:

```text
Discovery artifacts -> Training import/evaluation/context -> accepted Training outputs -> Knowledge/Trading consumers
```

The ledger may summarize and link to records in that flow, but it must not replace Discovery, Training, or evaluation records as authoritative.

## 4. Completed baselines this PRD may consume

| Baseline | Accepted source contract |
|---|---|
| #814 Training Experiment Intake, Context Selector, and Discovery Import Flow | Training-owned experiments, active context, and generic **Import from Discovery** vocabulary. Discovery-origin metadata exists for imported configuration packages without narrowing copy to one method. |
| #780 Training Artifact and Lineage Readiness | Backend-owned artifact/lineage summaries with complete, partial, missing, unsupported, stale, and conflicting states. Trading-facing display fields are read-only and provider-neutral. |
| #781 Training Chart Overlay API and Chart Integration | Read-only Training overlay availability and provenance from evaluation records. Signals/trades/windows are used only when source records provide complete evidence; missing or unsupported overlays remain explicit. |
| #840 Training and Discovery Integration Readiness | Source-truth map, fixture inventory, and revise-first recommendation for this PRD. Signal packages fail closed, pattern artifacts lack a direct Training contract, and direct debate-memory ingestion remains future scope. |

## 5. Provider-neutrality requirements

This work must remain provider-neutral.

- Provider, market, symbol, asset class, session model, timeframe, or data source values are source metadata, not product boundaries.
- Ledger filters may expose source metadata, but shared code must not hardcode Hyperliquid, Binance, crypto perpetuals, forex, equities, or any one provider as the ledger boundary.
- Unsupported provider capabilities, missing market context, incompatible source metadata, missing provenance, and unsupported artifact kinds must fail closed with explicit unavailable, blocked, stale, or conflicting states.
- Provider-specific behavior belongs in existing provider/datafeed capabilities, source records, fixtures, or validation profiles, not in ledger-specific assumptions.

## 6. Authoritative source records for first slice

| Evidence type | Source of truth | First-slice treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery export evidence | Canonical strategy/configuration package export and provenance | Index source locator and summary fields; do not mutate package records. |
| Training import evidence | Training configuration import record and import decision record | Index import status, preserved/stripped/deferred/unsupported context, and source locator. |
| Training experiment context | Training experiment record | Index experiment id/name/context as Training-owned display context. |
| Training evaluation evidence | Training configuration evaluation record | Index evaluation status, metrics summary, market context, adapter mode, and source locator. |
| Training write-back evidence | Training write-back preview/apply record and returned version reference | Index write-back status, changed sections, conflicts, returned version id/name, and source locator. |
| Artifact lineage evidence | #780 backend-owned derived summary | Use as derived status/diagnostic view only; source records remain authoritative. |
| Chart overlay evidence | #781 backend-owned derived availability/overlay summary | Use as derived availability/provenance view only; do not infer missing timestamps, prices, signals, or trades. |

## 7. Explicitly unavailable or future-scoped sources

These sources must not be treated as first-class ledger inputs in the first slice:

- Signal packages that currently fail closed at Training import with `unsupported_package_kind:signal`.
- Pattern artifacts without a stable Discovery-to-Training contract.
- Direct debate transcripts, raw critic feedback, debate memory sidecars, or lesson-card injection.
- Future Discovery method families without stable IDs, provenance, lifecycle state, market context, and provider-neutral contracts.
- Paper/live Trading feedback, Portfolio evidence, Analyze evidence, or broad memory records unless a later approved PRD adds those source contracts.

If any of these records are encountered, the first slice must return unavailable or unsupported states instead of inventing source truth.

## 8. In scope for first slice

- Read-only ledger record classification for stable strategy/configuration lifecycle evidence.
- Source locators back to authoritative Discovery and Training records.
- Search and filtering by supported source-owned fields:
  - source project,
  - source version,
  - package kind,
  - market context,
  - record type,
  - import/evaluation/write-back/lineage/overlay status,
  - stale/missing/conflicting/unsupported state.
- Operator-visible record list and detail view for stable lifecycle records.
- Clear distinction between source-owned fields and indexed summary fields.
- Explicit unavailable, blocked, stale, unsupported, and conflicting states.
- Stable configuration signature fields only when existing source records already provide them.
- Tests for provenance, filtering, record classification, source locator handling, unsupported states, and no-auto-apply guardrails.

## 9. Out of scope for first slice

- Implementing signal, pattern, direct debate transcript, debate memory, or future method ingestion as first-class ledger sources.
- Auto-promoting knowledge.
- Manual promotion flows unless a later approved revision explicitly scopes promotion guardrails.
- Search or recommendation over raw chat memory.
- Memory injection into Discovery or Training prompts.
- Similarity-driven recommendations that change or prefill forms.
- Auto-applying changes to Discovery packages, Training experiments, write-backs, or evaluations.
- Replacing the strategy/configuration package contract, import records, evaluation records, lineage summaries, or overlay summaries.
- Paper/live retraining loops, live trading, Portfolio integration, or Analyze integration.

## 10. Automation boundary

| Capability | First-slice decision |
|---|---|
| Read-only lifecycle evidence ledger | In scope |
| Source locator and provenance inspection | In scope |
| Search and filters over stable lifecycle evidence | In scope |
| Missing/stale/conflicting/unsupported state handling | In scope |
| Manual knowledge promotion | Future slice or separate approved revision |
| Similar prior record detection | Future slice unless based only on existing stable signatures and review-only copy |
| Human-reviewed recommendation drafts | Future slice |
| Memory injection | Out of scope |
| Form prefill from recommendations | Out of scope |
| Auto-applied configuration changes | Out of scope |

Any recommendation shown in a later slice must be review-only unless a separate PRD explicitly changes this policy.

## 11. User stories

### US-001: Search stable lifecycle evidence

As an operator, I want to search strategy/configuration lifecycle evidence across Discovery and Training so I can understand what happened to a package without manually reconstructing lineage.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] The ledger lists supported export, import, evaluation, write-back, lineage, and overlay availability records.
- [ ] The operator can filter by source project, source version, package kind, market context, record type, and status.
- [ ] Search results show record type, timestamp, status, source system, and concise summary.
- [ ] Empty states explain whether no records exist or source records are unavailable.

### US-002: Inspect provenance without replacing source truth

As an operator, I want each ledger record to link back to its authoritative source evidence so I can trust what the ledger is showing.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Each ledger record includes a source record locator.
- [ ] The detail view shows authoritative source type, source timestamp when available, and source-owned fields.
- [ ] Indexed summary fields are visually or structurally distinct from source-owned fields.
- [ ] Missing or moved source records produce stale-or-missing-source states.

### US-003: Fail closed for unsupported Discovery artifacts

As a product owner, I want unsupported signal, pattern, debate-memory, and future method artifacts to be unavailable rather than silently normalized.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Signal package evidence that is not part of the stable strategy/configuration lifecycle appears as unsupported or unavailable.
- [ ] Pattern artifacts without a stable source contract appear as unavailable or future-scoped.
- [ ] Raw debate transcripts and debate memory are not promoted or injected as validated knowledge.
- [ ] Unsupported records cannot appear as ready or promoted.

### US-004: Preserve generic Discovery-origin language

As an operator, I want ledger copy to describe Discovery-origin evidence generically so future Discovery methods can connect after stable contracts exist.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Primary copy uses Discovery-origin or Import from Discovery language where relevant.
- [ ] Method-specific labels appear only as source metadata, filters, or compatibility aliases.
- [ ] No route, enum, or UI label narrows the ledger to one Discovery method or provider.

### US-005: Prevent automated action

As a lead operator, I want the ledger to support inspection without changing source records so the first slice builds trust before leverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] No first-slice path mutates Discovery packages, Training imports, evaluations, write-backs, lineage summaries, or overlay summaries.
- [ ] No first-slice path auto-applies, pre-fills, or recommends configuration changes as an action.
- [ ] Similarity or signature fields, if present, are informational only.

## 12. Functional requirements

- FR-1: Expose a read-only ledger for stable strategy/configuration lifecycle evidence only.
- FR-2: Preserve source locators to authoritative Discovery and Training records.
- FR-3: Distinguish source-owned fields from indexed summary fields.
- FR-4: Support filters for project, version, package kind, market context, record type, and status where source records provide those fields.
- FR-5: Consume #780 lineage summaries and #781 overlay availability only as derived views, not source truth replacements.
- FR-6: Mark missing provenance, missing lifecycle state, missing market context, stale source records, conflicts, unsupported provider capabilities, and unsupported artifact kinds explicitly.
- FR-7: Treat signal packages, pattern artifacts, direct debate transcripts, debate memory, and future Discovery methods as unavailable or future-scoped unless a later approved contract supports them.
- FR-8: Keep first-slice operations read-only and non-mutating.
- FR-9: Do not auto-promote, auto-apply, inject memory, or prefill forms.
- FR-10: Preserve provider-neutral behavior and generic Discovery-origin terminology.

## 13. UX / UI notes

The first slice should expose a concise operator review surface with:

- search and filters,
- record list grouped or filterable by evidence type,
- record detail view,
- provenance/source locator section,
- source-owned versus indexed-summary distinction,
- unavailable/blocked/stale/conflicting state messaging.

Primary copy should stay user-facing and concise. Place diagnostics and source details behind details panels, tooltips, or secondary surfaces.

## 14. Technical approach

High-level only:

- Reuse existing source records and service contracts before adding new storage.
- Prefer one canonical ledger record classification model over per-surface ad hoc mapping.
- Index or query source-owned lifecycle records without duplicating their truth.
- Keep evaluation outcome fields tied to Training evaluation records.
- Keep lineage and overlay availability tied to their backend-derived summaries.
- Use stable configuration signatures only when already present in source records.
- Return explicit unavailable/unsupported/stale/conflicting states for unsupported sources.

The implementation may choose materialized, dynamic, or hybrid retrieval, but the product requirement is provenance-preserving read-only inspection, not a specific storage design.

## 15. Non-functional requirements

- Performance: Search/filtering should be responsive for normal operator review volumes; large-scale indexing can be optimized later.
- Security: Respect existing access rules for source records; do not expose records across unauthorized boundaries.
- Accessibility: Ledger, filters, detail panels, and unavailable states must be keyboard-accessible and screen-reader compatible.
- Observability: Log source-record lookup failures and stale-source states.
- Auditability: Source locators must be durable enough to explain which record produced each ledger row.
- KISS: Keep the first slice small; do not build a broad memory or recommendation platform in this PRD.

## 16. Failure modes

- Source record missing: show stale-or-missing-source state.
- Provenance missing: block ready state and show missing provenance.
- Market context missing: block ready state and show missing market context.
- Unsupported artifact kind: show unsupported or unavailable, not ready.
- Source record changed or moved: preserve original locator and show resolution failure.
- Conflicting source metadata: show conflict and block ready/promoted state.
- Evaluation record missing: show evaluation unavailable or pending; do not infer outcome.
- Overlay source incomplete: show partial/unavailable overlay availability; do not infer markers.
- Knowledge Base unavailable: source records remain authoritative and workflows continue without ledger enrichment.

## 17. Rollout

- Feature flag: recommended for the first operator-visible ledger surface.
- First rollout: internal/read-only ledger for stable strategy/configuration lifecycle records.
- Later rollouts require separate approval for promotion, similarity, recommendation drafts, debate memory, paper/live evidence, or broader Knowledge consumers.
- Rollback plan: disable the ledger surface; source records remain intact.

## 18. Test strategy

- Unit:
  - record classification,
  - filter parsing,
  - source locator handling,
  - source-owned versus indexed-summary field handling,
  - unsupported/stale/conflicting state mapping,
  - no-auto-apply guardrails.
- Integration:
  - export/import/write-back/evaluation source records appear in ledger results,
  - missing source records produce unavailable/stale states,
  - unsupported signal/pattern/debate/future method records do not appear ready,
  - lineage and overlay derived summaries do not replace source records.
- Frontend:
  - search/filter UI,
  - detail view provenance display,
  - unavailable/blocked/stale/conflicting rendering,
  - source-owned versus indexed-summary copy.
- Regression:
  - existing strategy/configuration export, import, evaluation, write-back, lineage, and overlay flows remain unchanged.

## 19. Verifier checkpoints before implementation

1. **Source-locator and record-classification contract**
   - Freeze supported evidence types, source locators, source-owned fields, indexed-summary fields, and unavailable states before UI work.
2. **Read-only query/index path**
   - Verify stable lifecycle records can be listed/searched without mutating source records or inventing missing truth.
3. **Unsupported/missing/stale/conflicting state handling**
   - Verify unsupported signal/pattern/debate/future method evidence and missing metadata fail closed.
4. **Operator review surface**
   - Verify generic Discovery-origin copy, source locator details, accessibility, and no method/provider narrowing.
5. **No-automation guardrail**
   - Verify no auto-promotion, auto-apply, memory injection, recommendation action, or form prefill exists.
6. **Final verifier bug-check**
   - Run final bug-check after implementation is complete.

## 20. Implementation handoff criteria

Before #578 moves from approved-gated to implementation handoff, confirm:

- [ ] Human explicitly releases #578 for implementation after this revision.
- [ ] The first slice remains read-only and strategy/configuration lifecycle scoped.
- [ ] #814, #780, #781, and #840 are treated as source-contract baselines.
- [ ] Signal packages, pattern artifacts, direct debate transcripts, debate memory, and future methods are unavailable or future-scoped.
- [ ] No auto-apply, auto-promotion, memory injection, recommendation action, or form-prefill behavior is included.
- [ ] Verifier checkpoints above are accepted before coding.

## 21. Future slice: manual promotion with approval metadata

Manual promotion may return in a later approved slice after the read-only ledger is stable.

Future promotion requirements must include:

- promotion requires a supported source ledger record or source locator,
- promotion records include approver, approval note, promoted kind, source evidence, and timestamp,
- promoted knowledge is visually distinct from raw lifecycle evidence,
- promotion does not mutate source records,
- unsupported or stale source records cannot be promoted without explicit resolution.

## 22. Future slice: debate memory evidence and critic lesson cards

This slice is explicitly deferred until the read-only ledger is stable and a later PRD approves debate-memory behavior. It extends lifecycle evidence into provenance-backed debate learning without treating raw chat memory as validated knowledge.

### Goal

Let future Discovery jobs reuse validated lessons from prior strategist/critic conversations so repeated misconfigurations are easier to avoid without losing human control.

### Source evidence

- raw debate turns,
- critic feedback inside saved debate transcripts,
- Phase 1 debug findings and validator artifacts,
- handoff outcomes, blocked states, and human decisions,
- fixed-pattern evidence from source changes and passing tests when available.

Raw transcript content is source evidence only. It must not be promoted or injected as validated guidance unless a future lesson-card contract preserves provenance and clearly states evidence status.

### Future-slice capabilities

- Store raw debate transcripts and critic feedback as searchable evidence with source artifact locators.
- Extract compact debate lesson cards from validated blocker/fix evidence.
- Distinguish `raw_critic_feedback`, `validated_blocker`, `fixed_pattern`, and `decision_required` lesson states.
- Allow manual promotion of supported debate lessons into shared knowledge with approval metadata.
- Inject only bounded, relevant lessons into future prompts as a sidecar.
- Record retrieval traces showing which lessons were injected and why.

### Boundaries

- Do not inject full historical transcripts into prompts by default.
- Do not treat critic opinion as proof without validator, debug, outcome, or human-review evidence.
- Do not auto-change seeds, contracts, packages, imports, evaluations, or Training records from debate memory.
- Do not let debate memory override selected market profile, seed thesis, candidate approval, or gate verdict.
- Keep recommendations review-only unless a later approved PRD changes the automation boundary.

## 23. Future work

- Manual promotion with approval metadata.
- Similarity and repetition detection after stable signatures are available.
- Human-reviewed recommendation drafts.
- Debate Memory Evidence and Critic Lesson Cards after the read-only ledger is stable.
- Signal and pattern evidence ingestion after stable Discovery contracts exist.
- Paper Trading and Live Trading evidence ingestion.
- Portfolio-level knowledge channels.
- Analyze integration for cross-surface inspection.
- Controlled form prefill after a separate approval gate.
