# PRD: Pattern Discovery Native Method

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Assigned agent/worktree: Evonome-discovery (`/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery`).
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Parent PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593
> Foundation PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/602
> Signal precedent: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/608 / https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/609
> Historical repo snapshot: [`tasks/prd/_archive/github-only-migration-2026-05-06/dev-plans/prd-pattern-discovery-native-method.md`](https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/blob/bab4b4b27c563af4601f6bd83b67bfdf712a02a7/tasks/prd/_archive/github-only-migration-2026-05-06/dev-plans/prd-pattern-discovery-native-method.md)
> Migration note: repo-local PRD files are historical only; update this issue body instead of maintaining a separate PRD copy.

---

---
title: Pattern Discovery Native Method
slug: pattern-discovery-native-method
created: 2026-05-06
status: approved
prd_review_status: approved
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-06
github_issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/611
originating_worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
parent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593
foundation_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/602
signal_precedent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/608
signal_precedent_pr: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/609
source_reference: tasks/prd/_archive/github-only-migration-2026-05-06/dev-plans/prd-pattern-discovery-native-method.md
---

## 1. Problem

Discovery Method Foundation established the shared method registry, shell contracts, create-modal seam, node/detail/modal contracts, compatibility aliases, and basic handoff vocabulary. The Signal Discovery slice then proved those seams with a first native non-Debate method.

Pattern Discovery is the next method in the Discovery Method Porting plan, but it still needs a method-owned implementation slice. Without a native Pattern slice, pattern work can remain either a placeholder surface or a Training-era flow with unclear ownership, incomplete evidence states, and handoff copy that may overstate readiness.

The primary risk is false confidence: recurrence evidence, mined structures, or candidate previews may look useful while not yet being a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package. Pattern Discovery must therefore expose pattern-specific creation and evidence review while keeping readiness truthful.

## 2. Product goal

Make Pattern Discovery a first-class Discovery method with a dedicated create flow, normalized method state, pattern-specific run nodes, evidence/result review, candidate/provenance visibility, and truthful handoff readiness.

The first implementation slice should prove Pattern can reuse the Signal-validated method seams without copying Signal-specific assumptions. It must preserve legacy Training-side Pattern access and must not implement System Builder or cross-method handoff normalization.

## 3. Locked context and dependencies

- Parent umbrella PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593.
- Discovery Method Foundation is complete: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/602.
- Signal Discovery native method precedent is merged: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/609.
- Pattern Discovery should follow Signal before Cross-Method Handoff Consistency.
- System Builder remains follow-on unless explicitly reprioritized.
- Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package remains the Discovery-to-Training boundary.
- Backend behavior changes are forbidden unless explicitly justified as a minimal non-breaking adapter for Pattern artifacts.

## 4. In scope

- Pattern Discovery create flow with pattern-specific intent and bounded inputs.
- Pattern-specific method state normalization for linked runs, evidence availability, candidate patterns, reasoning, and readiness.
- Pattern-specific nodes, detail panel, and phase/modal content using the Discovery method contract.
- Pattern evidence review: recurrence, market scope, metrics, source references, and candidate relevance where available.
- Candidate/provenance display for mined or selected patterns where existing artifacts support it.
- Truthful handoff readiness: `ready` only with a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package; otherwise `unavailable`, `blocked`, `incomplete`, or `decision_required`.
- Compatibility isolation for legacy Training-side Pattern flows and aliases.
- Regression protection for Debate and Signal surfaces touched by shared helpers.
- Concise implementation handoff documenting reusable Pattern seams versus Pattern-only logic.

## 5. Out of scope

- System Builder native implementation.
- Full cross-method handoff normalization across Debate, Signal, Pattern, and Builder.
- Training import, evaluation, optimization, refinement, or writeback behavior changes.
- Strategy Configuration schema changes.
- Backend migrations or broad API rewrites.
- Deleting, hiding, or renaming legacy Training-side Pattern flows.
- Route deletion or physical folder renames.
- Claiming Pattern Discovery is import-ready from pattern previews alone.
- Broad shared modal redesign unrelated to Pattern.

## 6. User stories

### US-001: Pattern-specific create entry

**Description:** As a Discovery user, I want Pattern Discovery to have a dedicated create flow so that I can start pattern work without Signal- or Debate-shaped assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Pattern Discovery create entry is reachable from the existing Discovery method shell/route.
- [ ] Create flow uses Pattern-specific intent copy and inputs.
- [ ] Inputs capture market scope, timeframe, exchange, pattern search focus, recurrence/evidence constraints, and bounded run controls where supported.
- [ ] Defaults are safe and bounded; no create path starts an unbounded job.
- [ ] Validation prevents missing market scope, empty Pattern intent, or invalid numeric bounds.
- [ ] Submitted jobs preserve method identity as `discovery_patterns` or the existing canonical Pattern method id.
- [ ] Legacy Training-side Pattern entry points remain reachable.

### US-002: Pattern run lifecycle and method state

**Description:** As a Discovery user, I want Pattern runs to show lifecycle and linked execution state clearly so that I understand whether evidence is pending, running, blocked, failed, or ready for review.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Pattern method state has one normalized read path for linked execution id, execution status, evidence count, candidate count, reasoning count, and readiness state.
- [ ] Pattern lifecycle UI distinguishes no linked run, pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled, blocked, and stale states.
- [ ] Refresh behavior updates linked Pattern artifacts without changing unrelated method state.
- [ ] Failed or missing linked-run loads show concise retry/refresh guidance.
- [ ] Discovery shell/search/filter behavior continues to work for Pattern runs.
- [ ] Lifecycle copy avoids Training-only terminology.

### US-003: Pattern evidence and recurrence review

**Description:** As an operator, I want to inspect pattern evidence and recurrence metrics so that I can decide whether a discovered structure is worth keeping.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Pattern evidence phase shows available pattern name/label, recurrence summary, market scope, quality score or relevant metric, and source artifact references where available.
- [ ] Empty states distinguish not started, still running, no patterns found, and artifact load failure.
- [ ] Pattern detail preserves provenance: source run id, market scope, generation timestamp when available, and source artifact references.
- [ ] Unsupported evidence sections are hidden or marked unavailable rather than faked.
- [ ] Pattern evidence uses Pattern-specific labels and avoids Signal/Debate phase terminology.
- [ ] Candidate preview artifacts do not set handoff status to `ready` by themselves.

### US-004: Candidate pattern review and provenance

**Description:** As a Discovery user, I want Pattern candidates and provenance to be visible so that downstream work can reference intentional Pattern outputs.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Candidate pattern list is deterministic where sorting logic is touched.
- [ ] Candidate details include recurrence/evidence metrics and source context where available.
- [ ] Selected or promoted Pattern outputs are marked without implying Training import readiness.
- [ ] Already-selected candidates are not duplicated in local Pattern state.
- [ ] Promotion/selection errors are recoverable and do not corrupt method state.
- [ ] Tests cover at least one candidate-present state and one missing-artifact state.

### US-005: Truthful Pattern handoff readiness

**Description:** As an operator, I want Pattern handoff readiness to be truthful so that I do not mistake pattern previews for import-ready Strategy Configuration packages.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Pattern handoff card/rendering path consumes the method handoff capability/readiness contract.
- [ ] `ready` appears only when a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package exists and passes readiness checks.
- [ ] Pattern candidates, evidence summaries, or preview payloads without a valid package render as `unavailable`, `blocked`, `incomplete`, or `decision_required`.
- [ ] Handoff copy explains what is missing and the next action without promising Training import.
- [ ] No Training import behavior changes are included.
- [ ] Tests cover truthy preview artifacts that must not render `ready`.

### US-006: Preserve Debate, Signal, and legacy access

**Description:** As a transition owner, I want existing Debate, Signal, and legacy Pattern flows to keep working while Pattern Discovery becomes native.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Existing Debate route, create entry, node/detail behavior, and artifact visibility still pass targeted regression tests where touched.
- [ ] Signal Discovery create/lifecycle/handoff regression tests still pass where shared helpers are touched.
- [ ] Historical Discovery aliases remain reachable.
- [ ] Legacy Training-side Pattern flows remain reachable.
- [ ] No route is deleted or renamed.
- [ ] No backend endpoint contract used by Training is changed.

### US-007: Documentation and implementation handoff

**Description:** As a future implementer, I want the Pattern seam documented so that Cross-Method Handoff Consistency can build on real Debate, Signal, and Pattern behavior.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Document Pattern-specific method state, artifact adapter expectations, and handoff readiness semantics in a concise repo-visible note or implementation handoff.
- [ ] Identify reusable helpers shared with Signal and Pattern-only logic.
- [ ] Record validation evidence and verifier checkpoints in the task artifact folder.
- [ ] Include follow-ons for Cross-Method Handoff Consistency and any backend adapter gaps discovered during implementation.

## 7. Functional requirements

- **FR-1:** Discovery must expose Pattern Discovery through the existing method registry and shell contract.
- **FR-2:** Pattern create must use Pattern-specific, validated, bounded inputs.
- **FR-3:** Pattern run lifecycle state must be normalized before it reaches nodes, details, or modal phases.
- **FR-4:** Pattern nodes must use Pattern-specific labels, statuses, metrics, and phase summaries.
- **FR-5:** Pattern detail/modal content must show evidence, recurrence, candidates/provenance, and handoff state where applicable.
- **FR-6:** Pattern preview artifacts must not produce `ready` handoff status.
- **FR-7:** Pattern handoff `ready` must require a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package.
- **FR-8:** Legacy Training-side Pattern flows must remain available during and after this slice.
- **FR-9:** Debate and Signal behavior must remain regression-protected where shared surfaces are touched.
- **FR-10:** Backend changes must be avoided unless a minimal non-breaking adapter is explicitly required and covered by tests.

## 8. Quality gates

Expected implementation gates:

- `pnpm --dir frontend typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir frontend check:discovery-terms`
- Targeted Vitest for Pattern Discovery create flow and validation.
- Targeted Vitest for Pattern nodes/detail/modal phases.
- Targeted Vitest for Pattern handoff readiness false-ready prevention.
- Targeted Vitest for registry/shell contracts touched by Pattern.
- Targeted compatibility test proving legacy Training-side Pattern entries remain reachable.
- Targeted Signal/Debate regression tests if shared helpers are touched.
- Backend tests only if a minimal backend-facing adapter is touched.
- `git diff --check`

Recommended pre-PR gates:

- Local quality gate if available: `/gate --ml`
- Verifier final bug-check after all scoped implementation is complete.

## 9. Verifier checkpoints

Implementation should use coder/verifier checkpoints before continuing across phases.

| Checkpoint | Scope | Required verifier focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pattern create flow and method state normalization | Method identity, bounded inputs, no Signal/Debate assumptions, legacy access preserved |
| 2 | Pattern nodes/detail/modal evidence phases | Evidence accuracy, lifecycle states, missing-artifact blockers, shared surface regressions |
| 3 | Candidate/provenance and handoff readiness | No false-ready handoff state, provenance display, no Training import changes |
| 4 | Documentation, compatibility, and final validation | Quality gates, legacy Pattern access, final bug-check, no scope creep |

A final verifier bug-check is required by default after implementation completion.

## 10. Implementation boundaries

Expected allowed paths:

- `frontend/src/discovery/**`
- `frontend/src/features/training-lab/workflows/**` only for compatibility metadata or tests
- `frontend/src/experimental/workflows/**` only for compatibility metadata or tests
- focused test files under the same frontend scopes
- implementation artifact folder under `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/<session>/`

Forbidden without separate approval:

- backend migrations
- Training import/evaluation/writeback behavior
- Strategy Configuration schema changes
- Signal, Debate, System Builder, or cross-method handoff implementation beyond targeted regressions
- route deletion or physical folder renames
- broad shared modal redesign
- deploy/config/secrets changes

## 11. Success metrics

- Pattern Discovery can be created through a method-owned Discovery entry with Pattern-specific intent and bounded controls.
- Pattern runs show truthful lifecycle, evidence, candidate/provenance, and handoff states.
- Unsupported or incomplete handoff states never render as import-ready.
- Legacy Pattern access tests pass.
- Signal and Debate regressions pass when shared surfaces are touched.
- Cross-Method Handoff Consistency can use Debate, Signal, and Pattern behavior as real inputs.

## 12. Human approval gates

CEO/Product review should confirm before implementation:

1. Which Pattern evidence fields are required for the first native slice.
2. Whether Pattern handoff remains display-only until Cross-Method Handoff Consistency.
3. Whether candidate selection/promotion should persist through existing backend APIs or remain a UI/provenance view over existing artifacts.
4. Whether any backend adapter is approved if the frontend cannot read required Pattern artifacts through existing APIs.
5. Whether Pattern should proceed immediately, or System Builder should be reprioritized.

### CEO/Product approval decisions — 2026-05-06

- Approved for implementation as the next Discovery Method Porting child PRD after Foundation #602 and Signal #608/#609.
- Minimum Pattern evidence surface for the first native slice: pattern label/name, recurrence summary, market scope/timeframe, source run or artifact reference, and an available quality/relevance metric when present. Unsupported fields must be hidden or shown as unavailable, not synthesized.
- Pattern handoff remains display-only unless an existing valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package is present and passes readiness checks. Candidate previews alone must never render `ready`.
- Candidate selection/promotion should remain a UI/provenance view over existing artifacts for this slice. New persistence or Training import behavior is deferred to Cross-Method Handoff Consistency or a follow-up PRD.
- Backend changes are not approved by default. Only a minimal non-breaking adapter for reading existing Pattern artifacts may be proposed; anything broader must stop for explicit approval.
- Proceed with Pattern Discovery now. System Builder remains deferred.

## 13. Non-goal reminders for implementation agents

- Do not implement System Builder while touching Pattern.
- Do not implement cross-method handoff consistency inside this PRD.
- Do not change Training import behavior.
- Do not mark Pattern handoff `ready` from candidate previews.
- Do not delete legacy routes or aliases.
- Do not expand into backend rewrites without explicit approval.

## 14. Open questions

Resolved by CEO/Product approval on 2026-05-06:

- Minimum evidence surface: pattern label/name, recurrence summary, market scope/timeframe, source run or artifact reference, and an available quality/relevance metric when present.
- Candidate selection/promotion persistence: defer new persistence; use existing artifacts only in this slice.
- Lifecycle vocabulary: reuse the Signal-linked lifecycle vocabulary where possible, with Pattern-specific `blocked` or `decision_required` copy when evidence or package readiness is incomplete.
- Legacy prominence: keep existing Training-side Pattern entry points reachable; do not delete, rename, or hide them in this slice.

# [PRD] TikTape-backed Hyperliquid datafeed catalog enablement

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Trigger: follow-up from GitHub issue #574 and Hyperliquid/TikTape historical bootstrap work.
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.
> Base branch: `main`.
> Working branch: `feat/tiktape-backed-datafeed-catalog-enablement-612`.
> Status: done; implemented and merged via PR #909.

---

title: TikTape-backed Hyperliquid datafeed catalog enablement
lifecycle: done
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-06-05
pipeline_status: done
prd_review_status: approved
assigned_agent: Evonome-data agent
worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data
base_branch: main
working_branch: feat/tiktape-backed-datafeed-catalog-enablement-612
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2

---

## CEO approval decisions

Approved for bounded implementation on 2026-06-05 with these binding decisions:

- Use the existing canonical/chart market catalog and readiness evidence as source of truth. TikTape coverage is provenance/evidence, not a parallel catalog source.
- Expose validated markets/timeframes as catalog-visible/selectable only. Live sync remains disabled unless an operator explicitly enables it behind a separate approved gate.
- Do not mutate production or preview collector schedules in this PRD. Schedule changes and bulk live enablement require a later human gate.
- Reuse and extend #820 validated chart market catalog and #845 readiness contracts. Do not create a second readiness model or duplicate catalog truth.
- Support the full TikTape/bootstrap interval set only where backed by canonical coverage/readiness evidence. Monthly `1M` must be calendar-month aware or fail closed.
- Keep internal capability models provider-neutral. Hyperliquid/TikTape are the first validation profile and provenance source, not the product boundary.
- Bulk enablement may be represented as a non-executing preview/dry-run or scoped admin selection model only. No broad live enable action is approved.
- #730, #796, #824, #820, #819, and #845 are complete and provide the candle/catalog/readiness foundation this PRD must not disturb.

---

## Problem / outcome

We are bootstrapping broad Hyperliquid historical OHLCV coverage from TikTape, but the live/datafeed adapter still exposes and enables only a small subset of Hyperliquid symbols and timeframes. Now that canonical candle/catalog/readiness foundations exist, operators need validated TikTape-backed assets/timeframes to be visible and selectable through the existing catalog surfaces, while keeping live collection opt-in and safe.

Desired outcome: every validated TikTape-backed Hyperliquid market/timeframe is available through the product's existing datafeed catalog/readiness paths and is clearly marked by capability: historical data available, live Hyperliquid-tradable, orderbook-supported, or historical-only. Intentional sync/collection enablement is modeled as an operator-reviewed plan, not executed by this PRD.

## Goals

- Expose validated TikTape-supported Hyperliquid markets through the existing datafeed symbol catalog without enabling all live streams by default.
- Expand Hyperliquid timeframe handling to the complete TikTape/bootstrap interval set:
  - `1m`, `3m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `2h`, `4h`, `6h`, `8h`, `12h`, `1d`, `3d`, `1w`, `1M`
- Preserve exchange-specific symbol identity, including case-sensitive symbols like `kPEPE` and synthetic/index-style markets like `@201`.
- Distinguish historical availability from live Hyperliquid collector support.
- Let operators preview bulk-enable or selectively enable plans for symbols/timeframes after reviewing storage and live stream impact; execution remains behind a later human gate.

## Non-goals

- Do not train Predict directly from TikTape.
- Do not hardcode API keys or provider credentials.
- Do not automatically enable all 500+ markets for live WebSocket/orderbook collection.
- Do not require TikTape for normal Predict/model training once data is stored in PostgreSQL.
- Do not replace native Hyperliquid metadata; reconcile it with TikTape coverage.

## Current observations

- `backend/config/datafeed.yaml` currently lists a small Hyperliquid subset.
- `symbol_sync_config` contains only a limited set of Hyperliquid rows and enabled symbols.
- Native Hyperliquid symbol cache and TikTape validated coverage have different scopes.
- Some datafeed code validates Hyperliquid symbols as short alphabetic strings, which rejects `@...` markets and may alter case-sensitive names.
- Some datafeed timeframe constants omit intervals already supported by the bootstrap path.

## Functional requirements

### 1. Catalog exposure from canonical readiness evidence

- Add a safe exposure/sync path from canonical catalog/readiness evidence into the datafeed catalog surfaces.
- Imported rows must default to disabled for live sync.
- Preserve raw exchange symbol exactly as provided by the coverage artifact.
- Record enough metadata to explain why a symbol is available:
  - source/provenance: TikTape coverage, native Hyperliquid metadata, canonical readiness evidence, or combinations of those sources
  - historical availability
  - live collector eligibility
  - orderbook eligibility when known

### 2. Capability-aware enablement

- Reuse or extend provider-neutral capability flags so operators can distinguish:
  - historical candles available in PostgreSQL
  - eligible for live candle stream
  - eligible for orderbook stream
  - historical-only / not native-live-tradable
- Enabling sync for a symbol must not imply orderbook collection unless explicitly selected.
- Bulk enablement preview/dry-run must support filters such as live-tradable only, historical-only, or selected assets.

### 3. Full timeframe support

- Normalize Hyperliquid/TikTape timeframe constants across:
  - datafeed config validation
  - subscribed-symbols endpoint
  - collector/history helpers
  - gap/backfill helpers where applicable
  - tests and UI responses
- Add support for `8h`, `3d`, and `1M` where currently missing and backed by canonical coverage evidence.
- Ensure monthly candle handling is calendar-month aware where historical data is interpreted.

### 4. Startup and schedule behavior

- Ensure `collector_schedules` and YAML fallback behavior can represent the broader catalog without auto-starting every asset by accident.
- Provide a dry-run plan or admin preview for creating/updating a Hyperliquid schedule from enabled symbols only; do not apply schedule changes in this PRD.
- Keep primary/default symbols small unless explicitly overridden.

### 5. UI/API visibility

- Datafeed APIs should show all available Hyperliquid catalog entries, not only currently enabled symbols.
- Subscribed/enabled views should remain separate from available/catalog views.
- Bar-count summaries should include all stored timeframes when historical data exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- All validated TikTape-supported markets can be exposed through existing catalog/config surfaces without being enabled by default.
- Existing enabled-symbol behavior remains backward compatible for currently tracked assets.
- Hyperliquid timeframe validation accepts all 15 bootstrap intervals.
- Case-sensitive and `@...` symbols are preserved and not rejected by validation.
- Operators can identify which symbols are historical-only versus live-tradable.
- A bulk enable/selective enable preview or dry-run path exists with safe defaults; execution is separately gated.
- Tests cover symbol import, timeframe validation, capability flags, and subscribed-symbols/API behavior.

## Suggested implementation tasks

- [ ] Audit current datafeed symbol/config tables and decide whether to extend `symbol_sync_config`, `exchange_symbol_cache`, or add a separate capability table.
- [ ] Implement canonical readiness-backed TikTape coverage exposure into the Hyperliquid catalog with disabled-by-default sync rows.
- [ ] Expand Hyperliquid timeframe constants and tests to the full 15-interval set.
- [ ] Relax Hyperliquid symbol validation to preserve case and allow validated `@...` markets where appropriate.
- [ ] Reconcile native Hyperliquid symbol metadata with TikTape-supported markets.
- [ ] Update datafeed/subscribed-symbol APIs so available catalog and enabled subscriptions are distinct.
- [ ] Add operator-safe bulk enablement and schedule update preview/dry-run flow.
- [ ] Add regression tests for historical-only symbols, live-tradable symbols, and full timeframe coverage.

## Validation commands

- `cd backend && python3 -m pytest tests/services/collector/test_datafeed_config.py tests/api/test_datafeed_subscribed_symbols.py tests/api/test_hyperliquid_config_hotreload.py -q`
- Add targeted tests for any new catalog import service or API.
- `git diff --check`

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Depends on completed #730/#796/#824/#820/#845 candle, catalog, and readiness foundations.
- Should consider findings from #574 and related bootstrap PRs.
- Numeric overflow/data-quality failures from the bootstrap should be handled separately unless they block catalog import.

## Human gates

Escalate before:

- enabling all live Hyperliquid streams by default,
- applying bulk enablement or schedule changes outside preview/dry-run mode,
- creating a parallel catalog/readiness source of truth,
- changing production collector schedules,
- adding provider credentials or secrets to config,
- making Predict depend directly on TikTape,
- changing database schema in a way that affects existing enabled-symbol behavior.

## Provider-neutral implementation note

Hyperliquid and TikTape are validation/provenance profiles for this PRD. Shared schemas, capability names, API responses, and UI semantics must stay provider-neutral and fail closed when another provider lacks equivalent historical, live, orderbook, timeframe, or provenance capabilities.

# PRD: Discovery Debate Frontend Fixes

## Status
- Pipeline Status: Approved
- PRD Review Status: Approved
- CEO Approved: Yes
- CEO Approved At: 2026-05-06
- Priority: P2 — ship all three fixes together in the next frontend pass
- Canonical Source: this GitHub issue body
- GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2

## Ownership
- Assigned Agent: Evonome-frontend agent
- Agent Label: `agent:evonome-frontend`
- Worktree Path: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-frontend`
- Repository: `hyperbotsx/SoldierOne`
- Target Surface: Preview frontend at `https://preview.evonome.com/app/discovery/debate`

## Background
The frontend needs a grouped fix PRD that can collect multiple UI issues before implementation. Some issues are specific to Discovery Debate, while others apply globally across the site and theme system. The first reported issue is in Experiment 2 while backend/job hardening is happening in another session. A large number of jobs accumulating is expected, and several views correctly show all jobs.

## Problem Statements

### Issue 1: Pipeline View omits expected Experiment 2 jobs
- Page: `https://preview.evonome.com/app/discovery/debate`
- Experiment: Experiment 2
- Reported views that show all jobs as expected:
  - Mind map
  - Concept map
  - Table view
- Broken view:
  - Pipeline View does not show all jobs that appear in the other views.
- User evidence:
  - Table view screenshot: https://cleanshot.com/share/r58sfQWk
  - Pipeline view screenshot: https://cleanshot.com/share/Xsr8mg60



### Issue 2: Global light theme editor surface tones are too high-contrast
- Scope: whole-site theme system and theme editor, not only Discovery Debate. Discovery Debate screenshots are examples of the global theme problem.
- Example page: `https://preview.evonome.com/app/discovery/debate`
- Affected surfaces: central content areas, tables, pipeline-style panels, cards, rows, bright surface areas, and any shared components that consume the editable light-theme tokens.
- Dark theme: no issue reported. Treat the dark theme as the visual reference for subtle surface layering, but do not change dark-theme behavior unless required by shared-token plumbing and verified not to alter its appearance.
- Light theme issue: central white/content areas are too bright compared with the selected off-white/warm background. They should use a pale off-yellow/off-white tone that remains brighter than the background while staying in the same tonal family.
- Theme editor requirement: adjust the theme editor/token mapping so users can control this surface hierarchy globally. The fix should come from the theme system rather than a page-specific override.
- Desired direction: light theme should mirror the dark theme's subtle layered relationship, but with warm pale tones rather than stark white panels.
- User evidence:
  - Dark theme example screenshot: https://cleanshot.com/share/6QBCf1CW
  - Light theme example screenshot: https://cleanshot.com/share/1cl17bwh


### Issue 3: Theme editor cannot save current choices as the app default
- Page: `https://preview.evonome.com/app/admin/theme`
- Current gap: users can tune theme settings such as square corners, background tint, accent, and related theme controls, but there is no explicit action to save the current configuration as the default app theme.
- Desired behavior: a user should be able to save the currently selected theme configuration as their preferred default. Future app loads should apply that saved default according to the confirmed existing preference scope.
- Preference scope gate: before implementation, engineering must inspect the existing theme/preference persistence model and confirm whether defaults are browser-local, authenticated-user-scoped, workspace-scoped, or another existing scope.
- Overwrite behavior: saving a new default should replace the previous saved default within the confirmed scope.
- UI requirement: add a clear action on the theme editor page, such as `Save as default` or equivalent concise wording.
- User evidence: https://cleanshot.com/share/drrvYHww

## Goals
- Make Pipeline View show the same complete set of expected jobs for Experiment 2 as Table View, Mind Map, and Concept Map.
- Preserve existing expected behavior for job accumulation during hardening.
- Ensure the Pipeline View uses the same canonical job source/filtering semantics as the other views unless there is an intentional, documented view-specific filter.
- Keep the Pipeline View completeness fix scoped to Discovery Debate frontend behavior unless investigation proves a shared contract issue.
- Improve light theme surface hierarchy globally through the theme editor/token system so the whole site feels visually cohesive with the selected app background.
- Let users persist their current theme editor choices as the default app theme for future loads according to the confirmed existing preference scope.

## Non-Goals
- Do not suppress, delete, or otherwise reduce accumulated jobs just to make views match.
- Do not change backend hardening behavior in this PRD unless a frontend-visible contract bug is confirmed and explicitly added.
- Do not redesign the Pipeline View layout beyond what is needed to display the full expected job set.

## Functional Requirements

### FR1: Pipeline job completeness
Pipeline View must render every Experiment 2 job that the canonical jobs dataset marks as visible for the current experiment and that appears in Table View under equivalent user-selected filters.

### FR2: Filter parity
Any filters, status grouping, pagination, virtualization, or stage mapping applied by Pipeline View must not accidentally exclude jobs that are visible in sibling views.

### FR3: Empty/overflow state clarity
If Pipeline View intentionally hides jobs because of an explicit user-selected filter, collapsed group, pagination, or unsupported status/stage, the UI must make that state discoverable instead of silently omitting jobs.

### FR4: Regression guard
Add or update tests so a dataset with many accumulated Experiment 2 jobs remains visible in Pipeline View and Table View with matching counts under equivalent filters.


### FR5: Global light theme surface tone refinement
The theme system must provide and apply light-theme tokens that create subtle tonal layering between the app background, central content region, tables, panels, cards, rows, borders, and muted text across the whole site.

### FR6: Light theme off-white surfaces
Light theme central content surfaces must avoid pure or near-pure white when the surrounding app background is warm/off-white. Surfaces should remain slightly brighter than the background while staying in the same warm tonal family.

### FR8: Theme-editor-first styling
Implement tonal fixes through the theme editor, shared theme tokens, or existing design primitives where possible, not one-off hardcoded colors in individual views.


### FR9: Save current theme as default
The theme editor must provide a clear action that persists the current theme configuration as the user's default app theme.

### FR10: Default theme auto-load
On future app loads, the app must initialize with the saved default theme according to the confirmed existing preference scope instead of falling back to an older default or unsaved temporary selection.

### FR11: Default overwrite behavior
Saving a new default theme must replace the previous saved default for that user/scope without creating ambiguous competing defaults.

### FR12: Save feedback and failure handling
The theme editor must show clear success and failure feedback when saving the default theme, and it must not imply persistence if the save fails.

### FR13: Preference scope discovery gate
Engineering must confirm and use the existing preference/theme persistence architecture before implementing saved defaults. If no clear existing model is available, stop and return a product/architecture recommendation instead of adding parallel storage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given Experiment 2 with many accumulated jobs, Table View and Pipeline View show matching total visible job counts under equivalent filters.
- Jobs shown in Table View can be located in Pipeline View, including jobs in less common statuses/stages.
- No expected accumulated jobs disappear from Pipeline View due to client-side limits, stale memoization, stage mapping gaps, or incompatible status filters.
- Existing Mind Map, Concept Map, and Table View behavior remains unchanged except for shared fixes that improve consistency.
- Automated coverage exists for the completeness/parity case, or the PRD task records a clear reason if existing test infrastructure cannot support it.

- In light theme, the central content area no longer appears as stark white against the warmer app background; it uses a warmer pale tone with subtle contrast.
- Dark theme appearance remains unchanged unless unavoidable shared-token changes are explicitly justified and verified.
- Primary, secondary, and muted text remain readable in light theme after the surface tone changes.
- The tonal adjustments apply consistently across shared site surfaces and do not create a one-off fix limited to Discovery Debate or a single screenshot state.
- The theme editor exposes or correctly maps the relevant surface tones so global theme changes produce coherent layered surfaces.

- The theme editor includes a clear `Save as default`-style action near the existing theme controls.
- After changing theme settings and saving as default, reloading the app applies those saved settings according to the confirmed existing preference scope.
- Saving a second configuration as default overwrites the first saved default within that confirmed scope.
- If persistence fails, the user sees an error state and the prior default remains intact.
- The implementation uses the existing theme persistence/user preference model where available rather than adding a parallel storage mechanism.
- If no clear existing persistence model exists, implementation pauses with a product/architecture recommendation before adding new storage.

## Investigation Notes for Implementer
- Compare the data source, experiment selector, filters, status/stage normalization, grouping, pagination, and memoization used by Pipeline View against Table View.
- Look for hardcoded limits, status allowlists, unknown-stage drops, stale cache keys, or rendering virtualization assumptions.
- Verify whether Pipeline View uses a derived pipeline-specific dataset that can fall out of sync with the canonical job list.
- Treat Table View as the visible-count reference for this issue unless product direction says otherwise.

- Audit the theme editor and light-theme tokens currently used for app background, content background, table surfaces, cards, borders, muted text, and row/card hover states.
- Identify any hardcoded `white`, near-white, black, or near-black classes in shared surfaces and replace them with theme tokens where practical.
- Check light mode against the current dark theme reference after changes; the intended light-mode relationship is subtle layered warm tones, not high-contrast white blocks.
- Verify that Discovery Debate is only an example consumer of the global theme fix, not the only patched surface.

- Inspect existing theme editor state, persistence, and app initialization logic before adding storage.
- Determine whether defaults are user-scoped, workspace-scoped, browser-local, or backend-backed; implement consistently with existing preference patterns.
- If no clear existing preference model exists, stop and return a product/architecture recommendation instead of inventing parallel storage.
- Confirm whether the current editor already persists draft/current selections separately from app defaults, and avoid conflating temporary preview state with saved default state.

## Verifier Checkpoints
1. Verify the implementation evidence that Table View and Pipeline View use equivalent filtering for Experiment 2 job visibility.
2. Verify automated coverage or documented manual reproduction proving Pipeline View count parity for a large accumulated-job dataset.
3. Verify light theme screenshots for global shared surfaces, including the Discovery Debate example, show subtle warm tonal layering and no stark white central panels; verify dark theme remains unchanged.
4. Verify theme default persistence discovery, including the confirmed existing preference scope or a product/architecture stop if no clear model exists.
5. Verify the theme editor can save a customized theme as default, app reload applies it according to the confirmed scope, and a later save overwrites the prior default.
6. Final verifier bug-check pass after all scoped frontend fixes in this PRD are complete.

## Open Items / Future Issue Intake
Additional frontend issues from the user should be appended to this PRD as new problem statements, requirements, and acceptance criteria before implementation approval.

## 1. Problem

Genesis Phase 1 hardening has produced useful family-specific fixes for volatility and mean reversion, but the work is not yet tracked as a single program across the full Operator Matrix. Without one canonical PRD, family hardening can drift into ad hoc loops, unclear completion criteria, and unsafe Phase 2 assumptions.

Operators need one source of truth for all ten strategy-family hardening tracks, their current Phase 1 status, blockers, validation evidence, and the human gate before any downstream phase proceeds.

## 2. Goal

Run Genesis Phase 1 hardening across all ten Operator Matrix families until each family reaches a reproducible Phase 1 green flag: `goal_met` with deterministic validators passing, adversarial debug passing, portable artifacts present, lessons captured safely, and no Phase 2 confirmation sent.

A family is considered Phase 1 green only when the latest canonical evidence shows:

- `goal_met: true`
- `debug_verdict: PASS`
- preflight, coupling, execution semantics, and comparability pass
- required Phase 1 artifacts are present and inspectable
- no unresolved Phase 1 debug findings remain
- no Phase 2 confirmation or Phase 2 artifacts were created
- validation commands and commit evidence are recorded

## 3. Non-Goals

- Do not confirm or advance Phase 2 in this PRD.
- Do not claim trading, training, deployment, or production approval from Phase 1 alone.
- Do not open PRs automatically.
- Do not create repo-local PRD copies.
- Do not make planned families runnable without explicit approval and safety checks.
- Do not bypass deterministic validation, adversarial recheck, or human gates.

## 4. Tracked Families

Phase 1 status has two distinct green levels:

1. **Canonical seed green**: the locked family seed reaches `goal_met` with deterministic validators and adversarial debug passing.
2. **Family Phase 1 ready**: canonical seed green plus seed-corpus maturity across multiple family-valid seed shapes.

A family must not be marked broadly Phase 1 ready from one canonical seed alone unless the CEO explicitly defers corpus maturity.

Definitions:

- **Seed**: a reusable family-valid prompt/contract scaffold such as `volatility_phase1` or `vol_alt_side_split_fill_stress_v1`. A seed captures the allowed strategy family, signal lineage, causal timing, execution assumptions, validation stress rules, known blocker lessons, and family-specific guardrails.
- **Job / attempt**: one concrete generation/recheck run from a seed, with its own attempt ID, artifacts, validator results, debug verdict, blockers, and Phase 2 absence evidence. A seed can produce many jobs over time.
- **Canonical seed green**: the locked seed has a current accepted job with `goal_met=true`, debug `PASS`, validators passing, and no Phase 2 artifacts.
- **Corpus evidence green**: a specific alternate seed has an accepted job with the same Phase 1 evidence criteria. This supports, but does not by itself equal, family Phase 1 readiness.

Contract generation flow for future strategy ideas:

1. A user and/or agents propose a strategy through adversarial debate.
2. The generator classifies the proposal into an approved family, or marks it decision-required if it would create a new family or drift outside the selected family.
3. The family seed/corpus supplies the scaffold: allowed indicators, causal timing, execution semantics, validation stress requirements, comparator rules, and known hardening guardrails.
4. The generated `phase1_contract.yaml` becomes the source of truth for the job. The job result must be read from the contract artifacts and validators, not from seed identity alone.
5. Any source-fixable contract/debug blocker must become a deterministic source/test fix. After such a fix, rerun the canonical seed and the affected alternate/job before accepting evidence.

Search-parameter governance:

- `search_contract.search_parameter_contracts` is the authoritative source of truth for any parameter that a future backtester or optimizer may expose in an Optimized section.
- A parameter must not appear in the optimizer UI unless it is declared in `search_parameter_contracts`.
- A declared search parameter must include at minimum: stable name, symbol, binding target, default, allowed values or range/step, owner phase, and any guardrail notes needed by validators.
- The backtester/optimizer must consume `search_parameter_contracts`; it must not invent additional knobs from indicator fields, UI heuristics, or raw prompt text.
- Family seeds define the allowed parameter categories. Adversarial debate may propose candidate knobs, but the verifier/debugger must reject knobs that are non-causal, overfit-prone, not executable, outside the family, or not wired to a machine-checkable binding.
- Every optimizable parameter must be bound to executable strategy behavior. Changing the parameter must change the relevant rule, hash, simulation input, or explicit runtime binding. Declared-but-hardcoded parameters are Phase 1 contract bugs.
- Constants not declared in `search_parameter_contracts` are fixed for that Phase 1 contract and should not be tuned in downstream tooling.

Future blocker handling:

- Expected external blockers, such as missing immutable funding artifacts, may leave a job operationally blocked while still accepted as Phase 1 green evidence when validators and debug pass and Phase 2 artifacts are absent.
- Source-fixable contract bugs may be repaired in a bounded supervised loop: patch generator/contract code, add or update deterministic tests, run targeted validation, commit, redeploy preview when needed, rerun canonical seed, rerun affected alternate/job, and record evidence.
- Product or strategy blockers, such as invalid thesis, family drift, new-family creation, or downstream promotion decisions, must be marked decision-required and must not be auto-fixed, auto-promoted, or converted into Phase 2 approval.
- Automatic detection/classification is allowed; automatic Phase 2 confirmation, family activation, promotion, or new prepared-track activation is not allowed without an explicit human gate.

## 6. Program Phases

### Phase A: PRD setup and evidence ledger

- [x] Approve this parent PRD.
- [x] Link existing volatility and mean-reversion evidence.
- [x] Normalize the per-family evidence template.
- [x] Confirm the authoritative worktree, branch policy, and runtime namespaces.

### Phase B: Foundation readiness

- [x] Complete or link the family module/refactor dependency in #586.
- [x] Confirm all ten families exist in the registry or have safe non-runnable stubs.
- [x] Confirm LCM memory read/write safety boundaries.
- [x] Confirm run caps, deploy caps, recheck caps, and watchdog behavior.

### Phase C: Per-family canonical-seed Phase 1 hardening

For each family:

- [ ] Seed/readiness checked for the canonical locked seed.
- [ ] One-cycle smoke run passes or produces a bounded source-fix blocker.
- [ ] Extended Phase 1 hardening run starts only after preflight and explicit activation.
- [ ] Source changes are validated with targeted pytest and ruff before commit/recheck.
- [ ] Latest canonical recheck reaches `goal_met` or records a hard blocker.
- [ ] LCM lessons are sanitized and recorded only through the approved path.
- [ ] No Phase 2 confirmation is sent.

### Phase C2: Per-family seed-corpus maturity

For each family after canonical `goal_met`:

- [ ] At least three alternate in-family seed shapes are defined or attached.
- [ ] Alternate seeds pass deterministic readiness and family-drift checks.
- [ ] Alternate seeds run one-cycle smoke/recheck, or a CEO-approved deferral is recorded.
- [ ] Any new source-fixable blocker is converted into deterministic tests/validators.
- [ ] Canonical seed and affected alternate seed are rerun after corpus fixes.
- [ ] Family is marked broadly Phase 1 ready only after corpus maturity passes or is explicitly deferred.

### Phase D: Cross-family Phase 1 consolidation

- [x] All ten families are canonical green and corpus-mature, or explicitly deferred with CEO-approved rationale.
- [x] Cross-family regression suite passes.
- [x] Portable artifact schema checks pass across green families and corpus attempts.
- [x] Operator Matrix status reflects canonical and corpus readiness separately.
- [x] Final Phase 1 evidence pack is prepared for human review.

### Phase E: Human gate before downstream phases

After Phase 1 is green across the program, the CEO/operator chooses what to do next. Phase 2 remains blocked until this gate is approved.

Possible post-Phase-1 actions:

1. Select which green families should advance.
2. Confirm Phase 2 separately per selected family.
3. Run downstream validation/backtest/search/training integration.
4. Compare families on common cost, slippage, funding, capacity, and robustness criteria.
5. Promote only families that pass downstream gates.

## 7. Acceptance Criteria

- [x] This GitHub issue is the canonical PRD and is added to Project 2.
- [x] Each of the ten families has visible canonical-seed and corpus-maturity status plus evidence trail.
- [x] Mean-reversion and volatility existing canonical results are verified before being marked canonical green.
- [x] Volatility and mean-reversion corpus maturity is either completed or explicitly deferred before they are marked broadly Phase 1 ready.
- [x] Every new family run has isolated runtime metadata and stop conditions.
- [x] `goal_met` for one seed is never treated as full family coverage, Phase 2, or production approval.
- [x] The final program state clearly separates canonical green, corpus-mature Phase 1 ready, Phase 2 approved, and downstream promoted.

## 8. Validation Expectations

Per-family validation should include targeted Genesis tests and ruff for touched files. Common commands should be recorded in the family evidence section, typically including:

```bash
cd backend && TMPDIR=/mnt/hyperliquid-data/tmp UV_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/hyperliquid-data/tmp/uv-cache \
  uv run pytest tests/genesis/test_phase1_contract_generation.py \
  tests/genesis/test_phase1_contract_seed_alignment.py \
  tests/genesis/test_debugger.py -q
```

```bash
cd backend && TMPDIR=/mnt/hyperliquid-data/tmp UV_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/hyperliquid-data/tmp/uv-cache \
  uv run ruff check app/services/genesis tests/genesis
```

Before any PR is requested, run the repo quality gate if available.

## 9. Dependencies and Related PRDs

- #616: Prepared Phase 1 track configs for the next eight Operator Matrix families
- PR #653: Mean-reversion Phase C2 corpus maturity source/evidence merge
- #657 / PR #661: Trend/Momentum canonical Phase 1 activation/evidence
- PR #669: Funding/carry canonical Phase 1/F2 activation/evidence
- #586: Genesis ideator family module refactor and 50-cycle hardening gate
- #579: Admin Hardening Parallel Lane Operations and Observability
- #563: Adversarial debate operational matrix and portable config artifacts
- #571: Admin Hardening Operator Matrix Dashboard
- #584: Historical Operator Matrix category expansion reference
- #585: Historical hardening LCM blocker memory reference

## 10. Open Questions

- Should the program execute strictly in family order 1 through 10, or allow safe parallel lanes after #579 isolation is proven?
- Resolved 2026-05-07: volatility canonical seed green and Phase C2 corpus maturity require the evidence recorded in the Volatility canonical and corpus evidence sections.
- Resolved 2026-05-08: mean-reversion canonical seed green and Phase C2 corpus maturity require the evidence recorded in the Mean-reversion canonical and corpus evidence sections.
- Resolved 2026-05-09: funding/carry canonical/F2 evidence requires the evidence recorded in the Funding/carry canonical-seed evidence section. Resolved 2026-05-16: funding/carry corpus maturity requires the evidence recorded in the Funding/carry Phase C2 corpus evidence ledger; promotion readiness remains blocked by the immutable timestamped funding artifact gate.
- Which families should be eligible for Phase 2 after all Phase 1 green flags are achieved?


## 11. Post-Phase-1 Program Brief for Next PRD Agents

When all ten families are canonical green and corpus-mature, this PRD should hand off to new downstream PRDs rather than continuing Phase 2 implicitly.

The next agent should produce PRDs that answer these questions:

1. **Family selection:** Which Phase 1-ready families should advance, and which should remain research-only?
2. **Phase 2 confirmation plan:** What explicit human gate, artifact bundle, and per-family approval wording is required before Phase 2 starts?
3. **Downstream validation:** How will Phase 2/2.5 validate backtests, walk-forward search, cost/funding/slippage realism, capacity, and robustness across selected families?
4. **Cross-family comparison:** How will families be compared on a common scorecard without mixing incompatible objectives?
5. **Training/import integration:** How will portable Phase 1 artifacts feed training, search, or strategy configuration contracts safely?
6. **Promotion governance:** What criteria move a family from research-ready to candidate-promotable, paper-tradable, or production-eligible?
7. **Operational rollout:** What runtime isolation, preview/deploy policy, monitoring, rollback, and audit evidence are needed for any later live-facing flow?

Expected next PRD set after this program:

- PRD: Genesis Phase 2 Confirmation and Artifact-Gate Workflow
- PRD: Cross-Family Validation, Backtest, and Robustness Scorecard
- PRD: Strategy Config Import and Training/Search Integration
- PRD: Candidate Promotion Governance and Operator Review
- PRD: Production/Paper-Trading Readiness, Monitoring, and Rollback

Hard stop: none of these downstream PRDs may assume Phase 2 is approved solely because Phase 1 reached `goal_met` or corpus maturity.

## Deferred Related PRDs

- #621 Strategy complexity profiles for seed generation is intentionally deferred. It should remain a future/reference PRD until Genesis Phase 1 hardening is completed as planned. It must not expand this PRD's active scope, change current Phase C2 execution, activate additional tracks, or alter the one-seed-at-a-time volatility corpus workflow.

# PRD: Cross-Method Handoff Consistency

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Assigned agent/worktree: Evonome-discovery (`/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery`).
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Parent PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593
> Foundation PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/602
> Signal precedent: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/608 / https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/609
> Pattern precedent: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/611 / https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/617
> Proposed branch after approval: `feat/cross-method-handoff-consistency`
> Migration note: repo-local PRD files are not canonical for this workflow. Update this issue body instead of maintaining a separate PRD copy.

---

---
title: Cross-Method Handoff Consistency
slug: cross-method-handoff-consistency
created: 2026-05-06
status: done
prd_review_status: approved
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-06T13:06:30Z
github_issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/618
originating_worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
parent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593
foundation_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/602
signal_precedent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/608
signal_precedent_pr: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/609
pattern_precedent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/611
pattern_precedent_pr: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/617
proposed_branch_after_approval: feat/cross-method-handoff-consistency
---

## 1. Problem

Discovery Method Foundation defined the shared method registry, method contracts, and light handoff vocabulary. Signal Discovery and Pattern Discovery then proved native non-Debate methods with local false-ready guards.

The next risk is method drift. Debate, Signal, Pattern, and later Builder can each display readiness, blockers, missing package states, and next actions differently. If those differences remain method-specific, operators may mistake candidate previews or partial evidence for import-ready Strategy Configuration / Handoff Packages.

The product needs one consistent Discovery-owned handoff semantics layer before downstream Training import decisions rely on native method output.

## 2. Product goal

Normalize handoff/readiness semantics across Debate, Signal, Pattern, and future Builder methods so Discovery only shows `ready` when a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package exists, and all non-ready states provide consistent blocker and next-action guidance.

This PRD should consolidate shared helpers and contracts where safe, preserve method-specific evidence review, and protect existing Debate, Signal, and Pattern behavior with targeted regressions.

## 3. Locked context and dependencies

- Parent umbrella PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593.
- Discovery Method Foundation is complete: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/602.
- Signal Discovery native method precedent is complete: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/608 / https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/609.
- Pattern Discovery native method is the immediate precedent: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/611. Implementation PR https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/617 merged on 2026-05-06 with targeted Pattern tests, compatibility tests, Discovery term gate, typecheck, and final bug-check evidence recorded.
- Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package remains the Discovery-to-Training boundary.
- Training import, evaluation, optimization, refinement, and writeback behavior must not change unless explicitly approved by CEO/Product.
- Builder and Evolutionary method behavior remains future work unless existing shared surfaces already expose readiness that this PRD must protect.

## 4. In scope

- One shared handoff readiness vocabulary: `ready`, `blocked`, `incomplete`, `unavailable`, and `decision_required`.
- Shared package-backed readiness check used by Debate, Signal, Pattern, and future Builder-ready seams where safe.
- Shared false-ready guard that prevents candidate previews, promoted candidates, evidence summaries, ensembles, local config-ready booleans, or legacy preview flags from producing `ready` without a valid package.
- Consistent user-facing copy for readiness state, blocker reason, next action, and consequence.
- Consolidation of duplicated Signal/Pattern readiness helpers into shared Discovery helpers where it does not destabilize method-specific behavior.
- Debate readiness alignment with the package-backed contract while preserving existing Debate artifact visibility.
- Regression protection for Debate, Signal, and Pattern route/detail/modal/handoff states.
- Documentation of the shared handoff contract and method-specific adapter responsibilities.
- Follow-up notes for Builder/Evolutionary coverage if implementation finds existing surfaces that need future native support.

## 5. Out of scope

- Training import, evaluation, optimization, refinement, or writeback behavior changes.
- New Training import endpoints or automatic imports from Discovery.
- Strategy Configuration schema/version changes.
- Backend migrations or broad API rewrites.
- System Builder native implementation.
- Evolutionary Strategy native implementation.
- New persistence for candidate selections or promotions.
- Deleting legacy routes, aliases, or Training-side method flows.
- Redesigning method detail modals beyond handoff/readiness copy and shared helper integration.
- Marking any candidate, evidence, preview, or local promotion state as `ready` without a valid package.

## 6. User stories

### US-001: Shared readiness state contract

**Description:** As an operator, I want each Discovery method to use the same readiness states so I can understand whether a method output is ready for handoff or still blocked.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Discovery exposes one canonical readiness state type: `ready`, `blocked`, `incomplete`, `unavailable`, and `decision_required`.
- [ ] Debate, Signal, and Pattern handoff rendering consume the same canonical state names.
- [ ] Unknown or malformed readiness values fail closed to `incomplete`, `blocked`, or `unavailable`; they do not render `ready`.
- [ ] Tests cover each readiness state and at least one malformed/unknown state.

### US-002: Package-backed readiness only

**Description:** As a transition owner, I want `ready` to mean an actual Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package exists so no method appears import-ready from previews alone.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Shared readiness resolution returns `ready` only when a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package record or path exists and passes the readiness check.
- [ ] Candidate previews, evidence summaries, promoted items, ensembles, local `config_ready` flags, and legacy readiness flags do not produce `ready` by themselves.
- [ ] Debate package/artifact paths that are already valid continue to render `ready`.
- [ ] Signal and Pattern false-ready tests remain covered through shared helper tests or method-level regression tests.
- [ ] Tests include truthy preview payloads that must not render `ready` for Debate, Signal, and Pattern.

### US-003: Consistent copy and next-action guidance

**Description:** As a Discovery user, I want handoff cards to tell me what is missing and what to do next without implementation narration.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Each readiness state has concise copy for status, reason, next action, and consequence.
- [ ] Copy avoids Training-owned claims unless a real package is ready for Training import review.
- [ ] `decision_required` clearly names the decision gate without implying a failure.
- [ ] `unavailable` distinguishes unsupported method capability from failed package generation.
- [ ] Method-specific details can add evidence context without changing shared readiness meaning.

### US-004: Shared helper and contract consolidation

**Description:** As a future implementer, I want Debate, Signal, Pattern, and Builder to share handoff semantics without duplicating fragile method-specific logic.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Duplicate Signal/Pattern readiness helper logic is consolidated where safe.
- [ ] Debate uses the shared package-backed resolver or a thin adapter around it without losing current artifact visibility.
- [ ] Shared helpers remain small and method-agnostic; method-specific evidence/provenance stays in method adapters.
- [ ] The helper contract documents expected inputs, fail-closed behavior, and adapter responsibilities.
- [ ] Builder/Evolutionary readiness seams are documented as future adapters unless touched by existing shared code.

### US-005: Regression protection across native methods

**Description:** As a product owner, I want the consistency pass to improve semantics without breaking existing native method flows.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Debate route, create entry, detail/modal handoff, and package artifact visibility still pass targeted regressions.
- [ ] Signal create/lifecycle/candidate/promotion/handoff regressions still pass where touched.
- [ ] Pattern create/lifecycle/evidence/candidate/handoff regressions still pass where touched.
- [ ] Historical Discovery aliases and legacy Training-side Signal/Pattern entries remain reachable.
- [ ] No route deletion, physical folder rename, or backend endpoint contract change is included.

### US-006: Documentation and handoff for later Builder

**Description:** As a future Builder implementer, I want a clear handoff semantics contract so Builder can adopt the same readiness behavior without another normalization pass.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A concise repo-visible note or implementation handoff documents shared readiness semantics, package-backed `ready`, false-ready guards, and copy rules.
- [ ] The note lists what Builder must provide to render each readiness state.
- [ ] Follow-ups are created only for uncovered Builder/Evolutionary work discovered during implementation.
- [ ] Validation evidence and verifier decisions are recorded in the task artifact folder.

## 7. Functional requirements

- **FR-1:** Discovery must have one canonical handoff readiness state contract for all native methods.
- **FR-2:** `ready` must require a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package.
- **FR-3:** Preview/candidate/evidence/provenance artifacts must not create `ready` handoff state by themselves.
- **FR-4:** Debate, Signal, and Pattern must expose consistent status, blocker, next-action, and consequence copy.
- **FR-5:** Shared helper consolidation must not remove method-specific evidence, provenance, or lifecycle behavior.
- **FR-6:** Legacy aliases and Training-side method access must remain reachable.
- **FR-7:** No Training import/writeback behavior changes are allowed without explicit approval.
- **FR-8:** Builder/Evolutionary support must be adapter-ready but not implemented unless already present in shared surfaces.

## 8. Implementation boundaries

Expected allowed paths:

- `frontend/src/discovery/**`
- `frontend/src/features/training-lab/workflows/**` only for compatibility metadata or tests proving legacy access remains reachable
- `frontend/src/experimental/workflows/**` only for compatibility metadata or tests proving legacy access remains reachable
- focused test files under the same frontend scopes
- concise implementation artifact folder under `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/<session>/`

Forbidden without separate approval:

- Training import/evaluation/writeback behavior
- backend migrations
- Strategy Configuration schema changes
- new persistence for candidate selections/promotions
- System Builder or Evolutionary Strategy native implementation
- route deletion or physical source folder renames
- deploy/config/secrets changes

## 9. Quality gates

Expected implementation gates:

- `pnpm --dir frontend typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir frontend check:discovery-terms`
- Targeted Vitest for shared handoff readiness resolver and copy mapping.
- Targeted Vitest for package-backed `ready` behavior and malformed-state fail-closed behavior.
- Targeted Vitest proving Debate preview/candidate-like artifacts do not create false-ready handoff state.
- Targeted Vitest proving Signal false-ready prevention still works through the shared helper.
- Targeted Vitest proving Pattern false-ready prevention still works through the shared helper.
- Targeted compatibility test proving legacy Training-side Signal and Pattern entries remain reachable.
- Targeted Debate, Signal, and Pattern route/detail/modal regressions for touched surfaces.
- `git diff --check`

Recommended pre-PR gates:

- Local quality gate if available: `/gate --ml`
- Verifier final bug-check after all scoped implementation is complete.

## 10. Verifier checkpoints

Implementation should use coder/verifier checkpoints before continuing across phases.

| Checkpoint | Scope | Required verifier focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shared readiness contract and package-backed resolver | State vocabulary, fail-closed behavior, package-backed `ready`, no Training behavior changes |
| 2 | Signal and Pattern helper consolidation | No candidate/preview false-ready state, method evidence/provenance preserved, tests migrated safely |
| 3 | Debate alignment and copy consistency | Debate artifacts remain visible, package-backed readiness only, consistent next-action copy |
| 4 | Compatibility, documentation, and final validation | Legacy access, quality gates, final bug-check, Builder follow-up notes, no scope creep |

A final verifier bug-check is required by default after implementation completion.

## 11. Success metrics

- Debate, Signal, and Pattern use one shared readiness vocabulary and consistent user-facing guidance.
- `ready` never appears without a valid Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package.
- Candidate previews, evidence summaries, promoted items, ensembles, and local ready booleans fail closed unless backed by a valid package.
- Debate, Signal, and Pattern regression tests pass.
- Legacy Training-side Signal and Pattern entries remain reachable.
- Builder can adopt the documented handoff contract later without redefining readiness semantics.

## 12. CEO/Product shaping decisions — 2026-05-06

These decisions resolve the approval questions for this PRD draft. Implementation must still wait for explicit CEO/Product approval.

1. **Sequencing:** Hold implementation approval until Pattern Discovery implementation is merged and its regression evidence is reviewed. Pattern PR https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/617 merged on 2026-05-06 with targeted Pattern tests, compatibility tests, Discovery term gate, typecheck, and final bug-check evidence recorded.
2. **Debate readiness:** Use a thin compatibility adapter for Debate in this slice. Do not do a deeper Debate readiness migration unless targeted tests prove it is safe and still within scope.
3. **Package validity gate:** Keep the first `ready` gate simple: package record/path presence plus the existing readiness check. Do not add stricter package shape validation in this PRD.
4. **Builder/Evolutionary scope:** Keep Builder and Evolutionary coverage to docs-only adapter guidance and follow-up notes. Do not implement Builder or Evolutionary readiness normalization in this PRD.
5. **Training boundary:** No Training import or writeback behavior changes are approved. Read-only compatibility tests may prove legacy access remains reachable, but Training behavior must stay unchanged.

## 13. CEO/Product approval note — 2026-05-06

Approved for implementation as the next Discovery Method Porting child PRD. Implementation branch should be `feat/cross-method-handoff-consistency` from `origin/main` after the assigned worktree is clean and refreshed.

Approval confirms the locked boundaries from section 12: thin Debate compatibility adapter, simple package-backed readiness gate, Builder/Evolutionary docs-only guidance, and no Training import/writeback behavior changes.

CEO approved at: 2026-05-06T13:06:30Z

## 14. Non-goal reminders for implementation agents

- Do not change Training import behavior.
- Do not change Training writeback behavior.
- Do not mark candidate previews, evidence, promoted items, ensembles, or local booleans as `ready` without a valid package.
- Do not implement System Builder or Evolutionary Strategy.
- Do not delete legacy routes or aliases.
- Do not change Strategy Configuration schema without a dedicated approved contract PRD.

## 15. Implementation completion

Completed by merged implementation PR: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/619

Completion evidence:

- PR merged at: 2026-05-06T14:26:07Z
- CI checks: Frontend and Backend passed on PR #619
- Verifier report: `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/session-1778072978488/verifier-report.md`
- Final verifier decision: `approved`
- Final bug-check status: `passed`
