# PRD: Discovery / Training Porting Completion Audit and Deferred Method Groundwork

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> GitHub issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/620
> Assigned agent/worktree: Evonome-discovery (`/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery`).
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Parent PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593
> Recent completed child PRDs: #602, #608, #611, #618
> Proposed branch after approval: `feat/discovery-method-porting-audit`
> Migration note: repo-local PRD files are not canonical for this workflow. Update this issue body instead of maintaining a separate PRD copy.

---

title: Discovery / Training Porting Completion Audit and Deferred Method Groundwork
slug: discovery-training-porting-completion-audit
created: 2026-05-06
status: done
prd_review_status: approved
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-06T17:23:29Z
github_issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/620
originating_worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
parent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/593
proposed_branch_after_approval: feat/discovery-method-porting-audit
---

## 1. Problem

Discovery Method Porting has now delivered the native Discovery shell/foundation, Signal Discovery, Pattern Discovery, and cross-method handoff consistency. The product is intentionally in a transitional state:

**Discovery currently shows:**

- Adversarial Debate
- Signal Discovery
- Pattern Discovery
- System Builder

Discovery does **not** currently show an Evolutionary Strategy menu item. Adding that Discovery menu entry, with the correct compatibility boundary to existing Training `Strategize`, is part of the work to scope in this PRD.

**Training currently shows:**

- Predict
- Discover
- Strategize
- Combine
- Size
- Allocate

The remaining risk is ambiguity about what still needs to move, what should stay in Training, and what should remain legacy-compatible while native Discovery surfaces mature. System Builder is not fully built as a native Discovery method yet. Evolutionary Strategy is different: the core workflow already exists substantially as Training `Strategize` and should be treated as an existing implementation that needs a Discovery-native port, not as an unbuilt greenfield feature. The product needs a clear completion audit and migration map before more section/menu work or method porting proceeds.

## 2. Product goal

Create an actionable Discovery/Training porting completion map that identifies remaining migration surfaces, locks the target ownership model, and defines groundwork-only expectations for deferred methods without implementing full System Builder or Evolutionary Strategy features.

This PRD should convert umbrella PRD #593 into the next executable planning slice by inspecting current code/config surfaces, documenting decisions, and producing follow-up issues for any implementation that should happen after the audit.

## 3. Current target model

### Discovery owns origin and handoff

Final Discovery methods are expected to include:

1. **Adversarial Debate** — native, implemented.
2. **Signal Discovery** — native, implemented.
3. **Pattern Discovery** — native, implemented.
4. **System Builder** — future native method; groundwork only in this PRD.
5. **Evolutionary Strategy** — existing legacy implementation currently surfaced as Training `Strategize`; this PRD should map the Discovery-native port and any safe groundwork, but must not rebuild the algorithm or remove Training compatibility.

Discovery owns method selection, creation workflows, candidate/evidence review, readiness state, and Strategy Configuration / Handoff Package display.

### Training owns import, evaluation, refinement, and writeback

Final Training workflows are expected to include:

1. **Predict** — remains Training-owned.
2. **Import / Imported Candidates** — future or existing Training import review surface for Discovery handoff packages.
3. **Backtest Evaluation** — evaluate imported Strategy Configuration / Handoff Packages.
4. **Optimization** — parameter/model/strategy optimization after import.
5. **Strategy / Model Training** — train/refine imported candidates.
6. **Hardening / Robustness** — stress, validation, and quality gates.
7. **Writeback** — preview/apply approved improvements back to source artifacts or handoff paths.

Training owns downstream decisions, evaluation, optimization, training, hardening, and writeback. Discovery must not take over Training import/writeback behavior.

## 4. In scope

- Audit current workflow/menu/config surfaces that still encode transitional Discovery/Training ownership.
- Inventory current entries for Discovery, Training, legacy `discover`, legacy `strategize`, System Builder, and Evolutionary Strategy.
- Explicitly map Training `Strategize` to target Discovery `Evolutionary Strategy`, including workflow identifiers, category values, create/detail/node builders, route/menu entries, and compatibility aliases.
- Define the Discovery menu addition for `Evolutionary Strategy`, because it is not currently present under Discovery.
- Confirm which current Training sections are temporary compatibility surfaces and which are target Training-owned workflows.
- Define what “groundwork only” means for System Builder and Evolutionary Strategy.
- Add or update lightweight repo-visible documentation for the migration map and ownership boundary.
- Add or update focused tests that lock current compatibility expectations where safe.
- Identify follow-up PRDs/tasks for:
  - System Builder native method implementation, if/when approved.
  - Evolutionary Strategy native Discovery port from existing Training `Strategize`, including any adapter-first slice if safe.
  - final menu/section cleanup after porting is complete.
  - Training import/evaluation/writeback follow-ons that are Training-owned.
- Keep legacy routes and Training-side method entries reachable during transition.

## 5. Out of scope

- Full System Builder native implementation.
- Rebuilding Evolutionary Strategy from scratch.
- Removing or breaking existing Training `Strategize` before a dedicated port PRD is approved and validated.
- Removing Training `Discover` or `Strategize` routes.
- Deleting legacy aliases or physical source folders.
- Training import/writeback behavior changes.
- Backend migrations or broad API rewrites.
- Strategy Configuration schema/version changes.
- Moving Predict into Discovery.
- Final top-level menu rearrangement unless it is documentation/test-only preparation.
- Creating automatic imports from Discovery into Training.

## 5.1 Strategize to Evolutionary Strategy mapping

The existing Training `Strategize` workflow should be treated as the implementation source for future Discovery `Evolutionary Strategy`. Current identifiers and surfaces to audit include:

- workflow type: `strategize`
- backend/category compatibility values: `strategy` and related strategy-run categories
- run mode: `evolutionary` where present
- likely frontend surfaces:
  - `frontend/src/features/training-lab/workflows/workflowMeta.ts`
  - `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/workflowRegistry.ts`
  - `frontend/src/features/training-lab/pages/Strategize*`
  - `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/workflows/strategy/**`
  - detail modals and node builders for strategy/evolutionary runs
  - experimental/prototype `strategize` routes and navigation

The target Discovery method name should be **Evolutionary Strategy** unless CEO/Product chooses a different user-facing name. Discovery does not currently include this menu item, so the port plan must define the new Discovery route/menu entry and how it maps to existing Training `Strategize`. The port should preserve Training `Strategize` compatibility until the Discovery-native method is validated and final menu cleanup is separately approved.

## 6. User stories

### US-001: Porting completion visibility

**Description:** As a product owner, I want to know which Discovery/Training migration pieces are complete, deferred, or still legacy-compatible so the remaining work can be sequenced safely.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The audit lists each current Discovery method and Training workflow.
- [ ] Each item is classified as target-owned, transitional legacy, deferred groundwork, or follow-up implementation.
- [ ] The audit identifies the source files/configs that currently define each item.
- [ ] The audit references parent PRD #593 and completed child PRDs #602, #608, #611, and #618.

### US-002: System Builder and Evolutionary Strategy boundaries

**Description:** As a future implementer, I want System Builder and Evolutionary Strategy clearly scoped so System Builder remains groundwork-only while Evolutionary Strategy is treated as a port of existing Training `Strategize` rather than a new feature build.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] System Builder is documented as a deferred native Discovery method with groundwork-only expectations.
- [ ] Evolutionary Strategy is documented as the target Discovery-native home for existing Training `Strategize`.
- [ ] The audit confirms Evolutionary Strategy is currently missing from the Discovery menu and specifies how/when it should be added.
- [ ] The audit maps `strategize`, `strategy`, and `evolutionary` identifiers to the proposed Discovery method boundary.
- [ ] Groundwork may include registry placeholders, readiness semantics, route/method inventory, adapter planning, and follow-up issue creation.
- [ ] Groundwork must not include new generation algorithms, persistence, backend endpoints, route deletion, or Training compatibility removal.

### US-003: Training ownership preserved

**Description:** As a Training user, I want Predict, import, evaluation, optimization, hardening, and writeback to remain Training-owned while Discovery migration continues.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Predict is explicitly marked Training-owned and not a Discovery method.
- [ ] Import/evaluation/optimization/hardening/writeback are documented as Training-owned.
- [ ] Existing Training-side `Discover` and `Strategize` entries remain reachable until replacement/removal is separately approved.
- [ ] No Training import or writeback behavior changes are included.

### US-004: Config and routing audit

**Description:** As an implementer, I want the relevant config files and route aliases identified before changing menus or moving code.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Audit covers `frontend/src/discovery/registry.ts`.
- [ ] Audit covers `frontend/src/discovery/compat.ts`.
- [ ] Audit covers `frontend/src/discovery/discoveryShellConfig.ts`.
- [ ] Audit covers `frontend/src/features/training-lab/trainingLabShellConfig.ts`.
- [ ] Audit covers `frontend/src/features/training-lab/workflows/workflowMeta.ts`.
- [ ] Audit covers `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/workflowRegistry.ts`.
- [ ] Audit covers experimental/prototype route/navigation configs where they still expose section ownership.

### US-005: Follow-up issue readiness

**Description:** As a planner, I want the audit to produce specific follow-up issues instead of leaving ambiguous “migration cleanup” work.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Follow-ups are created only for work that is out of this PRD’s implementation scope.
- [ ] Each follow-up has an owner/worktree, allowed paths, stop condition, and validation expectations.
- [ ] Follow-ups distinguish Discovery-owned work from Training-owned work.
- [ ] Any final menu cleanup follow-up preserves aliases until separately approved.

## 7. Functional requirements

- **FR-1:** Produce a repo-visible migration/ownership note or equivalent implementation artifact that maps current and target Discovery/Training ownership.
- **FR-2:** Preserve existing route and workflow compatibility during this PRD.
- **FR-3:** Identify all relevant frontend workflow/menu/config files involved in the current transition.
- **FR-4:** Keep System Builder at groundwork-only scope and define Evolutionary Strategy as a port of existing Training `Strategize` rather than a greenfield build.
- **FR-5:** Keep Training import/writeback behavior unchanged.
- **FR-6:** Produce follow-up issues for any full method implementation or menu cleanup.
- **FR-7:** Include validation evidence and verifier decisions in the task artifact folder.

## 8. Implementation boundaries

Expected allowed paths:

- `frontend/src/discovery/**`
- `frontend/src/features/training-lab/**` only for metadata/tests/documentation of compatibility and ownership
- `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/**` only for workflow registry audit/tests if needed
- `frontend/src/experimental/**` only for route/navigation audit/tests if needed
- `frontend/src/prototype/**` only for route/navigation audit/tests if needed
- `docs/**` or `dev-plans/agentops/**` for concise implementation artifacts and audit notes

Forbidden without separate approval:

- Training import/writeback behavior changes
- backend migrations
- Strategy Configuration schema changes
- new persistence
- full System Builder implementation
- full Evolutionary Strategy implementation
- route deletion
- physical folder renames
- deploy/config/secrets changes

## 9. Quality gates

Expected implementation gates:

- `pnpm --dir frontend typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir frontend check:discovery-terms`
- `git diff --check`
- Targeted tests for any touched route/navigation/workflow metadata files.
- Targeted compatibility tests proving legacy Training-side `Discover` and `Strategize` remain reachable if touched.
- Targeted tests proving Discovery method registry entries remain reachable if touched.

### Targeted validation suite

Run this suite, adding adjacent tests if new audit/config files are introduced:

- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/discovery/registry.contract.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/discovery/discoveryShellConfig.test.ts src/discovery/methodNavigation.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/features/training-lab/workflows/workflowMeta.discovery.test.ts src/features/training-lab/trainingLabShellConfig.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/experimental/navigation.section-navigation.test.ts src/experimental/layouts/TrainingLabLayout.section-navigation.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/prototype/routes.section-navigation.test.ts src/prototype/layouts/RootLayout.section-navigation.test.ts`
- If `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/workflowRegistry.ts` is touched, add or run a focused workflow registry test that proves `strategize` compatibility and target Discovery method mapping remain correct.

Recommended pre-PR gates:

- Local quality gate if available: `/gate --ml`
- Verifier final bug-check after all scoped implementation is complete.

## 10. Verifier checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Scope | Required verifier focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Current-state inventory and ownership map | Complete inventory, correct current/target ownership, no behavior changes |
| 2 | Groundwork boundaries and follow-up issues | System Builder not implemented, Evolutionary Strategy port from `Strategize` is mapped, follow-ups are specific and scoped |
| 3 | Compatibility tests/docs and final validation | Legacy reachability preserved, quality gates, final bug-check, no scope creep |

A final verifier bug-check is required by default after implementation completion.

## 11. Success metrics

- Product and implementation teams can see exactly which Discovery/Training sections are complete, transitional, or deferred.
- System Builder has clear groundwork boundaries and Evolutionary Strategy has a clear port map from existing Training `Strategize` without accidental rewrite or compatibility removal.
- Legacy Training-side `Discover` and `Strategize` remain reachable until final cleanup is separately approved.
- Follow-up issues are actionable and split by ownership.
- No Training import/writeback behavior changes occur.

## 12. CEO approval decisions

Approved at: `2026-05-06T17:23:29Z`

1. **Evolutionary Strategy visibility:** Add **Evolutionary Strategy** under Discovery as an active compatibility-backed entry using the existing Training `Strategize` route/workflow source, while preserving Training `Strategize` reachability.
2. **System Builder visibility:** Leave current System Builder behavior unchanged in this PRD and document only the deferred/groundwork boundary in the migration note.
3. **Legacy Training cleanup:** Training `Discover` and `Strategize` are not needed after their Discovery replacements are stable, but removal/hiding/alias-only behavior must be handled by a separate future cleanup PRD.
4. **Cleanup sequencing:** Final menu cleanup must wait until Evolutionary Strategy has a validated Discovery-native adapter and System Builder has at least an approved implementation PRD.
5. **Training import surface:** Define a Training-owned **Imported Candidates** follow-up before final cleanup so Discovery handoff packages have a clear downstream home.
6. **This PRD's success definition:** This PRD succeeds when it produces the audit, ownership map, compatibility tests/docs, and scoped follow-up issues. It does not complete the full Evolutionary Strategy port or full System Builder implementation.

## 13. Approval status

CEO/Product approved for implementation handoff. Implementation must remain within the scope boundaries, compatibility requirements, quality gates, and verifier checkpoints above.

# PRD: Strategy Complexity Profiles for Debate Seed Generation

## Status

Revised draft reference PRD. Not approved for implementation. Do not start work until CEO/Product explicitly approves and reprioritizes it.

This PRD has been revised to distinguish the proposed complexity profile from the existing **Idea Search Bias** control in Adversarial Debate.

## Owning metadata

- Proposed owning agent: Evonome-discovery
- Proposed worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery`
- GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
- Related Discovery tracker: #732
- Related active dependency/watch item: #681
- Target branch when approved: TBD

## Existing control: Idea Search Bias

Adversarial Debate already exposes an Idea Search Bias slider:

```text
Proven Patterns ←→ Novel Ideas
```

That control is functional and should remain. It influences seed novelty/search distance, seed-family selection, novelty/similarity metadata, and related generation context.

This PRD does **not** replace Idea Search Bias.

## Proposed new control: Strategy Complexity Profile

This PRD proposes a separate complexity axis:

```text
Simple / Balanced / Advanced
```

Complexity Profile controls the shape and interpretability of the generated strategy. It should guide component count, derived state, rule depth, search dimensions, and debate pressure against unnecessary complexity.

The two controls should be able to coexist:

| Idea Search Bias | Complexity Profile | Example outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Proven Patterns | Simple | Familiar pattern family with direct, readable rules. |
| Novel Ideas | Simple | Fresh thesis with few moving parts and minimal state. |
| Proven Patterns | Advanced | Known family with deeper execution and validation assumptions. |
| Novel Ideas | Advanced | Current adversarial hardening-style exploration. |

## Problem

Generated strategies can become intentionally complex during adversarial debate. That complexity is useful for hardening because it pressures validators, coupling checks, execution semantics, and debugger passes.

However, users may also want simple, understandable strategy rules while still benefiting from seed generation and adversarial debate. The system needs a user-selectable complexity profile that guides generation toward simple, balanced, or advanced strategies without weakening validation standards.

## Goals

1. Let users choose a Strategy Complexity Profile before seed generation.
2. Preserve the existing Idea Search Bias slider as the novelty/search-distance control.
3. Persist the selected complexity profile in job metadata and generated contract artifacts.
4. Keep validators equally strict across all complexity profiles.
5. Make simple outputs easier to understand, compare, and troubleshoot.
6. Let debate agents challenge complexity creep relative to the selected profile.
7. Preserve advanced adversarial generation for hardening and expert use.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace or remove Idea Search Bias.
- Do not weaken coupling, preflight, execution semantics, debugger, or promotion-readiness checks.
- Do not auto-advance Phase 2.
- Do not force all users into simple strategies.
- Do not replace existing advanced adversarial generation.
- Do not bundle broad corpus/reporting dashboards into the MVP.
- Do not block runtime/data-readiness work unless CEO/Product explicitly reprioritizes this PRD.

## User stories

### US1: User selects complexity independently from novelty

As a strategy-discovery user, I want to choose both novelty/search bias and complexity profile, so I can generate strategies that match my desired balance of originality and interpretability.

Acceptance criteria:

- Complexity profile is selectable before seed generation.
- Idea Search Bias remains available and keeps its current meaning.
- The UI distinguishes novelty from complexity in user-facing language.
- The selected complexity profile is persisted in job metadata.
- Generated contract artifacts record the selected complexity profile.

### US2: Simple profile keeps strategy rules intentionally small

As a user, I want Simple mode to produce strategies with fewer indicators and clearer rules, so I can understand and evaluate the output.

Acceptance criteria:

- Simple profile favors one primary thesis, a small component stack, limited derived state, direct entry/exit rules, and bounded parameter search.
- Simple profile uses soft caps with required justification when the generator exceeds them.
- If the thesis cannot be represented safely in a simple form, the output explains why instead of silently weakening validation.
- Debate agents challenge unnecessary added complexity.

### US3: Balanced profile allows moderate sophistication

As a user, I want Balanced mode to allow some derived state and richer validation assumptions, so I can explore strategies beyond simple rules without entering full advanced mode.

Acceptance criteria:

- Balanced profile permits moderate component stacks and limited derived state.
- Balanced profile avoids unnecessary component proliferation.
- The generated contract explains why each material component is required.
- Balanced is available as the recommended default unless CEO/Product chooses a different default.

### US4: Advanced profile preserves current adversarial pressure

As a hardening operator, I want Advanced mode to preserve complex adversarial strategy generation, so hardening continues to expose contract and validator weaknesses.

Acceptance criteria:

- Advanced profile can produce multi-component contracts, sparse state logic, and deeper execution/coupling surfaces.
- Advanced profile does not bypass KISS checks when a simpler equivalent rule would satisfy the thesis.
- Debug reports identify unnecessary complexity when present.
- UI copy makes clear that Advanced is best for hardening or expert use and may be harder to interpret.

### US5: Complexity metadata supports future hardening analysis

As a hardening operator, I want complexity profile metadata recorded now, so future corpus/reporting work can analyze blocker rates by complexity profile.

Acceptance criteria:

- Seed/job metadata includes selected complexity profile.
- Contract metadata includes selected and observed complexity fields.
- MVP stores enough metadata for later reporting without implementing full dashboards in this PRD.

## Proposed complexity profiles

### Simple

- One primary thesis.
- Small component stack.
- Minimal derived state.
- No unnecessary nested conditions.
- Simple hold/exit policy unless explicitly required.
- Minimal search dimensions.
- Strong preference for explainable indicators and direct rules.
- Exceeding soft caps requires an explicit justification in the generated artifact.

### Balanced

- One primary thesis with limited supporting state.
- Moderate component stack.
- Limited derived indicators or state machines.
- Bounded parameter search.
- Richer but still readable cost/fill validation.
- Recommended default unless CEO/Product chooses otherwise.

### Advanced

- Full adversarial generation allowed.
- Multi-component strategies and sparse state are permitted.
- More complex execution/fill/coupling assumptions are allowed when justified.
- Best suited for hardening and expert users.
- Still subject to KISS checks and strict validators.

## Complexity score inputs

Observed complexity should be computed from measurable inputs, including:

- component/indicator count,
- derived state count,
- rule dependency depth,
- number of entry conditions,
- number of exit/hold conditions,
- parameter/search dimensions,
- execution/fill assumption complexity,
- contract section length or rule expression length when useful.

The score should be advisory for generation and reporting. Validators remain strict and must not accept unsafe contracts because a profile is Simple.

## Soft-cap recommendation

Use soft caps with required justification rather than hard rejection for the MVP.

Rationale:

- Hard caps can block useful strategies that need one extra component.
- Soft caps let the system remain flexible while making complexity creep visible.
- Validators can still reject invalid or unsafe output independently of complexity.

## UI/API behavior

- Add a Strategy Complexity Profile selector near seed generation controls.
- Keep Idea Search Bias as a separate control.
- Default proposed value: Balanced.
- Advanced copy should warn that outputs may be harder to interpret and are best for hardening/expert review.
- Persist both controls distinctly:
  - `idea_search_bias` for novelty/search distance,
  - `strategy_complexity_profile` for complexity shape.

## Contract metadata

Generated artifacts should record:

- selected complexity profile,
- observed complexity score,
- complexity score inputs,
- any soft-cap violations,
- justification for any soft-cap violations,
- whether debate reduced, accepted, or escalated complexity.

## Suggested MVP implementation phases

### Phase 1: Schema and scoring

- Define `strategy_complexity_profile` values: `simple`, `balanced`, `advanced`.
- Define observed complexity score inputs.
- Add generated contract metadata fields for selected and observed complexity.
- Add tests for profile persistence and scoring.

Verifier checkpoint: schema/scoring review.

### Phase 2: Generation and debate guidance

- Add profile-aware seed-generation instructions.
- Add debate instructions that challenge unnecessary complexity creep.
- Add tests proving Simple prompts produce bounded simpler contracts unless justified.
- Add tests proving validators remain strict for every profile.

Verifier checkpoint: generation behavior review.

### Phase 3: UI/API exposure

- Expose complexity profile in the Debate seed-generation UI/API.
- Persist selection in job metadata and generated artifacts.
- Add concise user-facing copy for Simple, Balanced, and Advanced.
- Keep the existing Idea Search Bias slider unchanged.

Verifier checkpoint: end-to-end UX/API review and final bug-check.

## Follow-up scope, not MVP

Move the following into follow-up work unless CEO/Product explicitly expands scope:

- corpus seed backfill with inferred complexity metadata,
- blocker-rate dashboards by complexity profile,
- curriculum-style hardening run orchestration,
- cross-method complexity reporting,
- broad benchmark dashboards.

## Validation plan

- Unit tests for schema, persistence, and scoring.
- Contract-generation regression tests per complexity profile.
- Snapshot/evidence tests showing Simple mode avoids advanced-only components unless justified.
- Tests proving Idea Search Bias and Complexity Profile persist independently.
- End-to-end generation smoke for each profile.
- Adversarial debug pass verifying validators remain strict across all profiles.
- Browser QA confirming UI copy distinguishes novelty from complexity.

## CEO/Product review questions

1. Should the labels be Simple / Balanced / Advanced?
2. Should Balanced be the default?
3. Should Simple/Balanced use soft caps with required justification as proposed?
4. Should Advanced include a user-facing interpretability warning?
5. Is corpus/reporting support acceptable as follow-up scope rather than MVP?
6. Should this PRD remain parked until runtime/data-readiness surfaces are stable?

## Risks

- Users may confuse novelty and complexity if UI copy is not clear.
- Overly rigid Simple profile may prevent useful strategies.
- Soft constraints may fail to reduce complexity enough without good tests.
- Adding this before runtime/data-readiness is stable may distract from successful Discovery method runs.

## Recommendation

Keep this PRD parked until CEO/Product explicitly approves and prioritizes it. If approved, implement it as a distinct complexity axis next to the existing Idea Search Bias slider, with a narrow MVP focused on UI/API selection, metadata persistence, generation/debate guidance, and validation tests.

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Assigned agent: Evonome-trading agent.
> Worktree: TBD (no dedicated trading worktree yet — to be established when sequencing gate lifts).
> No historical repo snapshot — created post-migration (2026-05-06).

---

---
title: 10 Portfolio Management Agent Council
slug: 10-portfolio-management-agent-council
lifecycle: draft
ceo_approved: false
---

# PRD: Portfolio Management Agent Council

**Status:** Draft program PRD / scope guard
**Date:** 2026-05-06
**Type:** Program PRD
**Parent:** none — sibling to PRD: Strategy Configuration Contract (#576)

---

## 1. Overview

Today the platform can train and deploy individual strategies, but it has no live decision layer that treats a set of deployed strategies as one coordinated portfolio with explicit roles, cadence, and human-in-the-loop policy.

Prior planning produced a single-orchestrator design (archived `prd-nome-portfolio-orchestrator`, 2026-03-26). That design is comprehensive on scoring, sizing, exits, and self-review, but assumes one agent owns every decision, with one LLM "borderline reviewer" path and one daily self-review. It does not decompose the work into specialist roles, does not formalize a deliberation step, and does not address per-strategy optimization cadence as a first-class concern.

This PRD is the program parent for evolving that single-orchestrator model into an **agent council** of specialized roles that deliberate on a cadence and synthesise a portfolio-level action plan, plus a **Strategy Optimization Cell** per strategy that proposes parameter and money-management changes through the same approval boundary.

This program is a **planning and scope artifact**. Implementation is gated on substrate work in #575, #576, #577, #578 (see §10 Sequencing gate).

---

## 2. Why this matters now

The current GitHub project is correctly focused on the boundary between Strategy Discovery and Model Training (the configuration contract program) and on hardening the discovery substrate (Genesis, debate operational matrix, admin operations).

What is not yet represented on the board is the **layer above** that boundary — the layer that decides what to do with a group of trained, exportable strategies once they are ready to trade. If we let that layer be designed only when the substrate ships, two things will happen:

1. The Council will be forced to read whatever ad-hoc files happen to exist at that point, not the canonical contract.
2. The substrate PRDs (#577 evaluation, #578 knowledge ledger) will lock evidence shapes that may or may not match what the Council actually needs.

Writing this PRD now does **not** start implementation. It does:

- Capture the locked design decisions while they are fresh.
- Surface the open questions that need an explicit answer before child PRDs can be sharded out.
- Give #577 and #578 an explicit downstream consumer they can design against, so evidence shapes (rerun metrics, lineage, drift) are first-class instead of inferred.
- Give the Council a single home on the project board so future portfolio-related work has a parent issue to attach to, instead of accreting as scattered tasks.

---

## 3. Core product use case

A user has trained five strategies through the configuration-contract pipeline:

| # | Strategy type | Asset | Timeframe |
|---|---------------|-------|-----------|
| S1 | Mean reversion | BTC | 15m |
| S2 | Trend following | BTC | 1h |
| S3 | Trend following | ETH | 1h |
| S4 | Mean reversion | SOL | 5m |
| S5 | Breakout | ETH | 4h |

The user assembles them into one portfolio, presses **Play**, and the platform begins trading the five strategies as one coordinated book.

Behind that single button:

- A **per-signal executor** (the existing Nome orchestrator design, descoped to executor responsibilities) handles entries, sizing, and exits at signal time on deterministic logic.
- A **Portfolio Management Council** of specialist agents convenes on a cadence the user controls, deliberates on portfolio state, and produces a single ranked action plan with rationale.
- A **Strategy Optimization Cell** per strategy runs its own cadence and proposes parameter or money-management changes for that strategy.
- Both the Council's action plan and the Cells' proposals route through one **approval inbox**. In Auto mode they apply with a log entry. In Semi-auto mode the user approves them. Mode policy is configurable per action class.

The user never has to think about the fact that there are agents underneath. They press play, see one inbox, and either trust it (auto) or curate it (semi-auto).

---

## 4. Scope

### In scope

- Council architecture: roles, deliberation mechanism, output contract.
- Strategy Optimization Cell architecture: roles, cadence ownership, output contract.
- Cadence model: per-signal, daily, weekly, per-strategy, event-driven.
- Auto / Semi-auto policy at council and cell level (extends, does not replace, the existing per-signal mode).
- Approval inbox as the single human-in-the-loop surface.
- Memory boundary with the existing Nome LCM and portfolio decision journal.
- Read contract against the Knowledge Evidence Ledger (#578).
- Read contract against canonical strategy packages (#575/#576) and rerun metrics (#577).

### Out of scope for this program PRD

- Function signatures, schemas, or DB tables (these belong in child PRDs).
- New live-trading execution paths (covered by archived Nome PRD; this program reuses, does not replace).
- Cross-exchange margin management.
- Tax or accounting concerns.
- Replacing the per-signal executor's deterministic logic with LLM-time-of-signal decisions.

---

## 5. Locked product decisions

These decisions are carried forward from prior conversation and the archived Nome PRD. They are locked at the program level — child PRDs may not relitigate them.

### 5.1 The Council does not replace the executor

Per-signal entry, sizing, and exit decisions remain on the deterministic executor inherited from the archived Nome design. The Council operates at a slower cadence on portfolio-level questions: allocation, regime fit, drift, retirement, swap, and policy adjustment. The executor consumes Council output as constraints (weights, caps, mode), not as per-signal instructions.

**Why:** LLMs handle judgment, not math. Per-tick math should not depend on LLM availability.

### 5.2 Specialist roles, not one omnibus agent

The Council is a fixed set of named roles, each with one responsibility and a structured output contract. The roles for v1 are:

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| Allocator | Proposes target weights per strategy and per asset sleeve |
| Risk Officer | Veto / cap proposals on drawdown, correlation, exposure, regime risk |
| Regime Analyst | Calls the current regime and transition probability; flags type mismatches |
| Performance Auditor | Attribution, drift, alpha-vs-shadow, calibration of prior decisions |
| Strategy Doctor | Per-strategy diagnosis: pause, retrain, or retire candidates |
| Synthesiser (Chair) | Runs the deliberation, resolves conflicts, emits the final action plan |

**Why:** Bounded contracts are debuggable; one omnibus agent is not. Roles can be evaluated independently and improved without retraining one giant prompt.

### 5.3 Adversarial debate is reused as the synthesis mechanism

The Council's deliberation step uses the same adversarial-debate primitive that the contract program designates as producer #1 of the strategy configuration package (#576). One primitive, two roles: producing strategy configs (today) and producing portfolio decisions (later).

**Why:** Avoids inventing a parallel deliberation system. Hardening done for the discovery debate matrix benefits the Council automatically.

### 5.4 Auto / Semi-auto applies to council output, not just per-signal entries

The existing Aggressive / Conservative / Custom modes (archived Nome PRD §3.2) are extended: each *action class* the Council or a Cell can emit has its own mode policy.

| Action class | Default Auto-mode behaviour | Default Semi-auto behaviour |
|--------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Per-signal entry | Executor handles per existing rules | Executor handles per existing rules |
| Allocation rebalance | Apply, log, reversible | Queue in approval inbox |
| Strategy retire / pause | Queue regardless of mode | Queue in approval inbox |
| Optimization Cell parameter change | Apply if Validator passes | Queue in approval inbox |
| Optimization Cell MM change | Apply if Validator passes | Queue in approval inbox |
| Policy change (mode, thresholds) | Queue regardless of mode | Queue in approval inbox |

**Why:** Blast radius differs by action. A per-signal entry costs at most one trade; a strategy retirement removes a contributor for weeks. Modes must be per-action, not per-system.

### 5.5 Single approval inbox

All semi-auto proposals — Council action plans, Optimization Cell parameter changes, MM changes, policy changes — route through one inbox. The inbox is the only human-in-the-loop UI surface; there is no per-feature approval modal.

**Why:** N proposal types means N UI surfaces; users will lose track. One inbox forces the platform to design a uniform approval contract.

### 5.6 The Council reads the Knowledge Evidence Ledger but does not write to it

The Performance Auditor and Strategy Doctor are *read consumers* of the Knowledge Evidence Ledger (#578). Council decisions are persisted to a separate **Council Decision Journal** (extends the archived Nome decision journal pattern). The ledger is the system of record for evidence; the journal is the system of record for council deliberation.

**Why:** PRD #578 explicitly requires that the ledger be operator-trust-first and not driven by an autonomous recommender. Keeping read-only respects that gate.

### 5.7 The executor's per-signal LLM borderline path is preserved

The archived Nome PRD's "10–20% borderline path" (one LLM call at signal time on close-call signals) is preserved as-is. The Council does not run synchronously at signal time. The borderline reviewer becomes one role-bounded LLM call inside the executor, separate from the Council deliberation loop.

**Why:** Per-tick latency must remain milliseconds-to-seconds. Council deliberation is a multi-agent debate that can take minutes — incompatible with per-tick decisions.

### 5.8 Optimization Cells do not execute

A Cell emits proposals only. The same approval inbox and validator gate apply. A Cell never writes directly to live strategy parameters or money-management config.

**Why:** Keeps the safety boundary clean. One execution path, one audit trail.

---

## 6. Architecture sketch

### 6.1 Two cooperating teams

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                    │   Portfolio Mgmt Council     │
                    │  (deliberation, slow path)   │
                    │                              │
                    │  Allocator                   │
                    │  Risk Officer                │
                    │  Regime Analyst              │
                    │  Performance Auditor         │
                    │  Strategy Doctor             │
                    │  Synthesiser (Chair)         │
                    └──────────┬───────────────────┘
                               │ action plan
                               ▼
                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                    │      Approval Inbox          │
                    │   (auto / semi-auto)         │
                    └──────────┬───────────────────┘
                               │ approved actions
                               ▼
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │                Per-Signal Executor                    │
   │   (existing Nome orchestrator, descoped to exec)      │
   │   deterministic + per-tick borderline LLM             │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               ▲
                               │ proposals
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │      Strategy Optimization Cells (one per strategy)   │
   │   Diagnostician  Tuner  MM Adapter  Validator         │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 6.2 Cadence model

Cadence is a configurable trigger spec on each agent / cell, not a hard-coded schedule:

| Trigger | Owner | Default frequency |
|---------|-------|-------------------|
| Per-signal | Executor | Every signal |
| Portfolio review | Council | Daily |
| Deep review | Council | Weekly |
| Per-strategy review | Optimization Cell | Per-strategy override (e.g. 7 days, or N trades, or drift > X) |
| Event-driven | Council | Regime flip, drawdown breach, correlation spike |

### 6.3 Council deliberation loop (high level)

1. Trigger fires (cadence or event).
2. Each role independently produces its structured contribution against the current portfolio snapshot.
3. Synthesiser runs the adversarial-debate primitive to surface conflicts.
4. Synthesiser emits one ranked action plan with votes, rationale, and dissent.
5. Plan routes through approval inbox.
6. On apply, plan is persisted to the Council Decision Journal.

### 6.4 Optimization Cell loop (high level)

1. Cell trigger fires for strategy S.
2. Diagnostician summarises recent trade and drift evidence (read from #578 ledger).
3. Tuner proposes parameter ranges to re-search.
4. MM Adapter proposes risk and DD updates.
5. Validator runs the proposal through the existing rerun adapter (#577) on a recent OOS window.
6. If Validator passes, proposal routes through approval inbox.

### 6.5 Memory boundary

Three persistence stores, all distinct:

| Store | Owns | Pattern |
|-------|------|---------|
| Nome LCM (existing) | Conversation memory | SQLite, layered D0/D1/D2 |
| Council Decision Journal (new) | Council deliberations + outcomes | SQLite, extends archived Nome journal |
| Knowledge Evidence Ledger (#578) | Cross-system lineage and outcomes | Owned by #578, read-only to Council |

The Council reads from all three when deliberating; it writes only to the Council Decision Journal.

---

## 7. Open questions

These are the decisions that must be answered before child PRDs can be cut. They are not locked at this point — they are explicit holds. Each comes with a recommended default for discussion.

### Q1. Council scope: per-portfolio or site-wide?

A user with three portfolios — does each portfolio get its own Council instance, or does one site-wide Council manage all portfolios with portfolio scoping in its inputs?

- **Per-portfolio** isolates failures and mode choices but multiplies infra and prevents cross-portfolio learning.
- **Site-wide** allows learning across portfolios (e.g., "this regime hurt all three portfolios") but couples failure domains and complicates per-portfolio mode choices.

*Recommended default:* **per-portfolio** Council instance, with a thin site-wide layer that aggregates evidence for cross-portfolio insights but does not make decisions. Defer site-wide decision-making to v2.

### Q2. Optimization Cell memory: shared or sandboxed?

Does each Cell maintain its own memory of past proposals and outcomes for its strategy only (sandboxed), or does the Optimization Cell layer share a memory across strategies?

- **Sandboxed** is safer (one bad cell can't poison others) but loses cross-strategy patterns.
- **Shared** lets the platform learn "tightening stops in mean-reversion strategies during high vol generally helps" but has cross-contamination risk.

*Recommended default:* **sandboxed per strategy**, with read-only access to the Council Decision Journal for cross-strategy context. Defer shared optimization memory to v2.

### Q3. Debate transcript visibility

Does the user see the full Council debate transcript by default, only the synthesised action plan, or both behind a toggle?

- **Full** builds trust early, but is noisy and can teach users to micromanage agents.
- **Synthesised only** is clean but feels opaque — "what did Risk Officer say?"

*Recommended default:* **synthesised plan with role votes inline**, full transcript behind an expandable detail panel. Same pattern as the existing adversarial debate UI surfaces.

### Q4. Conflict between Council plan and live signals mid-cycle

The Council emits a plan saying "reduce S2 weight by 30%". One hour later S2 fires a strong LONG signal. Does the executor:

- **Honour the council**: refuse the entry until next council cycle.
- **Honour the executor**: take the entry at the new reduced weight.
- **Hybrid**: take the entry only if its edge score exceeds a higher threshold than usual.

*Recommended default:* **hybrid**. Council weights act as caps and as a sizing multiplier, not as a binary block. A high-conviction signal can still fire, sized smaller.

### Q5. Auto-mode unlock threshold

Auto mode for the executor (per-signal) and Auto mode for the Council (allocation changes) have very different blast radii. Should they share one switch, or unlock independently?

*Recommended default:* **independent unlock** — per-action-class as in §5.4. The user can run executor-auto + council-semi-auto, or the inverse. One global switch over-simplifies and forces the wrong tradeoff.

### Q6. Memory boundary with Nome LCM

Does the Council deliberation feed back into the Nome conversation memory (LCM), so when the user asks Nome "what did the council decide today?" Nome answers from one merged memory? Or are they kept strictly separate with Nome's context-builder merging at query time?

*Recommended default:* **strictly separate stores, merge at query time** — same pattern the archived Nome PRD chose for portfolio memory vs LCM. Cleaner separation of concerns, no write coupling.

### Q7. Approval inbox owner

Is the approval inbox a feature of the existing Nome chat surface (one place to talk to / approve), a feature of the Operations dashboard, or its own surface?

*Recommended default:* **Operations dashboard panel** with a Nome-chat shortcut that links into it. The approval inbox is operational, not conversational, and benefits from a fixed UI surface.

### Q8. Optimization Cell PRD: one or many?

Does v1 ship as one PRD covering all four Cell roles (Diagnostician / Tuner / MM Adapter / Validator), or split into two PRDs (parameter optimization vs money-management adaptation)?

*Recommended default:* **one PRD** for v1. The four roles share a cadence and a validator; splitting them adds coordination overhead with no isolation benefit. Split in v2 if the cell grows.

### Q9. Council failure modes

If one role times out or returns an unparseable response, does the Synthesiser proceed without it, fail the cycle, or retry with a fallback prompt?

*Recommended default:* **proceed without it, log the gap, and never enter Auto-apply for a plan with a missing role**. Risk Officer and Validator are exceptions — if either is missing, the cycle hard-fails.

### Q10. v1 strategy count and timeframe support

Does v1 support arbitrary strategy counts and any combination of timeframes (5m + 15m + 1h + 4h + 1d)? Or do we constrain v1 to a single dominant timeframe family?

*Recommended default:* **v1 supports up to 10 strategies and any timeframe mix the contract supports**. The Council is timeframe-agnostic; cadence is per-trigger, not per-timeframe.

---

## 8. Non-goals for this program

This program does not:

- Replace the per-signal executor's deterministic logic with LLM-time-of-signal decisions.
- Introduce a new live-trading execution path beyond what the archived Nome PRD specifies.
- Solve cross-exchange margin or accounting.
- Drive the Knowledge Evidence Ledger's content or schema (that is owned by #578).
- Replace the Strategy Refinement Pipeline's manual "Iterate" flow — Optimization Cells are recurring counterparts, not replacements.
- Define UI styling or component library choices.

---

## 9. Dependencies

| PRD | Why |
|-----|-----|
| #575 Strategy Configuration Contract Program Overview | Canonical strategy package the Council reasons over |
| #576 Strategy Configuration Contract | Parent contract program; Council operates on contract output |
| #577 Backtest Evaluation Interoperability | Rerun metrics consumed by Performance Auditor and Optimization Cell Validator |
| #578 Cross-System Knowledge Base Learning | Knowledge Evidence Ledger as Council read substrate |
| Archived `prd-nome-portfolio-orchestrator` (2026-03-26) | Historical context; specifies the per-signal executor that this Council sits above |
| Adversarial debate operational matrix (#563) | Synthesis primitive reused as Council deliberation mechanism |

---

## 10. Sequencing gate

Implementation on this program **must not begin** until:

1. #577 Backtest Evaluation Interoperability first slice is implemented, merged, and stable.
2. #578 Cross-System Knowledge Base Learning Knowledge Evidence Ledger first slice is approved.
3. Open questions §7 Q1–Q10 are resolved and lifted into §5 Locked product decisions.

The Council cannot deliberate trustworthily on evidence that is itself untrusted. Building the Council before the substrate is stable would force it to read whatever ad-hoc files exist at that point — exactly the drift the contract program is fixing.

This PRD may be **shaped, reviewed, and used to influence #577 / #578 evidence shapes** before the gate lifts. That is the purpose of writing it now.

---

## 11. Document map

When the gate lifts and the open questions are locked, this program will be sharded into the following child PRDs. None of these are written yet.

| Order | Working title | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 10A | Council role contracts and deliberation mechanism | Locks the structured output contract for each role and the Synthesiser primitive |
| 10B | Cadence and trigger specification | Configurable trigger spec, event-driven path, default frequencies |
| 10C | Approval inbox and mode policy | Per-action-class mode policy, inbox UX, audit trail |
| 10D | Council Decision Journal | Persistence layer; extends archived Nome decision journal |
| 10E | Strategy Optimization Cell | Cell roles, cadence, validator gate, write-back to contract (gated on #576 write-back) |
| 10F | Per-portfolio vs site-wide layer | Resolves Q1; thin aggregation layer if recommended default holds |

---

## 12. Naming and product copy

Per project naming policy:

- All internal source code, components, services, and types use institutional names: `Council`, `Cell`, `Allocator`, `RiskOfficer`, `RegimeAnalyst`, `PerformanceAuditor`, `StrategyDoctor`, `Synthesiser`.
- No evolutionary or metaphor-heavy terms in code surfaces.
- Display copy may use product-aligned names where clarity benefits the user (e.g., "Portfolio Council" in the dashboard header).
- Diagnostic and internal-state copy stays terse and operator-facing — see CLAUDE.md product-UI-copy rules.

---

## 13. Reference: archived prior art

Local archive (pre-GitHub-only-PRD migration), kept for historical context only:

- `tasks/prd/_archive/2026-03-26/prd-nome-portfolio-orchestrator_done.md`
- `tasks/prd/_archive/2026-03-26/nome-orchestrator-phases/phase-1-scoring-and-decision-framework.md`
- `tasks/prd/_archive/2026-03-26/nome-orchestrator-phases/phase-2-nome-integration-and-memory.md`
- `tasks/prd/_archive/2026-03-26/nome-orchestrator-phases/phase-3-portfolio-dashboard.md`
- `tasks/prd/_archive/2026-03-26/nome-orchestrator-phases/phase-4-advanced-reallocation-and-self-review.md`

These specify the per-signal executor, scoring rubric, paper-to-live promotion, and shadow tracking that this program reuses without re-specifying.

# PRD: Discovery Evolutionary Strategy Adapter from Training Strategize

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> GitHub issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/625
> Assigned agent/worktree: Evonome-discovery (`/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery`).
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Parent PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/620
> Proposed branch after approval: `feat/discovery-evolutionary-strategy-adapter`

---

title: Discovery Evolutionary Strategy Adapter from Training Strategize
slug: discovery-evolutionary-strategy-adapter
created: 2026-05-06
status: done
prd_review_status: approved
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-06T18:20:27Z
github_issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/625
originating_worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
parent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/620
proposed_branch_after_approval: feat/discovery-evolutionary-strategy-adapter
---

## 1. Problem

Discovery needs an **Evolutionary Strategy** entry that uses the existing Training `Strategize` workflow as its implementation source. The product goal is not to rebuild strategy generation, but to expose a Discovery-native entry point while preserving Training `Strategize` reachability during the transition.

Parent PRD #620 completed the porting audit and confirmed this should run before final menu cleanup.

## 2. Product goal

Add a Discovery-native **Evolutionary Strategy** entry through an adapter-first slice backed by the existing Training `Strategize` implementation, with compatibility tests proving both the new Discovery entry and legacy Training entry remain reachable.

## 3. CEO decisions

Approved at: `2026-05-06T18:20:27Z`

1. Promote this follow-up into the canonical approved PRD in-place.
2. Add **Evolutionary Strategy** as an active Discovery entry backed by existing Training `Strategize`.
3. Preserve Training `Strategize` reachability until a separate final cleanup PRD is approved.
4. Keep scope to adapter/navigation/compatibility work only.
5. Use minimal user-facing copy if needed; avoid primary UI text that narrates implementation plumbing.

## 4. In scope

- Add or wire the Discovery **Evolutionary Strategy** entry.
- Route or adapt the Discovery entry to the existing Training `Strategize` implementation source.
- Preserve Training `Strategize` route/workflow reachability.
- Add or update compatibility tests for Discovery entry reachability and Training `Strategize` reachability.
- Add focused registry/navigation tests where touched.
- Record implementation evidence under approved docs/artifact paths.

## 5. Out of scope

- Rebuilding the strategy generation algorithm.
- Removing Training `Strategize`.
- Deleting legacy aliases or routes.
- Training import/writeback behavior changes.
- Backend migrations.
- Strategy Configuration schema changes.
- New persistence.
- Deploy/config/secrets changes.
- Final menu cleanup.
- System Builder implementation.

## 6. Allowed paths

- `frontend/src/discovery/**`
- `frontend/src/features/training-lab/**` only for metadata/tests proving compatibility
- `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/**` only for strategy workflow adapter or registry compatibility tests approved by this PRD
- `frontend/src/prototype/**` only for Discovery and Training route/navigation coverage
- `frontend/src/experimental/**` only for route/navigation compatibility tests if needed
- `docs/**` and `dev-plans/agentops/**` for implementation evidence

## 7. User stories

### US-001: Discovery entry reachability

As a Discovery user, I can select **Evolutionary Strategy** from Discovery and reach the existing strategy workflow without needing to know it originated in Training.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Discovery exposes an **Evolutionary Strategy** entry.
- [ ] The entry uses the existing Training `Strategize` implementation source.
- [ ] Any user-facing copy is concise and product-facing.
- [ ] No new strategy generation behavior is introduced.

### US-002: Training compatibility preserved

As a Training user, I can still reach `Strategize` during the transition.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Training `Strategize` remains reachable.
- [ ] Legacy route and workflow aliases are not deleted.
- [ ] No Training import or writeback behavior changes are made.

### US-003: Compatibility locked by tests

As a maintainer, I have tests proving Discovery and Training routes remain compatible.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Discovery registry/shell/navigation tests cover the new entry.
- [ ] Training workflow metadata/shell tests continue to cover `Strategize` reachability.
- [ ] If `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/workflowRegistry.ts` is touched, a focused registry test proves `strategize` compatibility.

## 8. Functional requirements

- **FR-1:** Discovery must expose **Evolutionary Strategy** as an active compatibility-backed entry.
- **FR-2:** The Discovery entry must reuse or adapt existing Training `Strategize` surfaces rather than introduce a parallel algorithm.
- **FR-3:** Training `Strategize` must remain reachable.
- **FR-4:** Legacy aliases/routes must remain intact.
- **FR-5:** The implementation must not change Training import/writeback behavior.
- **FR-6:** Tests must prove both Discovery entry reachability and Training compatibility.

## 9. Stop condition

Discovery exposes an **Evolutionary Strategy** entry backed by the existing Training `Strategize` implementation, with compatibility tests proving both Discovery entry reachability and Training `Strategize` reachability.

## 10. Validation expectations

Required gates:

- `pnpm --dir frontend typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir frontend check:discovery-terms`
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/discovery/registry.contract.test.ts src/discovery/discoveryShellConfig.test.ts src/discovery/methodNavigation.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run src/features/training-lab/workflows/workflowMeta.discovery.test.ts src/features/training-lab/trainingLabShellConfig.test.ts`
- Focused workflow registry test if `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/workflowRegistry.ts` is touched
- `git diff --check`

Recommended pre-PR gates:

- Local quality gate if available: `/gate --ml`
- Verifier final bug-check after all scoped implementation is complete.

## 11. Verifier checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Scope | Required verifier focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Adapter/navigation plan and touched-file inventory | Confirms reuse of existing Training `Strategize`, no algorithm rewrite, allowed paths only |
| 2 | Discovery entry and Training compatibility | Confirms Discovery reachability and Training `Strategize` reachability remain intact |
| 3 | Final tests and bug-check | Confirms validation evidence, no scope creep, no final cleanup slipped in |

A final verifier bug-check is required after scoped implementation is complete.

## 12. Dependency and sequencing

- Parent audit PRD #620 is complete.
- This PRD should run before final menu cleanup.
- Final cleanup must remain a separate future PRD after this adapter is validated.

## 13. Approval status

CEO/Product approved for implementation handoff. Implementation must remain within this PRD's scope boundaries, compatibility requirements, quality gates, and verifier checkpoints.

# PRD: Training Imported Candidates Downstream Surface

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> GitHub issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/627
> Parent PRD: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/620
> Assigned agent/worktree: Evonome-training (`/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-training`)
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Base branch: `main`
> Working branch: `feat/training-imported-candidates-627`
> Status: Done
> Approval model: Phase 2 frontend-only path approved after the Phase 1 verifier/CEO checkpoint; implementation remains limited to fail-closed read-only/empty UI with no real candidate list.

---

title: Training Imported Candidates Downstream Surface
slug: training-imported-candidates-downstream-surface
created: 2026-05-31
updated: 2026-06-01
status: done
prd_review_status: approved
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-31T21:50:54Z
approval_scope: phase_2_frontend_only_fail_closed
github_issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/627
parent_prd: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/620
originating_worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-training
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
base_branch: main
working_branch: feat/training-imported-candidates-627
---

## 1. Problem

Parent PRD #620 established that Discovery owns candidate origin and handoff, while Training owns import review, evaluation, refinement, hardening, and writeback. The remaining product gap is a Training-owned downstream home where Discovery handoff packages can be reviewed before a human starts manual Training setup.

The codebase now has a generic Training Imports area, but it is not yet shaped as the approved Imported Candidates product surface. Without this PRD, final Discovery/Training menu cleanup can make the ownership model look complete while users still lack a clear place to answer: "Is this Discovery candidate ready for Training, and what should I do next?"

## 2. Product goal

Define and, only after an explicit readiness checkpoint, implement a Training-owned Imported Candidates surface that lets users review Discovery handoff packages and decide whether each package is ready for manual Training setup.

The surface must preserve the Discovery/Training boundary: Discovery produces and explains candidates; Training reviews downstream readiness and owns the decision to continue into Training workflows.

## 3. CEO shaping decisions

- Promote #627 from future follow-up to PRD candidate.
- Use a two-step PRD model:
  1. approve the product/UX/data-source plan first;
  2. allow implementation only after a verifier/CEO checkpoint confirms scope, data source, CTA policy, and ownership boundaries.
- First surface behavior: review Discovery handoff packages and decide whether they are ready for manual Training setup.
- The default v1 posture is **review-and-decide**, not create-and-run.
- All boundary risks are explicit approval gates:
  - no automatic Discovery-to-Training imports;
  - no Discovery method implementation changes;
  - no backend migrations;
  - no new backend endpoints or persistence models;
  - no Strategy Configuration schema changes;
  - no writeback behavior changes;
  - no route deletion or final menu cleanup.

## 4. Current-state notes

- Training has a generic Imports stage at `/training/imports` and `/training-lab/imports`.
- Legacy Training `discover` routes currently point users toward Training Imports.
- Existing frontend services already include import and lineage concepts such as configuration import previews, experiment import summaries, available imports, and artifact lineage.
- This PRD must not assume those existing services can safely enumerate Discovery handoff packages until Phase 1 confirms the source of truth and missing-state behavior.

## 5. Target experience

A Training user should be able to open Imported Candidates and see:

1. candidate source context from Discovery;
2. handoff/package readiness state;
3. missing or unsupported requirements;
4. provider/data capability context when available;
5. blocker ownership: Discovery source issue, Training setup issue, provider/data capability issue, or operator action;
6. a clear recommendation: ready for manual Training setup, incomplete, blocked, unsupported, stale, or already connected to a Training artifact;
7. next-step copy that explains the user action without creating automatic imports or writeback.

If a candidate is ready, the UI may guide the user toward an approved manual Training setup path. It must not silently create experiments, imports, evaluations, writebacks, backend records, or Discovery changes.

## 6. Provider-neutral requirements

- Imported Candidates must not hardcode one exchange, symbol format, session model, market type, data vendor, or asset class as the product boundary.
- Provider-specific examples may appear in fixtures or test data only.
- Readiness must use provider/datafeed capability metadata when available.
- If required provider, market, capability, lineage, or contract metadata is missing or unsupported, the candidate must fail closed into a blocked, incomplete, or unsupported state rather than being shown as setup-ready.
- Provider-specific behavior belongs in adapters, validation profiles, fixtures, or existing backend contracts, not in shared Training UI assumptions.

## 7. Scope

### Phase 1: Imported Candidates UX/data-source plan

Phase 1 is the only slice eligible for initial approval. It is planning-only unless the CEO explicitly approves otherwise.

The Phase 1 deliverable must be recorded back on #627 as a reviewable plan comment or linked artifact. It must include:

- route/menu placement and whether the user-facing label is `Imported Candidates` or existing `Imports` with updated copy;
- relationship to the existing `/training/imports` and `/training-lab/imports` routes;
- candidate card/list/detail information architecture;
- source-of-truth decision for candidate/package data;
- fail-closed data-source behavior;
- readiness states and setup-readiness rules;
- empty, unavailable, blocked, incomplete, unsupported, stale, ready, and already-connected states;
- blocker ownership taxonomy and user-facing blocker copy;
- CTA policy for every state;
- copy that explains manual next steps without implying automatic import behavior;
- existing frontend services that can be reused without backend/schema changes;
- Phase 2 implementation acceptance criteria and validation commands.

Phase 1 allowed paths and artifacts:

- GitHub issue #627 body and comments;
- `dev-plans/agentops/**` only for planning or verifier evidence if an artifact folder is needed;
- `docs/**` only for concise linked planning evidence if explicitly useful.

Phase 1 must not modify frontend source, backend source, route config, schemas, migrations, or runtime behavior.

### Phase 2: Conditional implementation slice

Allowed only after the Phase 1 verifier/CEO checkpoint approves the UX/data-source plan:

- Update Training-owned frontend surfaces for Imported Candidates.
- Reuse existing Training Imports route/menu structures where practical.
- Add candidate readiness and manual-review UI states approved in Phase 1.
- Add targeted tests for touched Training shell, route, workflow, and state logic.
- Record validation evidence in the approved agentops artifact location.

Phase 2 must stop at a read-only empty/planning state and spawn a separate backend/data-contract PRD if existing endpoints cannot safely enumerate Discovery handoff packages. It must not fabricate candidate availability in shared UI logic.

## 8. In scope after Phase 2 approval

Expected allowed paths after the implementation-readiness checkpoint:

- `frontend/src/features/training-lab/**`
- `frontend/src/pages/training-hub/**`
- `frontend/src/services/experimentsApi.ts` only for frontend types or client helpers around existing endpoints
- `frontend/src/prototype/**` only for Training route/navigation coverage
- `frontend/src/experimental/**` only for Training route/navigation coverage if approved
- `docs/**` and `dev-plans/agentops/**` for concise implementation evidence

## 9. Out of scope without a separate approved PRD

- Discovery method implementation changes.
- Backend migrations.
- New backend endpoints or persistence models.
- Strategy Configuration schema or contract-version changes.
- Automatic imports from Discovery into Training.
- Silent experiment creation from Discovery candidates.
- Evaluation, optimization, hardening, or writeback behavior changes.
- Route deletion.
- Final Discovery/Training menu cleanup.
- Deploy, config, or secrets changes.
- Mocked or fabricated production candidate availability.

## 10. CTA policy

V1 is review-and-decide. CTAs must follow these rules:

- Ready candidates may show an approved manual next step only.
- Incomplete, blocked, unsupported, or stale candidates must not show setup-ready CTAs.
- Already-connected candidates may link to existing Training context without mutating source records.
- Any action that creates an import, experiment, evaluation, writeback, backend record, or Discovery update requires explicit Phase 2 approval and must remain user-triggered.
- If Phase 2 does not approve a mutating CTA, the UI must stay read-only.

## 11. Blocker ownership taxonomy

Candidate blockers must identify the next owner:

| Owner | Use when | User-facing consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery source | Handoff package, source readiness, method evidence, or source artifact is missing or stale | Return to Discovery or source issue before Training setup |
| Training setup | Training needs user decisions, experiment context, or manual setup input | Complete Training setup before evaluation or training |
| Provider/data capability | Provider, market, timeframe, data quality, or capability metadata is missing or unsupported | Candidate is not setup-ready for this provider/data context |
| Operator action | Environment, permissions, unavailable service, or unresolved operational issue blocks review | Operator must resolve before the candidate can be reviewed |

## 12. User stories

### US-001: Candidate review home

As a Training user, I want a clear Imported Candidates destination so I can review Discovery handoff packages before deciding whether they are ready for Training setup.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Phase 1 identifies the route and menu placement for Imported Candidates.
- [ ] The surface is Training-owned and does not move Discovery responsibilities into Training.
- [ ] Candidate source context includes the Discovery source when available.
- [ ] Empty and unavailable states explain what the user can do next.

### US-002: Readiness and blockers

As a Training user, I want each candidate to show readiness and blockers so I do not start setup from an incomplete or unsupported package.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Readiness states include ready, incomplete, blocked, unsupported, stale, and already-connected where applicable.
- [ ] Missing required fields or capabilities fail closed.
- [ ] Blocker copy names the missing requirement and owner.
- [ ] Unsupported provider/capability states do not present ready-for-setup CTAs.

### US-003: Manual setup boundary

As a product owner, I want Imported Candidates to support manual setup decisions without creating automatic imports or writeback behavior.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] No user path silently creates an import, experiment, evaluation, or writeback.
- [ ] Any CTA that uses existing import APIs requires explicit user action and must be approved in the Phase 2 checkpoint.
- [ ] Discovery artifacts remain source-owned by Discovery.
- [ ] Training readiness decisions are displayed as downstream review, not source mutation.

### US-004: Existing Training compatibility

As an existing Training user, I want current Training Imports, Discover redirect, and legacy route behavior to remain reachable until final cleanup is separately approved.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `/training/imports` and `/training-lab/imports` remain reachable if touched.
- [ ] Legacy `discover` compatibility remains intact if touched.
- [ ] No route deletion or final menu cleanup is included.
- [ ] Final menu cleanup #626 remains dependent on this PRD reaching at least an approved Phase 1 plan state.

### US-005: Provider-neutral readiness

As a multi-provider Training user, I want Imported Candidates to handle provider and market capability gaps safely instead of assuming one exchange or asset class.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Readiness rules do not hardcode a single provider, symbol format, asset class, or session model.
- [ ] Missing provider/capability metadata blocks setup readiness.
- [ ] Tests or fixtures cover at least one ready case and one missing/unsupported capability case if Phase 2 touches UI logic.

### US-006: Fail-closed data source

As a product owner, I want the plan to stop safely if candidate enumeration is not supported by existing contracts.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Phase 1 identifies whether existing endpoints can safely enumerate Discovery handoff packages.
- [ ] If not, Phase 2 is limited to a read-only empty/planning state.
- [ ] A separate backend/data-contract PRD is created or recommended before any real candidate list is implemented.
- [ ] Shared UI does not fabricate production candidate availability.

## 13. Functional requirements

- **FR-1:** Define Imported Candidates as a Training-owned surface connected to Discovery handoff package review.
- **FR-2:** Preserve existing Training Imports and legacy route compatibility during this PRD.
- **FR-3:** Define source-of-truth and missing-data behavior before implementation.
- **FR-4:** Display candidate readiness states and blocker reasons in user-facing language.
- **FR-5:** Fail closed when required package, provider, capability, lineage, or contract metadata is missing.
- **FR-6:** Avoid automatic imports, automatic experiment creation, backend migrations, schema changes, and writeback behavior changes.
- **FR-7:** Keep implementation provider-neutral and adapter-friendly.
- **FR-8:** Produce verifier-ready evidence for Phase 1 and Phase 2 decisions.
- **FR-9:** Keep Phase 1 planning-only unless separately approved.
- **FR-10:** Keep mutating CTAs out of v1 unless explicitly approved at the implementation-readiness checkpoint.

## 14. Quality gates

Expected validation after any implementation slice:

- `pnpm --dir frontend typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir frontend check:discovery-terms`
- Targeted Training Lab shell, route, and page tests for touched files.
- Targeted Training Imports or workflow tests for readiness-state logic.
- Targeted prototype or experimental route/navigation tests if those route families are touched.
- `git diff --check`

Recommended final gate:

- Verifier final bug-check after all scoped implementation is complete.

## 15. Verifier checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Scope | Required verifier focus | Gate outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Phase 1 UX/data-source plan | Imported Candidates ownership, route/menu proposal, candidate states, provider-neutral fail-closed behavior, blocker ownership, CTA policy, and manual setup boundary | CEO may approve, revise, or block Phase 1 plan |
| 2 | Implementation readiness | Existing data source confirmed, allowed paths confirmed, no backend/schema/writeback/import automation, no fabricated candidate availability, tests identified | CEO/verifier approval required before coding |
| 3 | Final implementation verification | UI behavior, route compatibility, validation evidence, copy-compression pass, no scope creep, final bug-check | Ready for implementation completion handoff |

## 16. Dependencies and sequencing

- Depends on #620 for the Discovery/Training ownership model.
- #626 final Discovery/Training menu cleanup should wait for this PRD to reach at least an approved Phase 1 plan state.
- Phase 2 may require a separate backend/data-contract PRD if candidate enumeration is not safely supported by existing endpoints.
- Must not block unrelated Discovery method implementation unless final menu cleanup depends on the downstream Training home.

## 17. Success metrics

- Product can point to a Training-owned destination for Discovery handoff package review.
- Users understand whether a candidate is ready, blocked, incomplete, unsupported, stale, or already connected.
- Each blocker identifies the next responsible owner.
- Discovery ownership, Training ownership, and manual setup boundaries are clear.
- Final menu cleanup has a concrete downstream dependency rather than an ambiguous follow-up.
- No automatic import, backend migration, schema, writeback, fabricated candidate availability, or route-deletion scope creep occurs.

## 18. Approval status

CEO/Product approved Phase 1 UX/data-source planning at `2026-05-31T21:50:54Z`.

Human approved the Phase 2 frontend-only implementation path at `2026-05-31T22:23:16Z`.

Approval scope:

- Approved: implement `/training/imports` and `/training-lab/imports` as `Imported Candidates` with fail-closed read-only/empty states.
- Approved: frontend-only route/menu/page copy and targeted tests needed for the approved state.
- Not approved: real candidate lists, automatic imports, project-based package regeneration, package-directory preview, mutating CTAs, backend/data contracts, schemas, migrations, writeback, route deletion, deployment changes, or final menu cleanup.
- Required after implementation: verifier Checkpoint 3 final implementation verification and default bug-check where applicable.

Phase 2 must not fabricate candidate availability. If a real candidate source is needed, create a separate backend/data-contract PRD first.



## 19. Completion evidence

Final implementation verification completed at `2026-06-01T08:52:23Z`.

Evidence:

- Verifier report: `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/session-1780264432740/verifier-report.md`
- Browser QA report: `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/session-1780264432740/browser-qa/browser-qa-report.md`
- Preview: `https://training-preview.evonome.com/app/training/imports`

Completion scope:

- Implemented `/training/imports` and `/training-lab/imports` as `Imported Candidates` with fail-closed read-only/empty states.
- Preserved existing route compatibility.
- Added no real candidate list, backend/data contract, import automation, experiment creation, schema change, migration, writeback, route deletion, or final menu cleanup.
