# PRD: Hyperliquid Data Feed Degraded Status Diagnosis and Recovery

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
> Preview surface: https://preview.evonome.com/app/admin/data-feeds

---

```yaml
github_issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/645
status: done
created: 2026-05-07
area: datafeed
assigned_agent: Evonome-data
worktree_path: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-07
```

## CEO approval

Approved on 2026-05-07. No further product-shaping changes required before implementation handoff.

## CEO shaping decisions

Updated from CEO review on 2026-05-07:

1. **Urgency:** Treat this as high-priority datafeed reliability work. It does not require a broad production freeze, but Hyperliquid is core enough that a degraded adapter undermines trust in data readiness.
2. **Definition of fixed:** Every enabled/configured Hyperliquid live pair must work, not only BTC/ETH/SOL. The adapter must not show green if enabled pairs are silently stale, invalid, or receiving empty books with no usable live data.
3. **Upcoming pair expansion:** We expect to add many more Hyperliquid pairs soon because all-pair historical data has been downloaded separately. Later work will integrate those histories into the database, connect them to the data feed, backfill gaps, and keep them current. This PRD must make health checks and diagnostics pair-aware so that future expansion is safe, while leaving the broader catalog/database integration to the relevant follow-up work.
4. **Default behavior:** A smaller safe default live set is acceptable only when broader pairs are not enabled. Any pair listed as enabled for live collection must either stream correctly or be explicitly disabled/marked non-live with an operator-visible reason.
5. **UI expectation:** Lightweight operator diagnostics are required. If the admin page shows `Degraded`, it must explain the reason concisely. Logs alone are not enough.
6. **Approval scope:** If the root fix is simple, still ship the durable minimum: reason code, last activity/per-pair health, safe enabled-pair semantics, and regression tests. Do not expand into a large observability rebuild unless diagnosis proves it necessary.

## 1. Problem

On the Admin Data Feeds page, Binance and Kraken show as connected/healthy after a backend restart, but Hyperliquid shows `Degraded`. Hyperliquid previously worked, so this is likely a regression, configuration drift, or live-market eligibility issue rather than a new feature request.

The current UI does not explain why Hyperliquid is degraded. Operators cannot tell whether the collector is:

- running but receiving no live messages,
- receiving WebSocket messages but not updating runtime stats,
- blocked by stale or invalid subscribed symbols,
- blocked in writer/Redis/DB paths,
- using stale persisted freshness data,
- or simply reporting an ambiguous status.

## 2. Preliminary investigation findings

Code review points to the data-feed collector card status source:

- `frontend/src/components/datafeed/CollectorControlCard.tsx` displays `collectorStatus.exchange_status` from `GET /api/v1/collectors/{exchange}`.
- `backend/app/services/exchange_status.py` marks a running collector `degraded` when neither `stats.last_candle_time` nor `stats.last_orderbook_time` is within the 5-minute live activity threshold after the startup grace period.
- `backend/app/services/collector/orchestrator.py` updates those timestamps only when candle/orderbook writer loops consume queued live messages.
- `backend/config/datafeed.yaml` currently auto-starts Hyperliquid with `BTC, ETH, SOL, ARB, WIF, DOGE, BNB, AVAX, OP, MATIC` across several timeframes.
- A direct Hyperliquid public WebSocket probe on 2026-05-07 confirmed BTC/ETH/SOL live candle and orderbook subscriptions still produce messages, so the public endpoint itself is not globally down.
- The same probe showed `MATIC` orderbook responses with empty levels and no observed candles in a short window; ARB/OP also had no observed candles in that short probe. These may be delisted, low-activity, or otherwise unsuitable for default live subscriptions.
- Existing status copy does not expose per-symbol subscription health, empty-book counts, last received WebSocket message, queue depth, or writer-loop liveness, so preview must be instrumented or queried before declaring a single root cause.

Working hypothesis: Hyperliquid is being marked degraded because its collector status lacks recent runtime activity timestamps, likely due to live subscription/config drift or a runtime path that receives WebSocket traffic but does not successfully advance writer-loop stats. The fix should both restore Hyperliquid connectivity and make future degraded states self-diagnosing.

## 3. Goals

1. Determine the exact preview cause for Hyperliquid degraded status.
2. Restore Hyperliquid to connected/healthy after backend restart only when every enabled/configured live pair is validated and actively healthy, or explicitly disabled/marked non-live with a visible reason.
3. Reconcile default and scheduled Hyperliquid live subscriptions so stale, delisted, or invalid pairs cannot be silently counted as healthy.
4. Make degraded status actionable by exposing a concise reason and enough diagnostics to distinguish source, pair-level subscription, queue, writer, storage, and stale-data failures.
5. Add regression coverage so Hyperliquid startup health and pair-level health cannot silently regress while Binance/Kraken remain green.
6. Keep the design compatible with upcoming all-pair Hyperliquid historical-data integration and backfill/currentness workflows, without implementing that broader catalog/database integration here.

## 4. Non-goals

- Do not enable all Hyperliquid/TikTape catalog symbols for live streaming by default.
- Do not integrate the full downloaded all-pair historical dataset into the database in this PRD.
- Do not build the full gap-backfill/currentness system for the expanded pair universe in this PRD.
- Do not change trading/execution behavior.
- Do not require new provider credentials for public Hyperliquid live health.
- Do not make Predict depend directly on Hyperliquid/TikTape APIs.
- Do not broadly redesign the Data Feeds admin UI beyond the diagnostics needed for this issue.

## 5. User stories

### US-1: See the true Hyperliquid degradation reason

As an operator, I want Hyperliquid's degraded state to include a reason, so I know whether to fix subscriptions, restart, inspect storage, or wait for startup sync.

Acceptance criteria:

- The collector status response includes a stable reason code/message when `exchange_status = degraded`.
- The UI displays a short operator-facing reason on the Hyperliquid card.
- Reason codes distinguish at least: no owned symbols, no recent live messages, writer stalled, persistence unavailable, and stale persisted data.

### US-2: Restore healthy Hyperliquid default startup

As an operator, I want Hyperliquid to become connected after backend restart, just like Binance and Kraken, only when every enabled live pair is actually working.

Acceptance criteria:

- After restart, Hyperliquid reaches `running` and `connected` within the startup grace period on preview when all enabled live pairs are healthy.
- Hyperliquid does not show green solely because BTC/ETH/SOL are flowing while another enabled pair is stale, invalid, or returning unusable live data.
- `last_candle_time`, `last_orderbook_time`, or pair-level last activity advances continuously for every enabled live pair, with clear exemptions only for explicitly disabled/non-live pairs.
- The collector remains connected for at least 15 minutes in a validation run, with pair-level evidence for each enabled pair.

### US-3: Keep live subscriptions safe and current

As a data-feed maintainer, I want every enabled Hyperliquid live subscription to be validated, so stale or invalid pairs cannot be hidden behind an exchange-level green check.

Acceptance criteria:

- Hyperliquid default startup validates configured symbols against native live metadata or observed subscription responses.
- Symbols with empty orderbooks or no live candle activity are surfaced as per-symbol warnings and contribute to degraded status while enabled.
- Confirmed problematic live symbols are fixed, removed from the enabled live set, disabled, or explicitly marked non-live with an operator-visible reason.
- The validation approach scales beyond the current default list to the larger Hyperliquid pair universe expected from separate historical-data ingestion work.

### US-4: Detect runtime path stalls

As an engineer, I want to know whether WebSocket receive, queue consumption, Redis publish, DB persistence, or stats updates are failing, so degraded status is not a black box.

Acceptance criteria:

- Collector status exposes exchange-level and pair-level last WebSocket message time, last queued message time, queue depths, writer-loop last-consumed time, and persistence enabled/disabled flags where available.
- Writer-loop exceptions and queue saturation are counted and surfaced.
- Runtime health does not rely only on persisted DB freshness when the collector is actively receiving live messages.
- Future expanded-pair monitoring can reuse the same health semantics without treating BTC/ETH/SOL as special-case proof that the whole adapter is healthy.

## 6. Functional requirements

### 6.1 Preview diagnosis

- Query and record current Hyperliquid `GET /api/v1/collectors/hyperliquid` status on preview.
- Compare Hyperliquid stats to Binance/Kraken: state, `exchange_status`, owned symbols, `last_candle_time`, `last_orderbook_time`, counts, errors, plugin status, storage accounting.
- Check backend logs for Hyperliquid startup, subscription responses, empty orderbook warnings, writer errors, Redis publish errors, and DB persistence errors.
- Compare live schedule/config sources: `collector_schedules`, YAML fallback, and UI start defaults.

### 6.2 Hyperliquid live subscription remediation

- Validate current default Hyperliquid symbols against native Hyperliquid metadata and observed live stream behavior.
- Remove, disable, fix, or mark known bad default live subscriptions as non-live until catalog capability work handles them safely.
- Require every enabled live pair to have recent usable live activity before the adapter reports healthy.
- Do not use primary symbols (`BTC`, `ETH`, `SOL`) as a substitute for full enabled-pair health.
- Keep broad catalog/database integration separate from safe default live startup, but design the health semantics for the larger pair universe.

### 6.3 Health semantics and diagnostics

- Add a backend helper that computes `exchange_status_reason` alongside `exchange_status`.
- Return compact exchange-level and pair-level reasons in collector status schemas.
- Add Hyperliquid-specific diagnostics only where needed, but keep the status contract exchange-neutral.
- Preserve existing `connected`, `syncing`, `degraded`, and `down` values for frontend compatibility.

### 6.4 UI changes

- Show the degraded reason on `CollectorControlCard` when present.
- Show affected pair names when pair-level failures cause degradation.
- Show recent message timestamps or a concise detail line when a collector is running but degraded.
- Avoid verbose implementation narration in the primary UI; keep deeper diagnostics behind details or secondary text.

## 7. Suggested implementation tasks

1. Add a short diagnostic script or admin-only log checklist to capture preview collector status and logs before code changes.
2. Add `exchange_status_reason` and relevant diagnostic fields to collector schemas/responses.
3. Add tests for `exchange_status.py` covering running-without-activity, startup grace, stale persisted fallback, and reason codes.
4. Reconcile Hyperliquid default symbols/schedules so every enabled pair is either healthy, fixed, disabled, or explicitly marked non-live; investigate examples such as `MATIC` if confirmed by preview/native metadata.
5. Add Hyperliquid collector tests for empty orderbook handling, missing live activity, and per-symbol warnings that correctly degrade the adapter while affected symbols remain enabled.
6. Update `CollectorControlCard` to show the reason/details concisely, including affected pairs.
7. Validate on preview with a backend restart and a 15-minute observation window that covers every enabled Hyperliquid pair.

## 8. Validation plan

Minimum local checks:

- `cd backend && python3 -m pytest tests/services/test_exchange_status.py tests/api/routers/test_collectors.py tests/services/collector -q`
- Add or update targeted tests for Hyperliquid empty orderbook/default-symbol handling and pair-level health semantics.
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run CollectorControlCard`
- `git diff --check`

Preview checks:

- Restart backend or trigger the same startup path that currently causes the issue.
- Confirm Binance and Kraken collector cards reach `Connected` or `Syncing` during startup and then `Connected` after live activity.
- Confirm Hyperliquid reaches `Connected` only when every enabled pair has recent usable live activity or is explicitly disabled/non-live.
- Confirm Hyperliquid exchange-level and pair-level activity advances for at least 15 minutes.
- Confirm any disabled/stale Hyperliquid symbols are visible as warnings or config differences, not silent whole-exchange green status.

## 9. Verifier checkpoints

1. **Diagnosis checkpoint:** verifier reviews captured preview status/log evidence and confirms the root cause is identified before remediation changes are accepted.
2. **Backend checkpoint:** verifier reviews status reason semantics, pair-level health semantics, Hyperliquid config/collector changes, and targeted backend tests.
3. **Frontend checkpoint:** verifier reviews UI copy/diagnostic rendering and frontend tests.
4. **Final bug-check:** verifier runs a final regression pass after preview validation evidence is recorded.

## 10. Dependencies and related work

- Related: #591 Data Feed Quality Tab Truthful Recovery State.
- Related: #612 TikTape-backed Hyperliquid datafeed catalog enablement.
- This PRD should stay focused on restoring safe live Hyperliquid startup and diagnostics for all enabled pairs. Broader catalog/database integration and expanded historical-data enablement belongs in #612 or related follow-up work.

## 11. Human gates

Escalate before:

- changing production collector schedules beyond fixing/removing/marking confirmed-bad enabled pairs,
- enabling a larger Hyperliquid live symbol set,
- treating primary-symbol health as sufficient for whole-adapter green status,
- changing health status semantics used by other pages,
- adding new secrets or provider credentials,
- or deciding Hyperliquid can remain degraded if primary live data is flowing.

content.body:
# PRD: NOME chat integration UX across desktop and mobile

## Lifecycle metadata

- status: approved
- type: prd
- owner_agent: Evonome-frontend
- worktree_path: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-frontend`
- github_project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
- working_branch: `feat/nome-chat-responsive-polish`
- base_branch: `main`
- prd_review_status: approved
- ceo_approved: yes
- ceo_approved_at: 2026-05-07T21:57:16Z
- previous_approval: superseded by the 2026-05-07 UX pivot
- implementation_status: approved for Checkpoint A no-code baseline audit; product-code changes remain blocked until baseline target UX approval
- created_at: 2026-05-07
- revised_at: 2026-05-07


## CEO approval notes

Approved on 2026-05-07T21:57:16Z. Scope is approved as a baseline-first NOME chat integration UX PRD. Implementation must begin with Checkpoint A no-code baseline screenshots/clips from `origin/main`; no product-code changes may begin until the baseline target UX is human-approved. Approved product decisions: phone full-screen chat sheet, tablet portrait sheet, tablet landscape side panel, Browse hide-and-restore, and desktop preservation-first behavior. Training Lab visual work, Portfolio rebuild, Settings content build-out, backend reliability work, and full light-theme redesign remain out of scope.

## Revision note

This PRD supersedes the earlier spacing-focused PRD. Browser validation and direct product review showed that NOME chat felt better before the prior implementation started, especially on Discovery where the panel became too tall. The branch should restart from the `origin/main` chat experience and treat measurements as supporting evidence, not the primary product goal.

Approved on 2026-05-07T21:57:16Z. Implementation may proceed only with Checkpoint A, the no-code baseline audit. Product-code changes remain blocked until the baseline target UX is reviewed and approved.

## Background

NOME chat is already functional and partially integrated into the app shell. The next pass should improve the overall user experience of how chat belongs in the product across desktop, tablet, and mobile rather than forcing a uniform pixel model across routes.

The highest-risk area is responsive behavior. Desktop can remain a side-panel pattern where it already works well. Phone widths should use a true full-screen chat sheet. Tablet portrait should follow the phone pattern, while tablet landscape should use the desktop side-panel pattern.

## Problem statement

NOME chat should feel like a native part of the app, not a layer that fights page content. The current work should answer this by preserving what already feels good on desktop and deliberately improving phone/tablet integration.

Primary problems to solve:

- The phone-width experience needs a clear full-screen chat sheet pattern with keyboard-safe input behavior.
- The closed launcher must remain visible, tappable, and understandable on phone and tablet.
- Tablet portrait and tablet landscape need intentional behavior instead of inheriting an awkward breakpoint.
- Desktop changes must not regress route-specific layouts that already feel good, especially Discovery.
- Browse and other blocking overlays should not visually or interactively compete with chat.
- Frontend-owned conversation states should feel calm and finished.

## CEO shaping decisions

- **Mobile:** at phone widths, NOME opens as a true full-screen chat sheet by default.
- **Tablet:** tablet portrait follows the phone/full-screen sheet pattern; tablet landscape uses the desktop side-panel pattern.
- **Browse modal:** when Browse opens while NOME is open, temporarily hide NOME and restore its prior open/closed state when Browse closes.
- **Desktop:** preserve `origin/main` desktop behavior unless baseline visual review identifies a specific route problem.
- **Validation:** human visual review of screenshots or clips is the pass/fail source when measurements and perceived quality conflict.
- **Checkpoint A:** implementation begins with a no-code baseline audit from `origin/main`; coding is blocked until the target UX is approved.

## Product principles

1. Preserve the `origin/main` baseline wherever it already feels better.
2. Human screenshot or clip review comes before pixel-perfect measurements.
3. Desktop, tablet, and phone may use different patterns when that produces a better UX.
4. Route-specific behavior is acceptable for genuinely different content models, but avoid scattered magic numbers.
5. Keep implementation minimal and reversible; avoid broad app-shell refactors unless the baseline audit proves they are needed.
6. Do not make Training Lab visual changes as part of this PRD.

## Goals

1. Define and validate the desired NOME chat experience for desktop, tablet, and mobile before coding.
2. Preserve or restore the desktop baseline that currently feels better.
3. Make the mobile closed launcher visible, tappable, and understandable.
4. Make phone-width NOME open as a keyboard-safe full-screen chat sheet.
5. Make tablet portrait use the full-screen sheet pattern and tablet landscape use the desktop side-panel pattern.
6. Ensure NOME does not collide with primary controls on Discovery, Charts, Trading, Admin, Settings, Archive, or Browse.
7. Improve obvious frontend-owned conversation polish.
8. Establish verifier and browser/human review gates that prioritize visual UX over isolated spacing metrics.

## Non-goals

- No Training Lab / training-page visual work.
- No Portfolio rebuild.
- No Settings content build-out.
- No backend reliability work for NOME responses.
- No new NOME product features such as multi-thread history, memory, or model controls.
- No full light-theme redesign; only smoke-check for obviously unreadable or broken states.
- No requirement that every desktop route use an identical vertical anchor if a route-specific anchor produces a better user experience.
- No pixel-perfect symmetric-gutter mandate without visual approval.

## In-scope surfaces

- NOME launcher and open panel/sheet.
- App shell integration on desktop, tablet, and phone.
- Discovery routes and view modes.
- Charts.
- Paper Trading and Live Trading.
- Admin data feeds.
- Settings.
- Archive.
- Browse modal interaction with chat.

## User stories and acceptance criteria

### Story 1 — Baseline audit before implementation

As the product owner, I want to see the current `origin/main` NOME experience before changes so we do not regress what already feels right.

Acceptance criteria:

- Capture current baseline screenshots or short clips for the required viewport matrix before coding.
- For each tested surface, record `keep`, `change`, or `needs decision` notes.
- Include Discovery-specific review confirming whether the panel height feels appropriate relative to the canvas.
- Include Charts-specific review confirming whether the current side-panel relationship preserves chart usability.
- Human approval of the target UX is required before implementation begins.
- No product-code changes are made in Checkpoint A.

### Story 2 — Phone-width full-screen chat sheet

As a phone user, I want an obvious way to open NOME and a full-screen chat surface that remains usable with the keyboard.

Acceptance criteria:

- At phone widths, NOME opens as a true full-screen chat sheet rather than a desktop side panel or partial bottom sheet.
- At 390 × 844 and 375 × 667, a NOME launcher is visible or available through an obvious labeled chat entry point when chat is closed.
- The launcher has an accessible name and a practical touch target.
- Opening chat does not cause horizontal overflow.
- The message list and input remain usable when the keyboard is open where device tooling can validate it.
- Closing chat returns to the prior page without scroll jump or route change.
- Header actions remain accessible when chat is closed.

### Story 3 — Intentional tablet behavior

As a tablet user, I want NOME to adapt to portrait and landscape instead of inheriting an awkward desktop or phone layout.

Acceptance criteria:

- At tablet portrait size around 820 × 1180, NOME uses the phone-style full-screen sheet pattern.
- At tablet landscape size around 1180 × 820, NOME uses the desktop side-panel pattern.
- Tablet closed-state launcher is visible, tappable, and accessible in both orientations.
- Tablet controls meet touch-target expectations.
- Orientation changes do not strand the chat in an unusable or clipped state.

### Story 4 — Desktop chat preserves what already works

As a desktop user, I want NOME chat to feel placed intentionally beside app content without awkward route regressions.

Acceptance criteria:

- The desktop side-panel pattern is preserved where it already works well on `origin/main`.
- Discovery pages do not stretch the chat panel unnecessarily; prior good visual height should be preserved unless baseline review approves a change.
- Charts do not hide critical chart controls or create unusable dead space.
- Admin, Settings, Archive, Paper Trading, and Live Trading remain visually usable with chat open.
- Desktop changes are limited to route problems identified during the no-code baseline audit.
- Measurements may be recorded, but human visual review is the pass/fail source when measurements and perceived quality conflict.

### Story 5 — Conversation surface polish

As a user chatting with NOME, I want the chat surface to feel calm and finished.

Acceptance criteria:

- Error bubbles do not render duplicated prefixes such as `Error: Error:`.
- Raw HTTP failure strings are not the primary user-facing copy.
- Failed responses provide calm copy and a retry affordance when frontend-owned.
- Long prompts are reviewable before send.
- The input grows or scrolls in a controlled way.
- The message area uses available space without excessive blank gaps after the latest message.
- Send button styling reads as an action, not as a permanently selected input state.

### Story 6 — Browse modal hide and restore

As a user opening Browse while NOME chat is open, I should not see or interact with chat controls through the modal.

Acceptance criteria:

- When Browse opens while NOME is open, NOME is temporarily hidden.
- Closing Browse restores NOME to its prior open/closed state.
- Chat controls are not interactable through Browse.
- The behavior is consistent on desktop and tablet.
- If NOME was closed before Browse opened, it remains closed when Browse closes.

## Required baseline and sign-off viewport matrix

| Viewport | Required review |
| --- | --- |
| 1440 × 900 | Desktop full-size side-panel baseline and after-state review |
| 1200 × 800 | Desktop windowed baseline and after-state review |
| 1024 × 768 | Desktop/tablet boundary review |
| 1180 × 820 | Tablet landscape side-panel review |
| 820 × 1180 | Tablet portrait full-screen sheet review |
| 390 × 844 | Mobile large full-screen sheet review |
| 375 × 667 | Mobile small full-screen sheet review |

## Route-specific visual checks

For each in-scope route, verify chat in these states where practical:

- Closed launcher state.
- Open greeting state.
- Open conversation with at least one user message.
- Failed assistant response state.
- Long user prompt before send.
- Scrolled chat history state.
- Browse modal open while chat was already open.
- Mobile keyboard-open state where device tooling allows it.

## Checkpoints and gates

### Checkpoint A — No-code baseline and target UX approval

- Start from `origin/main` behavior.
- Produce screenshots or clips across the viewport matrix.
- Record which behaviors should be preserved, changed, or decided.
- Include explicit Discovery review that the panel height feels appropriate relative to the canvas.
- Include explicit mobile/tablet launcher and open-chat baseline notes.
- Stop for human approval before any product-code changes.

### Checkpoint B — Mobile and tablet interaction

- Implement only the approved phone full-screen sheet and tablet portrait/landscape behavior.
- Prioritize launcher visibility, touch targets, input visibility, keyboard safety, and no horizontal overflow.
- Browser/human visual gate required before continuing.

### Checkpoint C — Desktop route integration

- Make only desktop changes approved from Checkpoint A evidence.
- Preserve Discovery height and any other baseline behavior marked `keep`.
- Do not perform a broad single-anchor or symmetric-spacing rewrite unless baseline evidence supports it.
- Browser/human visual gate required before continuing.

### Checkpoint D — Conversation and Browse/modal polish

- Implement frontend-owned conversation polish.
- Implement Browse hide/restore behavior.
- Verify chat is not interactable through blocking overlays.
- Verifier review required; browser review required if visual or stacking risk remains.

### Final pass

- Run verifier final review and default bug-check.
- Final sign-off requires human acceptance of before/after evidence across the viewport matrix.

## Validation evidence to record

- `git status --short --branch`.
- Baseline and after screenshots or clips.
- Viewport matrix results.
- Routes checked and unavailable routes.
- Typecheck, lint, and build results where applicable.
- Verifier reports and browser/human visual gate notes.
- Light-theme smoke-check result if the theme toggle is available.

## Open questions for Checkpoint A

These should be answered by the no-code baseline audit before implementation:

1. Which desktop route states should be marked `keep`, `change`, or `needs decision`?
2. Does the current mobile launcher appear anywhere usable, or does the new full-screen sheet require a new launcher placement?
3. Does the current tablet breakpoint map cleanly to portrait sheet and landscape side panel, or is a breakpoint adjustment required?
4. Which conversation polish items are visible and frontend-owned in the current baseline?

## Out-of-scope follow-up candidates

- Fix or remove `/app/trading/portfolio` route if it remains linked from Browse.
- Complete Settings cards that currently render as empty shells.
- Separate light-theme visual pass for the app shell and NOME chat.
- Real-device mobile keyboard QA infrastructure if browser tooling cannot reliably emulate keyboard behavior.


## Product decision

This method is a Discovery-owned product surface. Training Strategize may be used as historical reference, migration reference, or narrow compatibility support only. It must not remain the canonical product route, frontend create surface, backend ownership model, persisted method identity, lifecycle label, or user-visible job context.

Compatibility aliases are allowed only when needed for existing jobs or unavoidable migration safety. Any remaining alias must be narrow, documented, hidden from the primary Discovery product experience, and backed by a follow-up cleanup issue when it cannot be removed inside this PRD.

## Configuration output contract

This PRD is part of the four-method Discovery ownership set: #647 Signal Discovery, #648 Pattern Discovery, #649 System Builder, and #650 Evolutionary Strategy. These methods may have method-specific job inputs and lifecycle evidence, but configuration output must look deliberately designed and consistent across all four.

Canonical output requirements:

- Use one shared Strategy Configuration v1 package family as the downstream configuration boundary.
- Use one export route: `GET /api/v1/autoresearch/export-strategy-configuration?project=<project>`.
- Use one package root: `strategy-configuration-package`.
- Use one primary artifact name: `strategy-configuration.json`.
- Use the same companion artifact names: `configuration-handoff-summary.json`, `import-readiness.json`, `provenance.json`, and `supporting-evidence/index.json`.
- Use `compatibility/compatibility.json` and `compatibility/genomespec-handoff.json` only for narrow migration support; compatibility files must not become the canonical product output.

`strategy-configuration.json` must keep the same top-level Strategy Configuration v1 section structure across all four methods:

- `contract_version`
- `schema_ref`
- `schema_dialect`
- `configuration_metadata`
- `package_kind`
- `source_method`
- `market_context`
- `data_requirements_and_lineage`
- `component_or_trait_references`
- `execution_and_sizing_summary`
- `risk_guardrails_and_portfolio_intent`
- `validation_summary`
- `provenance_and_source_version`
- `import_readiness`
- `source_specific_evidence_extension_area`

For this PRD, `source_method.content.value` must resolve to `signal_discovery` and the Discovery method id must resolve to `discovery_signals`. Method-specific differences belong inside canonical section `content`, `source_specific_evidence_extension_area`, or supporting-evidence artifacts. They must not create separate top-level package shapes, separate canonical filenames, separate frontend download flows, or separate backend export services.

If the method is not ready to emit a valid configuration package, it must fail closed through the shared readiness vocabulary (`unavailable`, `incomplete`, `blocked`, or `decision_required`). Candidate previews, local `config_ready` booleans, and method-specific preview JSON are not valid configuration output by themselves.

## Adversarial Debate reference baseline

Adversarial Debate is the mature Discovery reference implementation for configuration output. These PRDs should align with that model so the app feels intentionally designed rather than patched method-by-method.

Use Adversarial Debate as the reference for:

- registry-owned Discovery method identity and shell integration in `frontend/src/discovery/registry.ts`;
- package-backed readiness, including fail-closed behavior, in `frontend/src/discovery/methods/debate/debateHandoffReadiness.ts` and `frontend/src/discovery/handoffReadiness.ts`;
- the shared output surface in `frontend/src/discovery/shared/StrategyConfigHandoffCard.tsx`;
- the canonical backend package builder/exporter under `backend/app/services/discovery/strategy_configuration/`;

```json
"ucb_exploration": 1.4,
"stagnation_threshold": 3,
"llm_budget": 0
  }
}
```

Confirm optional Discover-source and ML-filter controls fail gracefully when no compatible source artifact exists, rather than blocking unrelated default job creation.

If the current implementation reaches this contract through Training-owned helpers or Strategize compatibility, the coder must not treat that as complete. They must either move the canonical path under Discovery or neutral shared infrastructure, or record a precise verifier-reviewed blocker explaining why a temporary alias remains and what follow-up removes it.

Deliverables:

- Remove, replace, or narrow canonical paths that send users through Training Strategize UI/chrome or Training-owned product context.
- Create the job from the terminal/API using the same Discovery-owned payload shape the UI should submit.
- Verify the response contains the created job id, status, symbol, timeframe, exchange, Discovery category/method identity, workflow config, model/provider fields where relevant, and experiment linkage when applicable.
- Verify the job appears in the list/read endpoint used by the Discovery page with the same Discovery-owned identity and expected workflow config.
- If creation fails, capture the exact error, root cause it, and fix the smallest backend/frontend contract gap.
- Delete or clearly mark test jobs according to the repo's normal cleanup path.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 2. The verifier independently reviews terminal evidence, ownership cleanup, and any fixes before linked lifecycle work begins.

### Phase 2 — Linked lifecycle and method-state behavior

Exercise the Discovery-owned Pattern Discovery linked lifecycle with `discovery_mode: pattern_discovery` and the smallest safe generation budget. If the current runtime still invokes a legacy Strategize/guided-loop runner, it must be treated as internal shared execution or temporary compatibility only, not as the product owner. Confirm `strategize_job_id`/legacy runner id, `strategize_status`/lifecycle status, linked reasoning/frontier display, and source-artifact compatibility errors are persisted and presented as Pattern Discovery state with exact mismatch details.

Deliverables:

- Exercise the cheapest safe lifecycle path available for the method.
- Confirm method-state fields update truthfully and do not show false readiness.
- Confirm lifecycle labels, logs, and status surfaces present Discovery ownership rather than Training Strategize ownership.
- Confirm failures surface specific operator-facing reasons instead of generic or silent failures.
- Add or update tests that cover the repaired contract and error behavior.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 3. The verifier confirms the method-specific lifecycle is truthful, preserves Discovery ownership, and no unrelated scope was absorbed.

### Phase 3 — Browser/web-agent confirmation

Web agent opens `/app/discovery/patterns`, creates a default Pattern Discovery job without optional upstream artifacts, and records job id, visible method label, status, and network/console errors. If terminal testing fixed optional-source behavior, the browser agent should also verify that the optional control shows the expected disabled/error state.

Deliverables:

- After terminal/API checks pass, request a browser/web agent to open the preview route and create a job through the modal.
- Browser evidence must show Discovery product context and must not rely on a Training Strategize page as the final user flow.
- Browser agent must record route, input values, submit result, resulting job id/name/metadata, visible status, and any console/network errors.
- Coder fixes actionable browser-only regressions and sends another verifier checkpoint if code changes after browser QA.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 4. The verifier confirms browser evidence matches terminal behavior and preserves Discovery ownership.

### Phase 4 — Final verification, bug-check, and PR evidence

Deliverables:

- Run applicable quality gates.
- Verifier runs final `bug-check` pass without asking for another approval once scoped implementation is complete.
- Prepare PR evidence only: summary, validation commands, terminal job ids or sanitized logs, browser check notes, bug-check result, configuration-output contract evidence, remaining risks, and any explicit compatibility alias/follow-up issue.
- Do not create/open a PR unless the user explicitly asks.

Verifier checkpoint: final approval or revision request.

## Functional requirements

- FR-1: Pattern Discovery terminal creation must use a Discovery-owned product contract with category `genesis_patterns` and method id `discovery_patterns`.
- FR-2: Default pattern creation must not require a completed Discover/Predict/Combine artifact.
- FR-3: Payloads must preserve market scope, pattern intent, family selection, data-window selection, direction, budget, and optional source metadata.
- FR-4: Linked lifecycle must preserve Discovery-owned Pattern Discovery method identity. Any Strategize runner/category usage must be internal compatibility, not the canonical contract or visible product owner.
- FR-5: Optional source compatibility errors must be specific and recoverable.
- FR-6: Canonical frontend code for Pattern Discovery create and lifecycle surfaces must live under Discovery ownership or shared neutral infrastructure, not Training-owned UI/chrome.
- FR-7: Any retained Training or Strategize compatibility must be documented as migration support with verifier-reviewed rationale and a cleanup follow-up when not removable in this PRD.

- FR-CFG: Configuration output must use the shared Strategy Configuration v1 package family, artifact names, export route, readiness vocabulary, and frontend handoff/export component shared across #647–#650.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Terminal creates a `genesis_patterns` job and records the job id.
- [ ] Terminal list/read verification finds the same job with expected Discovery method identity and workflow config.
- [ ] The canonical creation path no longer depends on Training Strategize UI/chrome or Training-owned product context.
- [ ] Any remaining `strategize` usage is compatibility-only, hidden from the primary product flow, documented, and either justified or tracked for cleanup.
- [ ] Linked Pattern Discovery lifecycle is exercised or blocked with a precise accepted reason.
- [ ] Default no-upstream creation works or has a documented product-approved blocker.
- [ ] Browser agent creates a Pattern Discovery job after terminal success in Discovery product context.
- [ ] Configuration output uses the shared Strategy Configuration package root, artifact inventory, top-level section structure, export route, readiness vocabulary, and shared frontend output path used by the sibling Discovery methods.
- [ ] Adversarial Debate is used as the reference baseline for output architecture, and any intentional divergence is documented with rationale.
- [ ] Verifier checkpoints and final bug-check are recorded.

## Quality gates

The coder must record exact commands, exit codes, and relevant output excerpts at every checkpoint.

Minimum gates, adjusted only when a command is unavailable and the verifier accepts the substitute:

- Frontend touched: `cd frontend && pnpm typecheck`
- Frontend touched: `cd frontend && pnpm lint`
- Frontend touched: targeted Vitest/Playwright tests for changed Discovery/Training compatibility surfaces, then broader `cd frontend && pnpm test` when feasible
- Backend touched: `cd backend && uv run ruff check app tests`
- Backend touched: targeted `cd backend && uv run pytest ...` for changed routers/services/contracts
- Configuration output touched: targeted backend Strategy Configuration export/import-readiness tests and frontend shared handoff/export tests, plus a cross-method fixture or assertion that this method matches the same package inventory and top-level section structure as the sibling Discovery methods
- Reference parity touched: include Adversarial Debate/shared-output regression tests such as `backend/tests/discovery/test_strategy_configuration_foundation.py`, `backend/tests/discovery/test_strategy_configuration_export.py`, `frontend/src/discovery/shared/StrategyConfigHandoffCard.test.tsx`, `frontend/src/discovery/methods/debate/DebateDetailPanel.test.tsx`, and `frontend/src/discovery/registry.contract.test.ts` when related seams change
- End of implementation: run the local quality gate if available: `/gate --ml`
- End of implementation: verifier runs a final `bug-check` pass before PR preparation and before this PRD can be marked done

Browser checks do not replace terminal/API checks. They are the final product confirmation after the terminal path is passing.

## Success metrics

- A terminal/API create attempt succeeds for a real bounded job with Discovery-owned method metadata.
- Any discovered create-time or first-lifecycle error is fixed or escalated with a precise blocker.
- The UI create flow works in Discovery product context after terminal verification.
- Training Strategize is not the canonical ownership model for Pattern Discovery creation or lifecycle presentation.
- Adversarial Debate remains the reference baseline for coherent configuration output architecture.
- Verifier checkpoints are recorded between phases.
- Final verifier bug-check is complete before PR preparation.

## CEO approval

Approved on 2026-05-07. The original “patent discovery” wording was a voice-to-text error; this PRD targets the existing Pattern Discovery page at `/discovery/patterns`. CEO ownership amendment added on 2026-05-07: Pattern Discovery must be Discovery-owned; Training Strategize may remain only as internal compatibility or shared execution support, not the canonical product owner.

# PRD: System Builder Job Creation Verification and Repair

---

```yaml

verifier_socket: /tmp/agentops/pi-verifier-system-builder-job-creation-verification-repair.sock
```

## Product decision

This method is a Discovery-owned product surface. Training Strategize may be used as historical reference, migration reference, or narrow compatibility support only. It must not remain the canonical product route, frontend create surface, backend ownership model, persisted method identity, lifecycle label, or user-visible job context.

Compatibility aliases are allowed only when needed for existing jobs or unavoidable migration safety. Any remaining alias must be narrow, documented, hidden from the primary Discovery product experience, and backed by a follow-up cleanup issue when it cannot be removed inside this PRD.

## Configuration output contract

This PRD is part of the four-method Discovery ownership set: #647 Signal Discovery, #648 Pattern Discovery, #649 System Builder, and #650 Evolutionary Strategy. These methods may have method-specific job inputs and lifecycle evidence, but configuration output must look deliberately designed and consistent across all four.

Canonical output requirements:

- Use one shared Strategy Configuration v1 package family as the downstream configuration boundary.
- Use one export route: `GET /api/v1/autoresearch/export-strategy-configuration?project=<project>`.
- Use one package root: `strategy-configuration-package`.
- Use one primary artifact name: `strategy-configuration.json`.
- Use the same companion artifact names: `configuration-handoff-summary.json`, `import-readiness.json`, `provenance.json`, and `supporting-evidence/index.json`.
- Use `compatibility/compatibility.json` and `compatibility/genomespec-handoff.json` only for narrow migration support; compatibility files must not become the canonical product output.

`strategy-configuration.json` must keep the same top-level Strategy Configuration v1 section structure across all four methods:

- `contract_version`
- `schema_ref`
- `schema_dialect`
- `configuration_metadata`
- `package_kind`
- `source_method`
- `market_context`
- `data_requirements_and_lineage`
- `component_or_trait_references`
- `execution_and_sizing_summary`
- `risk_guardrails_and_portfolio_intent`
- `validation_summary`
- `provenance_and_source_version`
- `import_readiness`
- `source_specific_evidence_extension_area`

For this PRD, `source_method.content.value` must resolve to `system_builder` and the Discovery method id must resolve to `discovery_builder`. Method-specific differences belong inside canonical section `content`, `source_specific_evidence_extension_area`, or supporting-evidence artifacts. They must not create separate top-level package shapes, separate canonical filenames, separate frontend download flows, or separate backend export services.

If the method is not ready to emit a valid configuration package, it must fail closed through the shared readiness vocabulary (`unavailable`, `incomplete`, `blocked`, or `decision_required`). Candidate previews, local `config_ready` booleans, and method-specific preview JSON are not valid configuration output by themselves.

## Adversarial Debate reference baseline

Adversarial Debate is the mature Discovery reference implementation for configuration output. These PRDs should align with that model so the app feels intentionally designed rather than patched method-by-method.

Use Adversarial Debate as the reference for:

- registry-owned Discovery method identity and shell integration in `frontend/src/discovery/registry.ts`;
- package-backed readiness, including fail-closed behavior, in `frontend/src/discovery/methods/debate/debateHandoffReadiness.ts` and `frontend/src/discovery/handoffReadiness.ts`;
- the shared output surface in `frontend/src/discovery/shared/StrategyConfigHandoffCard.tsx`;
- the canonical backend package builder/exporter under `backend/app/services/discovery/strategy_configuration/`;
- the canonical export endpoint `GET /api/v1/autoresearch/export-strategy-configuration?project=<project>`;
- the package inventory and Strategy Configuration v1 schema tested by `backend/tests/discovery/test_strategy_configuration_foundation.py`, `backend/tests/discovery/test_strategy_configuration_export.py`, and the `backend/tests/discovery/fixtures/strategy_configuration/exported-ready-package/` fixture family.

The new methods should not copy Debate-specific phase names or legacy compatibility terminology. They should reuse the same seams: method-owned identity, shared package-backed readiness, shared handoff/export component, shared backend package family, and method-specific evidence placed inside canonical sections or supporting evidence.

## Problem

The page loads and the new-job modal appears, but that is not enough to trust the feature. The larger risk is that System Builder still depends on Training Strategize or Training-owned scaffolding after the Discovery port. That would leave confusing ownership across frontend routes, API helpers, backend validation, persistence metadata, list/read paths, lifecycle labels, and future maintenance.

We need an implementation PRD that verifies the current job-creation path, repairs actionable failures, completes Discovery ownership for System Builder job creation, proves real bounded jobs can be created from the terminal first, and then asks a browser/web agent to create through the UI as the final product check.

## Goal

Make `/discovery/builder` trustworthy as a Discovery-owned job creation and first-lifecycle flow. The implementation must prove the Discovery-specific create payload reaches the correct backend contract, persists with Discovery method ownership and expected metadata, surfaces actionable errors, reaches a truthful lifecycle state or precise blocker, and works through the browser after terminal verification passes.

## Starting confirmation from CEO

- The page loads.
- The job list/canvas surface loads.
- The new-job modal appears.
- The missing confidence is real Discovery-owned job creation, ownership cleanup, linked lifecycle behavior where applicable, error handling, and final browser confirmation.

## Scope and permissions

### Coder/verifier operating rules

- Owning agent: Evonome-discovery agent.
- Owning worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery`.
- The implementation agent may inspect and fix both `frontend/` and `backend/` in the same branch. Do not block a required frontend fix because the session started from a backend worktree, and do not block a required backend fix because the session started from a frontend worktree.
- Use one isolated coder/verifier pair for this PRD.
- Proposed artifact folder: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-discovery/.agent-artifacts/system-builder-job-creation-verification-repair/`.
- Proposed verifier socket: `/tmp/agentops/pi-verifier-system-builder-job-creation-verification-repair.sock`.
- The coder must update `coder-ready.md` after each phase with scope, diff summary, validation evidence, known risks, and the next requested verifier decision.
- The verifier must update `verifier-report.md` with Machine Status before the coder continues to the next phase.
- `revision_requested`, `rejected`, or `needs_human` blocks further phase work except bounded requested fixes.
- PR creation remains human-managed. Agents may prepare evidence and draft PR text only after final verification.

### Parallel Adversarial Debate hardening coordination

- This PRD may run in parallel with Adversarial Debate hardening in a separate worktree/session.
- Before changing shared Strategy Configuration, Discovery readiness/handoff, registry, shared output components, fixtures/tests, or job/lifecycle infrastructure, the coder must recheck the active Adversarial Debate branch and record any drift or conflict in Phase 0.
- If Adversarial Debate reference architecture changes, pause and rebase or reconcile before continuing.


### Validation environment

- All real terminal/API and browser-created jobs must target the preview backing environment used by `https://preview.evonome.com/app/discovery/builder`.
- Local execution is allowed for unit tests, static checks, and development support only; it cannot replace preview job evidence.
- Each checkpoint must record the preview API base/host, credential context, test job IDs, and cleanup or durable test-job marking evidence.
- Bounded preview jobs are allowed only with the smallest safe budgets and must be cleaned up or durably marked as test evidence according to repo practice.

In scope:

- Completing Discovery ownership for this method across route, UI create surface, API helper/contract, backend validation, persistence metadata, list/read behavior, and lifecycle presentation.
- Classifying and removing, renaming, extracting, or narrowing Training/Strategize dependencies that remain in the canonical path.
- Preserving compatibility for existing Training/Strategize jobs only where needed and documenting any unavoidable alias.
- Terminal/API creation of a real test job for this method.
- Debugging and fixing frontend create payload, backend request validation, persistence, list/read paths, error messages, and method-state sync required for job creation.
- Exercising the cheapest safe linked execution/lifecycle path when this method has a method-owned launch action.
- Browser/web-agent final creation check after terminal success.
- Tests and validation evidence.

Out of scope:

- Broad redesign of Discovery, Training, or Trading.
- Expensive production-scale searches unless explicitly approved.
- Deleting unrelated legacy Training compatibility routes unless required to stop canonical Discovery ownership leakage for this method.
- Creating or opening a PR without explicit human instruction.

## Implementation phases and verifier checkpoints

### Phase 0 — Baseline ownership trace and test harness plan

Trace at minimum:

- `frontend/src/discovery/registry.ts` method id `discovery_builder`.
- `frontend/src/discovery/methods/builder/SystemBuilderCreateModal.tsx`.
- `frontend/src/discovery/methods/builder/SystemBuilderPhaseWorkspace.tsx`.
- `frontend/src/discovery/methods/builder/systemBuilderMethodState.ts`.
- `frontend/src/features/training-lab/components/mindmap/useJobActions.ts` if the current Discovery path still depends on this Training-lab helper.
- `backend/app/api/discovery.py` `POST /api/v1/autoresearch/jobs` and `GET /api/v1/autoresearch/jobs`.
- Current linked lifecycle path through `POST /api/v1/guided-loop` with category `strategize` and `discovery_mode: system_builder`, if still present, to classify whether it is removable, shared infrastructure, or temporary compatibility.

Deliverables:

- Identify the exact route, create modal/component, frontend API helper, backend endpoint(s), category/method identifiers, list/read path, and any linked execution path.
- Identify every Training/Strategize dependency in the canonical path and classify it as remove, rename/extract to neutral shared infrastructure, compatibility-only, or acceptable internal execution detail.
- Define the Discovery-owned terminal test payload and expected response/list/read metadata before creating any jobs.
- Verify this method's configuration-output path against the shared four-method contract: same package root, artifact names, Strategy Configuration v1 section structure, export route, readiness vocabulary, and frontend output component.
- Compare the method against the Adversarial Debate reference path and record any intentional divergence from Debate's registry, readiness, shared output component, backend package builder/exporter, fixture inventory, or test coverage.
- Record a terminal test plan with request payloads, cleanup steps, and the smallest safe execution budget.
- Confirm active worktree, branch, base branch, and artifact/socket paths.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 1. The verifier confirms the terminal plan proves Discovery ownership, targets the same contract the UI uses, and does not rely on browser-only evidence or Training Strategize as the canonical path.

### Phase 1 — Terminal job creation and persistence

All real Phase 1 requests must use the preview backing API for `https://preview.evonome.com/app/discovery/builder`. Terminal creation must use the Discovery-owned System Builder contract first: `POST /api/v1/autoresearch/jobs` with category `genesis_builder` and method id `discovery_builder`. Use a bounded payload equivalent to the modal, for example:

```json
{
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "timeframe": "1h",
  "exchange": "hyperliquid",
  "category": "genesis_builder",
  "workflow_config": {
"method_id": "discovery_builder",
"method_intent": "system_builder",
"tuning_budget": 10,
"entry_direction": "both",
"preferred_signal_mode": "discover_library",
"source_components": ["alpha_registry", "predict_hof"]
  }
}
```

Confirm that a System Builder job can be created without upstream artifacts while the UI/backend truthfully warns that linked execution has less source material instead of failing with a generic error. Also create a valid source-component payload, or select the cheapest safe available source setup, so implementation proves both no-upstream behavior and normal source-aware creation.

If the current implementation reaches this contract through Training-owned helpers or Strategize compatibility, the coder must not treat that as complete. They must either move the canonical path under Discovery or neutral shared infrastructure, or record a precise verifier-reviewed blocker explaining why a temporary alias remains and what follow-up removes it.

Deliverables:

- Remove, replace, or narrow canonical paths that send users through Training Strategize UI/chrome or Training-owned product context.
- Create bounded preview jobs from the terminal/API for the no-upstream/low-source path and the valid source-component path using the same Discovery-owned payload shapes the UI should submit.
- Verify each response contains the created job id, status, symbol, timeframe, exchange, Discovery category/method identity, workflow config, selected source metadata where relevant, model/provider fields where relevant, and experiment linkage when applicable.
- Verify each job appears in the list/read endpoint used by the Discovery page with the same Discovery-owned identity and expected workflow config.
- Record preview API base/host, credential context, test job IDs, and cleanup or durable test-job marking evidence.
- If creation fails, capture the exact error, root cause it, and fix the smallest backend/frontend contract gap.
- Delete or clearly mark test jobs according to the repo's normal cleanup path.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 2. The verifier independently reviews terminal evidence, ownership cleanup, and any fixes before linked lifecycle work begins.

### Phase 2 — Linked lifecycle and method-state behavior

Exercise the Discovery-owned System Builder linked lifecycle with `discovery_mode: system_builder` and the smallest safe tuning budget. This is a hard acceptance gate when a method-owned launch action exists: the linked lifecycle must launch successfully, persist method state, and poll truthfully. A blocked or unavailable lifecycle does not satisfy acceptance unless Phase 0 proves no method-owned launch path exists and the verifier records a precise accepted reason.

If the current runtime still invokes a legacy Strategize/guided-loop runner, it must be treated as internal shared execution or temporary compatibility only, not as the product owner. Persist and present a Discovery-owned System Builder lifecycle state. Legacy fields such as `strategize_job_id` or `strategize_status` may remain only as internal compatibility aliases; they must not be the user-visible canonical labels. Confirm selected source metadata and signal-source mode are persisted, and verify no-upstream and incompatible-upstream cases show truthful warnings/errors without substituting for the lifecycle launch gate.

Deliverables:

- Launch the cheapest safe lifecycle path available for the method, or document verifier-accepted proof that no method-owned launch path exists.
- Confirm canonical System Builder method-state fields update truthfully and do not show false readiness.
- Confirm legacy `strategize_*` fields, if retained, are internal compatibility aliases and not user-visible canonical product labels.
- Confirm lifecycle labels, logs, and status surfaces present Discovery ownership rather than Training Strategize ownership.
- Confirm failures surface specific operator-facing reasons instead of generic or silent failures.
- Add or update tests that cover the repaired contract and error behavior.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 3. The verifier confirms the method-specific lifecycle is truthful, preserves Discovery ownership, and no unrelated scope was absorbed.

### Phase 3 — Browser/web-agent confirmation

Web agent opens `https://preview.evonome.com/app/discovery/builder`, creates a System Builder job with default selected components, and records job id, visible method label, status, source warnings, and network/console errors. If linked launch is available in the browser, the web agent must trigger the smallest safe launch after terminal success. If linked launch is unavailable in the browser, the browser report must tie back to the Phase 2 verifier-accepted reason.

Deliverables:

- After terminal/API checks pass, request a browser/web agent to open the preview route and create a job through the modal.
- Browser evidence must show Discovery product context and must not rely on a Training Strategize page as the final user flow.
- Browser agent must record route, input values, submit result, resulting job id/name/metadata, visible status, and any console/network errors.
- Coder fixes actionable browser-only regressions and sends another verifier checkpoint if code changes after browser QA.

Verifier checkpoint: required before Phase 4. The verifier confirms browser evidence matches terminal behavior and preserves Discovery ownership.

### Phase 4 — Final verification, bug-check, and PR evidence

Deliverables:

- Run applicable quality gates.
- Verifier runs final `bug-check` pass without asking for another approval once scoped implementation is complete.
- Prepare PR evidence only: summary, validation commands, terminal job ids or sanitized logs, browser check notes, bug-check result, configuration-output contract evidence, remaining risks, and any explicit compatibility alias/follow-up issue.
- Do not create/open a PR unless the user explicitly asks.

Verifier checkpoint: final approval or revision request.

## Functional requirements

- FR-1: System Builder terminal creation must use a Discovery-owned product contract with category `genesis_builder` and method id `discovery_builder`.
- FR-2: Payloads must preserve symbol, timeframe, exchange, tuning budget, entry direction, preferred signal mode, and selected source components.
- FR-3: Default no-upstream creation must be supported with truthful source warnings, and valid source-component creation must also be proven.
- FR-4: Linked lifecycle must launch successfully and preserve Discovery-owned System Builder method identity when a method-owned launch path exists. Any Strategize runner/category usage must be internal compatibility, not the canonical contract, canonical persisted product state, or visible product owner.
- FR-5: Source compatibility and missing artifact states must be specific, recoverable, and visible.
- FR-6: Canonical frontend code for System Builder create and lifecycle surfaces must live under Discovery ownership or shared neutral infrastructure, not Training-owned UI/chrome.
- FR-7: Any retained Training or Strategize compatibility must be documented as migration support with verifier-reviewed rationale and a cleanup follow-up when not removable in this PRD.
- FR-8: Preview validation must record API base/host, credential context, created job IDs, and cleanup or durable test-job marking evidence.

- FR-CFG: Configuration output must use the shared Strategy Configuration v1 package family, artifact names, export route, readiness vocabulary, and frontend handoff/export component shared across #647–#650.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preview terminal/API creates a no-upstream or low-source `genesis_builder` job and records the job id plus source-warning evidence.
- [ ] Preview terminal/API creates a valid source-component `genesis_builder` job, or selects the cheapest safe available source setup, and records the job id plus source metadata.
- [ ] Terminal list/read verification finds each created job with expected Discovery method identity and workflow config.
- [ ] Preview API base/host, credential context, test job IDs, and cleanup or durable test-job marking evidence are recorded.
- [ ] The canonical creation path no longer depends on Training Strategize UI/chrome or Training-owned product context.
- [ ] Any remaining `strategize` usage is compatibility-only, hidden from the primary product flow, documented, and either justified or tracked for cleanup.
- [ ] Legacy `strategize_job_id` or `strategize_status` fields, if retained, are internal aliases behind a Discovery-owned System Builder presentation layer.
- [ ] Linked System Builder lifecycle launches successfully, persists Discovery-owned lifecycle state, and polls truthfully when a method-owned launch path exists; otherwise Phase 0 and the verifier record a precise accepted reason that no such path exists.
- [ ] No-upstream and incompatible-upstream source states are truthful, recoverable, and do not masquerade as success-ready.
- [ ] Browser agent creates a System Builder job after terminal success in Discovery product context and records source warnings plus network/console errors.
- [ ] Browser agent triggers the linked launch when available after terminal success, or records the verifier-accepted reason it is unavailable.
- [ ] Configuration output uses the shared Strategy Configuration package root, artifact inventory, top-level section structure, export route, readiness vocabulary, and shared frontend output path used by the sibling Discovery methods.
- [ ] Adversarial Debate is used as the reference baseline for output architecture, and any intentional divergence is documented with rationale.
- [ ] Verifier checkpoints and final bug-check are recorded.

## Quality gates

The coder must record exact commands, exit codes, and relevant output excerpts at every checkpoint.

Minimum gates, adjusted only when a command is unavailable and the verifier accepts the substitute:

- Frontend touched: `cd frontend && pnpm typecheck`
- Frontend touched: `cd frontend && pnpm lint`
- Frontend touched: targeted Vitest/Playwright tests for changed Discovery/Training compatibility surfaces, then broader `cd frontend && pnpm test` when feasible

content.body:
# PRD: Evolutionary Strategy Discovery-Owned Job Creation Verification and Repair

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> GitHub issue: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/issues/650
> Assigned agent: Evonome-discovery agent.

> Historical repo snapshot: none for this verification PRD; use related canonical PRDs as background only.
> Related PRD: #634 Discovery Evolutionary Strategy Route Wrapper
> Related PRD: #625 Discovery Evolutionary Strategy Adapter from Training Strategize
> Related PRD: #620 Discovery / Training Porting Completion Audit
> Related PRD: #593 Discovery Method Porting

---

```yaml

slug: evolutionary-strategy-discovery-owned-job-creation-verification-repair

status: approved
prd_review_status: approved
ceo_approved: true
ownership: discovery_owned
configuration_output_contract: strategy_configuration_package_v1
canonical_job_category: genesis_evolutionary_strategy
```
