content.body:
# [PRD] Datafeed multi-resolution extension and UI coexistence

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.
> Related research/root PRD: #681 DSP-ready market data foundation for algorithmic trading research.
> Related approved DATA foundations: #810 raw-event foundation, #612 catalog enablement, #752 gap repair probe.
> Approved child PRDs: #685 stream-aware configuration, #686 dataset catalog and stream-specific quality surfaces, and #687 derived dataset registration/chart selector coexistence.
> Pending/future child PRDs: #688 strategy/training data compatibility gate.
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2.
> Base branch: `main`.
> Working branch: `feat/datafeed-multiresolution-coexistence-682`.
> Status: in progress on `feat/datafeed-multiresolution-coexistence-682` as parent/alignment PRD only.

---

title: Datafeed multi-resolution extension and UI coexistence
lifecycle: in_progress
ceo_approved: true
ceo_approved_at: 2026-06-05
pipeline_status: in_progress
prd_review_status: approved
assigned_agent: Evonome-data agent
worktree: /mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data
base_branch: main
working_branch: feat/datafeed-multiresolution-coexistence-682
project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2
implementation_mode: parent_alignment_only

---

## Current active session

- Active as of 2026-06-06 on `feat/datafeed-multiresolution-coexistence-682`.
- Mode remains parent/alignment only: update sequencing, dependency gates, and acceptance language without broad direct implementation.
- Recent DATA completion before this handoff: #686 completed via PR #919.

## CEO approval decisions

Approved on 2026-06-05 as a parent/alignment PRD only, with these binding decisions:

- #682 must not implement the broad multi-resolution platform directly. Code changes must be routed through approved child PRDs or separately approved slices.
- Strategy/training/backtest launch gating remains a future contract only. Actual enforcement/blocking belongs to #688 or another separately approved PRD and must coordinate with adversarial #897/#898.
- Raw-event storage, ClickHouse/high-volume infrastructure, and raw collector execution are not authorized by #682. #810 controls raw-event contracts and approved PostgreSQL metadata plus Parquet-first boundaries.
- Derived dataset generation and chart selector implementation are not authorized by #682. Route that scope to #687 after approval.
- #685, #686, and #687 are approved children. #688 remains pending/future until explicitly approved. #810, #612, and #752 are related approved DATA foundations.
- #682 may require child PRDs to expose preflight-readable facts, but does not authorize backtest/training/strategy enforcement or blocking.
- Provider-neutral behavior is required by default. Hyperliquid is a validation profile only; generalized child implementations must include synthetic non-Hyperliquid fixtures where applicable.
- Parent completion means child sequencing, dependency gates, and acceptance language are current; it does not mean every child feature is implemented.

---

## 1. Problem

Existing datafeed adapters, collectors, charts, backtests, and training paths are built around OHLCV candles. That must remain supported because many strategies only need candles and because OHLCV is cheaper, simpler, and sufficient for some trend, volatility, and lower-frequency cycle methods.

The DSP-ready data initiative adds raw trades, quotes, order books, activity-time bars, and derived fair-price datasets. If this is bolted on as a separate system, the product will drift into two incompatible data worlds: candle strategies in one path and microstructure/DSP research in another. If it is forced into the current OHLCV model, it will overload existing tables, confuse gap checks, and make the UI imply that every strategy needs high-volume tick data.

We need a coexistence layer: the current OHLCV adapter system remains the default path, while richer streams and derived datasets extend the same catalog, capability, quality, and strategy-selection surfaces.

## 2. Current observations

- The datafeed plugin guide already expects capability-driven adapters and lists OHLCV, quotes, order books, trades, funding, open interest, corporate actions, sessions, and execution fills as possible capabilities.
- `backend/app/services/datafeed/support_matrix.py` already declares exchange capability truth such as historical candles, live candles, order books, funding, open interest, and feature capability names.
- The frontend Datafeed Administration surface already has collector control, adapter health, symbol configuration, history download status, data coverage, and quality/recovery views.
- `SymbolConfigurationPanel` currently exposes symbol-level `Sync`, `Orderbook`, and `History` controls. This is a good starting point but is not expressive enough for separate candle, trade, quote, L2, derived-bar, and paid-provider import streams.
- Data quality UI and backend terminology are currently candle/gap oriented. Future datasets need stream-specific quality semantics so tick/order-book issues do not appear as OHLCV candle failures.

## 3. Product goal

Define the parent coexistence contract for extending the existing datafeed system into a multi-resolution data platform while preserving OHLCV as the default and backward-compatible data product. Operators should be able to see, enable, quality-check, and use OHLCV and richer datasets side by side without ambiguity, accidental high-volume subscriptions, or strategy/data incompatibility as child PRDs implement scoped slices.

## 4. Goals

- Keep existing OHLCV adapters, tables, APIs, charts, and strategies working without behavior changes.
- Add a capability and dataset registry that distinguishes raw streams, exchange candles, imported provider files, and derived datasets.
- Let adapters declare and expose stream capabilities independently: candles, trades, quotes, order book, funding, open interest, metadata, corporate actions, sessions, and derived outputs.
- Let operators enable high-volume streams explicitly, not as a side effect of enabling a symbol.
- Let strategy/research jobs declare dataset requirements and fail closed when the selected dataset cannot satisfy them.
- Update the interface so users understand whether they are looking at time OHLCV, raw events, order-book data, or derived activity-time bars.
- Preserve existing candle-first workflows as the easiest path.

## 5. Non-goals

- Do not implement broad parent scope directly; route implementation through approved child PRDs or separately approved slices.
- Do not remove or deprecate OHLCV.
- Do not require raw tick/order-book data for strategies that only request OHLCV.
- Do not store raw trades or order-book deltas in the existing OHLCV table.
- Do not add raw-event storage, ClickHouse/high-volume infrastructure, or live/raw collectors.
- Do not auto-enable trades, quotes, or order books for every enabled symbol.
- Do not implement strategy/training/backtest enforcement or blocking.
- Do not implement derived dataset generation or chart selector behavior directly in #682.
- Do not show non-time bars as if they were normal time candles without clear labeling.
- Do not make paid-provider data or licensed equities/forex data visible in unsupported export paths.
- Do not build a full DSP research workbench in this PRD; this PRD defines coexistence and UI foundations.

## 6. Core model

### 6.1 Keep three layers separate

1. **Source streams**: What adapters/providers deliver.
   - Examples: exchange 1m candles, raw trades, BBO quotes, L2 deltas, L2 snapshots, funding events, open interest, corporate actions.

2. **Stored datasets**: What the platform persists and can query.
   - Examples: PostgreSQL OHLCV candles, ClickHouse trade events, ClickHouse quote events, Parquet provider backfill files, order-book snapshots, data-quality summaries.

3. **Derived views**: Deterministic outputs built from stored datasets.
   - Examples: tick bars, volume bars, dollar bars, imbalance bars, reconstructed OHLCV, global VWAP, fair-price series, spread/depth features.

Adapters should not masquerade derived bars as source candles. Derived datasets must retain lineage to their input source streams.

### 6.2 Dataset identity

Introduce a dataset identity model that can represent both current OHLCV and future data:

- `dataset_id`
- `asset_class`
- `exchange` or `provider`
- `instrument_id`
- `venue_symbol`
- `data_kind`: `candle`, `trade`, `quote`, `book_delta`, `book_snapshot`, `funding`, `open_interest`, `corporate_action`, `derived_bar`, `derived_feature`
- `sampling`: `time`, `tick`, `volume`, `notional`, `imbalance`, `event`, `snapshot`, `as_of`
- `granularity`: `1m`, `1h`, `1000_ticks`, `$10m_notional`, etc.
- `source_mode`: `live_collector`, `historical_backfill`, `paid_provider_import`, `derived`
- `storage_backend`: `postgres`, `clickhouse`, `parquet`, `external_provider`
- `coverage_window`
- `quality_status`
- `license_visibility`
- `lineage` for derived datasets

Existing OHLCV rows become datasets with `data_kind=candle`, `sampling=time`, and `storage_backend=postgres`.

### 6.3 Backward compatibility rule

Current consumers that request candles should keep using the existing candle APIs unless they opt into the new dataset selector. Internally, the system can map the legacy candle request to a dataset query:

`exchange + symbol + timeframe` -> default `data_kind=candle`, `sampling=time`, `source_preference=canonical_ohlcv`.

This preserves existing behavior while making the new system queryable through a richer API.

## 7. Backend requirements

### 7.1 Capability declarations

Extend support/profile surfaces to separate these concepts:

- `supports_historical_candles`
- `supports_live_candles`
- `supports_trades`
- `supports_quotes`
- `supports_orderbook_l1`
- `supports_orderbook_l2`
- `supports_orderbook_l3`
- `supports_funding`
- `supports_open_interest`
- `supports_reference_data`
- `supports_corporate_actions`
- `supports_provider_import`
- `supports_derived_bars`

Keep existing booleans as compatibility aliases where practical. For example, `orderbooks_supported` can map to one or more order-book levels until migration is complete.

### 7.2 Stream subscription config

Replace symbol-only configuration with stream-aware configuration while preserving old fields:

- `sync_enabled` remains a compatibility alias for candle/live sync or symbol-level enabled status.
- `include_orderbook` remains a compatibility alias for enabling the default order-book stream.
- New config tracks stream toggles independently:
  - candles live
  - candles historical/backfill
  - trades live
  - quotes/BBO live
  - L2 snapshots/deltas live
  - funding/open interest
  - derived bar generation

High-volume toggles must be disabled by default and require explicit confirmation.

### 7.3 Storage boundaries

- Keep current PostgreSQL OHLCV tables for canonical candle data.
- Future raw tick/order-book storage remains governed by #810 and later explicit infrastructure gates. #682 does not authorize ClickHouse, high-volume storage, or raw collector execution.
- Store dataset registry, capability metadata, stream config, and quality summaries in PostgreSQL.
- Expose a unified query service that routes requests to the correct backend by dataset identity.

### 7.4 Derived dataset service

Future child PRD #687 should add a deterministic derivation layer, not inside the adapter itself:

- Inputs: one or more stored datasets.
- Outputs: registered derived datasets.
- Required metadata: parameters, code version/hash, input dataset ids, causality mode, warmup, quality gates.
- Initial derived outputs: reconstructed OHLCV, tick bars, volume bars, dollar bars, and global VWAP.

### 7.5 Strategy/data compatibility

Future child PRD #688 should define how strategies and model jobs declare required data capabilities:

- `requires: [OHLCV]`
- `requires: [OHLCV, FUNDING_RATE]`
- `requires: [TRADES, DOLLAR_BARS]`
- `requires: [ORDERBOOK_L2, QUOTES]`

The job launcher should show compatible datasets and fail before execution if requirements are missing, stale, or license-blocked.

## 8. Interface requirements

### 8.1 Datafeed dashboard

Keep the current candle-first dashboard but add a concise dataset summary:

- Active adapters by health.
- Active streams by type: candles, trades, quotes, L2, funding.
- Stored datasets by type.
- High-volume stream warning count.
- Quality status split by data type.

Copy should stay operator-focused. Avoid internal implementation narration in primary UI.

### 8.2 Adapter / source detail page

Show adapter capabilities as chips grouped by class:

- **Core**: OHLCV, metadata, sessions.
- **Microstructure**: trades, quotes, L1, L2, L3.
- **Derivatives**: funding, open interest, mark/index.
- **Reference**: corporate actions, calendars.
- **Derived available**: tick bars, volume bars, dollar bars, imbalance bars.

For each capability show:

- supported / unavailable / planned
- live / historical / imported / derived
- auth needed
- storage enabled
- quality status

### 8.3 Symbol / instrument configuration

Evolve the current Symbol Configuration table from two toggles into stream-aware rows:

Columns or expandable row sections:

- Symbol
- Base / quote / asset class
- Historical candles
- Live candles
- Trades
- Quotes / BBO
- Order book
- Funding / open interest where relevant
- Derived bars
- Storage estimate / risk badge
- Last quality status

Bulk actions should support filters:

- enable candle sync only
- enable selected microstructure streams
- disable all high-volume streams
- generate derived bars from stored trades
- import paid-provider history

### 8.4 Dataset catalog page

Add a dataset catalog separate from adapter runtime status.

Rows/cards should show:

- Dataset name: `Hyperliquid BTC 1m OHLCV`, `Binance BTC trades`, `Global BTC $10m bars`
- Data kind and sampling type
- Source/provider
- Storage backend
- Coverage window
- Quality tier
- License/export status
- Derived lineage link
- Actions: view quality, generate derived bars, open chart, use in research job

### 8.5 Data quality page

Split quality views by dataset kind:

- Candles: gaps, stale candles, reconstruction parity.
- Trades: duplicates, sequence gaps, out-of-order events, trade count anomalies.
- Quotes: stale quote windows, spread anomalies, crossed markets.
- Order book: checksum failures, sequence resets, snapshot/delta repair status.
- Derived datasets: input coverage, parameter hash, failed derivation windows.

Do not display trade/order-book quality problems as OHLCV candle gaps.

### 8.6 Charts and visual exploration

Default chart behavior remains OHLCV candlesticks.

Add an explicit dataset selector:

- Source: exchange/provider/global derived.
- Sampling: time, tick, volume, dollar, imbalance.
- Granularity/threshold.
- Display mode: candles, line, volume profile, depth, spread/dispersion overlay.

For non-time bars:

- Label the x-axis as event/bar index with timestamp ranges, not uniform time.
- Show start/end time on hover.
- Warn if users compare non-time bars against time-based indicators without compatible alignment.

### 8.7 Strategy and training UI

Future child PRD #688 should add a data requirement step before launch:

- Strategy input profile: candle-only, candle+funding, microstructure, derived bars, order-book.
- Compatible datasets list.
- Missing data and quality blockers.
- Default selection stays OHLCV when the strategy does not require richer data.

## 9. Recommended PRD decomposition

This PRD should be the coexistence/interface parent. Implementation can be split into child PRDs or task issues:

1. **Dataset registry and capability contract**
   - Schema/API changes only; no high-volume ingestion.
2. **Stream-aware symbol configuration**
   - Backend config compatibility plus UI table evolution.
3. **Dataset catalog and quality surfaces**
   - UI/API for dataset inventory and stream-specific quality.
4. **Raw event storage pilot integration**
   - Connects #681 storage decision to the existing datafeed system.
5. **Derived dataset generation and chart selector**
   - Tick/volume/dollar bars visible alongside OHLCV.
6. **Strategy/data compatibility gate**
   - Job launch requirements and fail-closed behavior.

Current approval state:

- #684, #689, #690, and #691 are complete foundation/guardrail PRDs.
- #685, #686, and #687 are approved child PRDs.
- #688 remains pending/future until explicitly approved.
- #810, #612, and #752 are approved related DATA foundations and must be respected by child implementations.

## 10. Parent alignment phased plan

### Phase 1: Contract-only compatibility extension

- Define dataset identity and capability schema.
- Add compatibility aliases so existing OHLCV APIs continue to work.
- Add tests proving legacy candle requests resolve unchanged.

Exit criteria:

- Existing datafeed tests pass.
- Dataset registry can represent current OHLCV without duplicate source truth.

### Phase 2: Stream-aware config and UI foundation

- Extend symbol config to represent stream toggles.
- Preserve old `sync_enabled` and `include_orderbook` behavior.
- Update Symbol Configuration UI with clear stream columns and high-volume confirmations.

Exit criteria:

- Operators can enable candle sync without enabling trades/order books.
- Operators can see but not accidentally enable high-volume streams.

### Phase 3: Dataset catalog and quality split

- Add dataset catalog API/UI.
- Split quality summaries by data kind.
- Keep candle gap recovery behavior isolated to candle datasets.

Exit criteria:

- OHLCV quality and tick/order-book quality are displayed separately.
- Dataset catalog can show coverage and source for current candle datasets.

### Phase 4: Derived datasets and chart selector — future child #687

- Register derived bar outputs from stored data.
- Add chart dataset selector with non-time-bar labeling.
- Keep default charts unchanged.

Exit criteria:

- Users can switch from standard OHLCV to a derived dataset without changing the default path.
- Non-time bars are not visually presented as uniform time candles.

### Phase 5: Strategy compatibility gate — future child #688

- Add strategy/model data requirement declarations.
- Add dataset compatibility checks to launch flows.
- Show missing requirements and quality blockers before jobs start.

Exit criteria:

- Candle-only strategies remain one-click compatible with OHLCV.
- Microstructure strategies cannot start against OHLCV-only datasets.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

- Existing OHLCV adapters and candle consumers remain backward compatible.
- New raw/derived dataset concepts are represented without overloading OHLCV tables.
- Operators can distinguish source streams, stored datasets, and derived views.
- High-volume stream enablement is explicit and guarded.
- UI surfaces show OHLCV and richer datasets side by side with clear labels.
- Quality checks are stream-specific and do not conflate candle gaps with tick/order-book problems.
- Strategy and training launch-flow requirements remain documented for future #688 implementation; #682 itself does not enforce or block launches.
- Tests cover legacy compatibility, capability mapping, stream config, dataset catalog responses, and UI display rules.

## 12. Suggested validation commands

- `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/services/datafeed tests/services/collector tests/api/test_collectors.py -q`
- Add targeted backend tests for dataset identity, compatibility aliases, and stream-aware config.
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run frontend/src/components/datafeed frontend/src/pages/datafeed`
- Add frontend tests for dataset labels, high-volume stream warnings, and non-time-bar chart selector copy.
- `git diff --check`

## 13. Human gates

Escalate before:

- changing or removing existing OHLCV APIs,
- migrating canonical candle storage,
- enabling trade/quote/order-book streams by default,
- adding ClickHouse or another high-volume storage dependency in any environment,
- executing raw/live collectors,
- exposing paid/licensed datasets in UI exports,
- allowing non-time bars to drive strategy launch without compatibility checks,
- implementing strategy/training/backtest enforcement or blocking,
- mutating adversarial/Genesis readiness, training handoff, promotion, or workflow state,
- expanding implementation beyond approved child PRD boundaries.



---

## 14. Cross-asset provider model update

The coexistence layer must support crypto exchanges, forex brokers, and stock brokers as first-class provider categories.

New audit PRD: #689 Cross-asset provider capability audit.

Dataset and capability surfaces should distinguish:

- exchange-native data from crypto venues,
- broker/account-specific prices from forex and stock brokers,
- third-party market-data vendor feeds,
- consolidated or synthetic datasets,
- derived datasets generated inside the platform.

UI and strategy compatibility rules must not imply that every provider supports raw trades, L2 books, historical ticks, corporate actions, or non-time bars. Each provider exposes only the capabilities proven by the provider audit and stored in the dataset/capability registry.



---

## 15. Reuse-first quality/backfill note

The coexistence layer should integrate with existing datafeed gap audit and repair behavior for current candle datasets instead of duplicating it. Stream-specific quality and repair paths should be added only where the current candle-specific components do not fit cleanly.

Related PRD #690 owns the detailed reuse inventory and quality/backfill architecture.



---

## 16. Backtest and historical feature quality gate update

The coexistence model must support preflight-readable data-quality facts for future backtests and historical app features; actual enforcement remains separately gated.

When a user selects a provider, instrument, dataset, sampling mode, and date range, future approved consumers should be able to verify that the requested window is clean before execution. If the data is incomplete or degraded, child PRDs may expose facts and safe repair options, but #682 does not implement execution blocking.

This requirement depends on #690 for verifier/backfill behavior and #688 for launch gating.



---

## Provider-neutral implementation requirement

The system must be provider-neutral by default. Implementation code should not hardcode a specific exchange, broker, or vendor as the default path for multi-provider behavior.

Requirements:

- Provider behavior must be driven by the provider/capability registry, configuration, adapter contracts, or explicit provider plugin metadata.
- Generic services must not branch on one provider slug when the behavior should apply to crypto exchanges, forex brokers, stock brokers, or market-data vendors.
- Provider-specific code is acceptable inside provider adapter/plugin modules, provider-specific fixtures, provider-specific tests, migration compatibility shims, and documentation examples.
- Existing provider-specific v1 paths may remain temporarily for backward compatibility, but new generalized work should wrap or migrate them behind provider-neutral interfaces.
- Default UI copy and API responses should describe provider capabilities, not imply that one crypto exchange is the canonical model for all future providers.
- Tests should include at least one non-Hyperliquid provider fixture or synthetic provider fixture for generalized services so provider-neutral behavior is proven.

Acceptance criteria addition:

- No new generic backfill, verifier, dataset registry, quality, strategy gate, or UI service hardcodes Hyperliquid, Binance, Kraken, IG, Interactive Brokers, or any other provider as a special default unless the code lives inside that provider's adapter or is explicitly marked as a temporary compatibility shim.



---

## 17. Master plan and conformance harness pointer

Program execution order, branches, checklist, and Codex `/goal` design are tracked in #681 section 18.

This coexistence PRD should be executed through the child/cross-cutting PRDs in this order:

1. #689 Provider capability audit — complete.
2. #684 Dataset registry and capability contract — complete.
3. #691 Provider-neutral datafeed conformance harness — complete.
4. #690 Market data QA, verification, and auto-backfill — complete.
5. #685 Stream-aware symbol configuration — complete.
6. #686 Dataset catalog and stream-specific quality surfaces — complete via PR #919.
7. #687 Derived dataset registration and chart selector coexistence — approved, not started.
8. #688 Strategy/training/backtest compatibility gate — draft/future.

#691 is a cross-cutting guardrail. It must prove that generalized registry, quality, configuration, catalog, and gating code works through provider capabilities rather than hardcoded provider names.



---

## 18. Codex `/goal` card for #682

Objective: keep the multi-resolution coexistence parent aligned while child PRDs implement dataset registry, conformance, QA/backfill, stream config, catalog/quality, derived charts, and compatibility gates.

Context to read: #681 section 18, #682, #684-#691.

Constraints: do not implement broad parent scope directly; route implementation through approved child PRDs. Preserve OHLCV as the default path. Do not authorize raw storage/collectors, derived generation/chart selector, or strategy/training/backtest enforcement from #682.

Done when: child PRDs remain sequenced, dependency gates are clear, tracker updates are current, and parent acceptance criteria reflect provider-neutral, cross-asset, quality-visible operation without claiming all child features are implemented.

Verification/evidence: parent issue checklist updated and child PRDs linked with current statuses.

Stop/escalate if: a child PRD expands scope beyond the parent, raw-storage decisions move ahead of #689/#681 gates, or OHLCV compatibility is threatened.

## 19. Parent alignment tracker

Current child sequencing and gates as of 2026-06-06:

- [x] #689 Provider capability audit is complete and remains the first cross-asset input.
- [x] #684 Dataset registry and capability contract is complete.
- [x] #691 Provider-neutral datafeed conformance harness is complete and remains the cross-cutting guardrail.
- [x] #690 Market data QA, verification, and auto-backfill is complete.
- [x] #685 Stream-aware symbol configuration is complete.
- [x] #686 Dataset catalog and stream-specific quality surfaces is complete via PR #919.
- [ ] #687 Derived dataset registration and chart selector coexistence is approved, not started, and is the next bounded child after parent alignment; it must not be implemented from #682 directly.
- [ ] #688 Strategy/training/backtest compatibility gate remains draft/future and must not be implemented from #682 directly.

Parent gate summary:

- #682 remains the active parent/alignment checkpoint; product-code changes belong to approved child PRDs or separately approved slices.
- OHLCV compatibility, provider neutrality, explicit high-volume enablement, and stream-specific quality semantics remain binding acceptance criteria for children.
- Raw-event storage and collector execution remain governed by #810 and related explicit storage gates.
- Derived dataset generation/chart selector implementation remains under #687.
- Strategy, training, and backtest launch enforcement remains under #688 and coordinated readiness/adversarial gates.

## DATA parallel-work boundary

This parent PRD may be maintained in parallel with adversarial-debate PRDs only as a sequencing/alignment artifact. # [PRD] Dataset registry and capability contract

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.  
> Parent PRD: #682 Datafeed multi-resolution extension and UI coexistence.  
> Related research PRD: #681 DSP-ready market data foundation for algorithmic trading research.  
> Requested by: CEO split of #682 into implementation-sized child PRDs.  
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.  
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.  
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2.  
> Status: Done — final verifier bug-check passed and PR #694 merged to main.

---

## 1. Problem

The existing datafeed stack is candle-first. Future raw streams and derived datasets need a shared identity and capability model, but the first implementation slice must not change legacy OHLCV behavior or require high-volume storage decisions from #681.

## 2. Product goal

Create the backend contract that lets the platform represent current OHLCV data and future streams as datasets, while preserving existing candle APIs, adapter behavior, tests, and operator workflows.

## 3. Scope

### In scope

- Dataset identity model for current OHLCV datasets and future stream/derived datasets.
- Capability declarations for adapters and providers.
- Compatibility aliases for current support matrix and adapter booleans.
- Dataset registry metadata stored in PostgreSQL/control-plane tables or equivalent existing metadata layer.
- Read APIs/services for listing registered datasets and adapter capabilities.
- Tests proving legacy candle requests resolve unchanged.

### Out of scope

- Raw trade, quote, or order-book ingestion.
- ClickHouse/object-storage production dependency.
- Derived bar generation.
- UI rebuilds beyond minimal labels needed to validate API responses.
- Strategy launch gating.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Dataset identity

Represent datasets with fields that can cover both existing candles and future streams:

- `dataset_id`
- `asset_class`
- `exchange` or `provider`
- `instrument_id`
- `venue_symbol`
- `data_kind`
- `sampling`
- `granularity`
- `source_mode`
- `storage_backend`
- `coverage_window`
- `quality_status`
- `license_visibility`
- `lineage` for derived datasets

Existing OHLCV rows must map to `data_kind=candle`, `sampling=time`, and the current storage backend without duplicating source truth.

### 4.2 Capability contract

Adapters/providers should be able to declare:

- historical candles
- live candles
- trades
- quotes
- order book L1/L2/L3
- funding
- open interest
- reference data
- corporate actions
- provider import
- derived bars

Existing support fields remain as aliases where practical.

### 4.3 Backward compatibility

Legacy candle consumers continue to call existing APIs unless they opt into dataset selection. The mapping from `exchange + symbol + timeframe` to the canonical candle dataset must preserve current behavior.

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- Existing OHLCV tests pass without behavior changes.
- Current candle datasets can be represented in the registry.
- Adapter capability responses distinguish candle, trade, quote, book, funding, and reference capabilities.
- Compatibility aliases preserve current support matrix semantics.
- No high-volume data stream is enabled or implied by this work.
- Tests cover dataset identity, capability aliases, and legacy candle request mapping.

## 6. Verifier checkpoints

- Checkpoint 1: Contract/schema/API review before any migration-like changes.
- Checkpoint 2: Compatibility review after legacy candle tests and new registry tests pass.

## 7. Suggested validation

- `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/services/datafeed tests/services/collector tests/api/test_collectors.py -q`
- Add targeted backend tests for dataset identity, capability mapping, and legacy candle compatibility.
- `git diff --check`

## 8. Human gates

Escalate before:

- changing or removing existing OHLCV APIs,
- migrating canonical candle storage,
- adding high-volume storage dependencies,
- enabling any trade, quote, or order-book stream by default,
- expanding into child PRDs #2-#5 without approval.



---

## 9. Cross-asset provider update

This registry must support provider categories from #689: crypto exchanges, forex brokers, stock brokers, and third-party market-data vendors.

Dataset identity and capability contracts must distinguish exchange-native data, broker/account-specific pricing, vendor-provided market data, consolidated data, and platform-derived datasets. Capabilities must be nullable or unavailable where a provider does not expose raw trades, L2/L3 depth, historical ticks, reference data, corporate actions, or funding/open interest.



---

## 10. Reuse-first quality/backfill note

Dataset registry work should expose current OHLCV datasets in a way that allows existing candle gap audit and repair services to keep working. If new dataset identifiers wrap legacy candle requests, compatibility tests must prove current audit/repair behavior is unchanged.



---

## 11. Backtest preflight registry update

Dataset identity and registry responses must provide enough metadata for future backtest preflight checks:

- verified coverage windows,
- quality state by window where available,
- dataset lineage,
- provider/source identity,
- license/export visibility,
- accepted exceptions,
- repair/backfill status references.

Legacy candle datasets should expose these fields through compatibility mappings where possible so existing OHLCV data can participate in backtest quality checks.



---

## 12. Provider-neutral registry requirement

The dataset registry and capability contract must be the source of truth for provider-specific behavior. Generic code should ask the registry what a provider supports instead of hardcoding exchange or broker names.

Provider slugs are valid as data identifiers, adapter registrations, fixtures, and documentation examples, but generalized services must use capability flags and provider metadata.



---

## 13. Codex `/goal` card for #684

Objective: implement provider-neutral dataset identity and capability contracts that represent current OHLCV and future crypto, forex, stock, vendor, and derived datasets.

Context to read: #681, #682, #689, #691, existing support matrix, collector tests, and datafeed plugin docs.

Constraints: preserve legacy candle APIs; do not add high-volume ingestion; avoid provider hardcoding in generic services.

Done when: current OHLCV datasets map into the registry, capability aliases preserve existing behavior, and synthetic/non-Hyperliquid fixtures prove provider-neutral lookup.

Verification/evidence: backend tests for dataset identity, capability mapping, legacy candle compatibility, and provider-neutral fixtures; `git diff --check`.

Stop/escalate if: legacy candle behavior would change, dataset identity conflicts with existing storage truth, or provider capability semantics are ambiguous.


---

## Approval scope update — 2026-05-14

Human implementation request opened #684 in full-auto coder-verifier mode on branch `feat/data-registry-capabilities-684`. Approval remains bounded to this PRD only. Human gates still apply for PR creation/merge, scope changes, vendor spend, credentials, licensed ingestion, production collectors, deployment, storage infrastructure/migrations, high-volume raw events, and child PRDs #691, #690, #685, #686, #687, #688, or the #681 raw event storage pilot.

lifecycle: done

## CEO approval decisions

Approved for bounded implementation on 2026-06-05 with these binding decisions:

- #685 may proceed before #810 implementation, but must align with #810 approved stream names, capability semantics, and provider-neutral boundaries. If #810 changes shared contracts before #685 merges, #685 must adapt before merge.
- This PRD authorizes disabled-by-default configuration/control semantics only. It does not authorize trades, BBO, L2, funding, or other high-volume collection.
- Preserve current `sync_enabled` and `include_orderbook` behavior exactly through explicit compatibility aliases and migration/regression tests. Any semantic change requires a separate human gate.
- Show controls only for provider-supported or planned capabilities. Unsupported streams must be unavailable, hidden, or fail closed based on provider capability metadata.
- Candle-only enablement and high-volume disablement may be executable. Bulk enablement of trades/BBO/L2 must remain preview/confirmation-gated and disabled by default.
- Provider capability registry/config/adapter metadata drives stream options. Hyperliquid may be a validation fixture, but generic UI/API/config must also support a synthetic non-Hyperliquid provider fixture.
- Do not touch adversarial-debate backtest readiness, training import, strategy gating, Genesis workflow surfaces, or promotion/readiness decisions.
- #684/#691 are complete. #810, #612, and #752 are approved related DATA PRDs, but #685 must not implement raw-event storage, catalog repair, or gap write behavior from those PRDs.

---

## 1. Problem

Current symbol configuration is too coarse for multi-resolution data. A symbol-level enablement path can accidentally imply expensive or high-volume streams. Operators need separate controls for candles, trades, quotes, books, funding, and derived outputs while preserving current `sync_enabled` and `include_orderbook` behavior.

## 2. Product goal

Make stream enablement explicit, safe, and backward-compatible so candle-first operation remains the default and microstructure streams require deliberate operator action.

## 3. Scope

### In scope

- Backend stream configuration model for enabled datafeed streams per symbol/instrument.
- Compatibility aliases for existing symbol fields.
- UI evolution of Symbol Configuration from coarse toggles to stream-aware controls.
- High-volume stream safeguards and confirmation copy.
- Bulk actions for candle-only sync and high-volume stream disablement.

### Out of scope

- Implementing raw event storage.
- Building new collectors for every stream.
- Capturing trades, BBO, L2, funding, or any high-volume stream data.
- Mutating production/preview schedules or runtime collector config outside explicit operator action covered by tests.
- Dataset catalog page.
- Strategy launch gating.
- Backtest readiness, training readiness, or adversarial-debate workflow changes.
- Derived dataset generation.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Stream toggles

Track independently where supported:

- historical candles
- live candles
- trades live
- quotes/BBO live
- L2 snapshots/deltas live
- funding/open interest
- derived bar generation request or availability

### 4.2 Compatibility aliases

- `sync_enabled` remains compatible with candle/live sync or existing symbol enabled behavior.
- `include_orderbook` remains compatible with the existing default order-book behavior until migration completes.

### 4.3 High-volume safeguards

Trades, quotes, and order-book streams are disabled by default. Enabling them requires explicit confirmation and clear storage/risk labeling. Bulk enablement of high-volume streams must be preview/confirmation-gated and must not be reachable through symbol-level defaults.

### 4.4 UI table evolution

Symbol rows should expose stream columns or an expandable section for:

- Symbol
- Base/quote/asset class
- Historical candles
- Live candles
- Trades
- Quotes/BBO
- Order book
- Funding/open interest
- Derived bars
- Storage estimate/risk badge
- Last quality status

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- Operators can enable candle sync without enabling trades, quotes, or order books.
- Existing symbol settings continue to behave as before.
- High-volume streams cannot be enabled accidentally through a symbol-level default.
- Bulk action supports candle-only enablement and disabling all high-volume streams.
- UI copy is concise and operator-facing.
- Backend and frontend tests cover aliases, stream toggles, and high-volume confirmation behavior.

## 6. Verifier checkpoints

- Checkpoint 1: Backend config compatibility, legacy alias, provider-capability, and migration review.
- Checkpoint 2: UI safety review for high-volume stream controls, confirmation/preview behavior, and concise operator-facing copy.
- Checkpoint 3: Provider-neutral rendering review with Hyperliquid and synthetic non-Hyperliquid fixtures.
- Final bug-check after scoped implementation is complete.

## 7. Suggested validation

- `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/services/datafeed tests/services/collector tests/api/test_collectors.py -q`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run frontend/src/components/datafeed frontend/src/pages/datafeed`
- Add targeted tests for stream toggles, compatibility aliases, disabled-by-default high-volume streams, synthetic non-Hyperliquid provider fixtures, and confirmation/preview states.
- `git diff --check`

## 8. Human gates

Escalate before:

- enabling trades, quotes, or order books by default,
- changing semantics of existing `sync_enabled` or `include_orderbook` without migration approval,
- adding storage dependencies from #681 or #810,
- collecting or storing raw trades/BBO/L2/funding data,
- changing backtest, training, strategy, Genesis, or adversarial-debate readiness behavior,
- expanding UI scope beyond symbol configuration.



---

## 9. Cross-asset provider update

Stream-aware configuration must be capability-driven by provider class. Crypto exchange symbols may expose trades, quotes, order books, funding, and open interest. Forex broker instruments may expose bid/ask pricing and candles but no universal last-trade tape. Stock broker instruments may depend on market-data subscriptions and exchange permissions.

The UI must only show enablement controls for capabilities that the provider audit and registry mark as supported or planned.



---

## Provider-neutral implementation requirement

The system must be provider-neutral by default. Implementation code should not hardcode a specific exchange, broker, or vendor as the default path for multi-provider behavior.

Requirements:

- Provider behavior must be driven by the provider/capability registry, configuration, adapter contracts, or explicit provider plugin metadata.
- Generic services must not branch on one provider slug when the behavior should apply to crypto exchanges, forex brokers, stock brokers, or market-data vendors.
- Provider-specific code is acceptable inside provider adapter/plugin modules, provider-specific fixtures, provider-specific tests, migration compatibility shims, and documentation examples.
- Existing provider-specific v1 paths may remain temporarily for backward compatibility, but new generalized work should wrap or migrate them behind provider-neutral interfaces.
- Default UI copy and API responses should describe provider capabilities, not imply that one crypto exchange is the canonical model for all future providers.
- Tests should include at least one non-Hyperliquid provider fixture or synthetic provider fixture for generalized services so provider-neutral behavior is proven.

Acceptance criteria addition:

- No new generic backfill, verifier, dataset registry, quality, strategy gate, or UI service hardcodes Hyperliquid, Binance, Kraken, IG, Interactive Brokers, or any other provider as a special default unless the code lives inside that provider's adapter or is explicitly marked as a temporary compatibility shim.



---

## 10. Codex `/goal` card for #685

Objective: evolve symbol configuration into provider-capability-driven stream controls while keeping candle-first workflows safe and simple.

Context to read: #684, #691, #682, #690, Symbol Configuration UI, collector config, and support matrix.

Constraints: high-volume streams stay disabled by default; controls only appear when supported or planned by provider metadata; preserve `sync_enabled` and `include_orderbook` compatibility; do not implement collectors, raw-event storage, schedule mutation, or backtest/training/strategy readiness changes.

Done when: operators can enable candle sync without enabling trades, quotes, or books; high-volume streams require explicit confirmation/preview; tests cover legacy aliases, disabled-by-default high-volume streams, and at least two provider classes or synthetic fixtures.

Verification/evidence: backend and frontend tests for stream toggles, aliases, high-volume confirmation, and provider-neutral capability rendering.

Stop/escalate if: enabling a symbol could implicitly enable costly/high-volume streams or a generic UI path requires provider-specific branching.

## DATA parallel-work boundary

This PRD may run in parallel with adversarial-debate PRDs only while it remains limited to datafeed symbol configuration and provider-capability controls. Shared backtest readiness, training handoff, strategy compatibility, Genesis workflow copy, portfolio/evidence artifacts, and promotion/readiness surfaces are explicitly out of scope.



---

## Implementation completion evidence

Completed on 2026-06-06 by the Evonome-data agent on branch `feat/stream-aware-datafeed-symbol-configuration-685`.

Evidence:

- Coder/verifier artifacts: `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/session-1780725410615`

- PR #927 merged to `main` for #687.

- Deferred follow-up: route-mounted data-preview integration is #926.
- Still not authorized: derived generation jobs, raw-event storage, strategy/backtest/training gates, execution semantics, default route changes, or Genesis/adversarial readiness mutation.

## CEO approval decisions

Approved for bounded implementation on 2026-06-05 with these binding decisions:

- #687 authorizes derived dataset registration metadata, lineage contracts, and explicit chart selector UI for existing, fixture, or registered derived datasets only.
- #687 does not authorize derived dataset generation jobs, raw-event ingestion/storage, or high-volume storage dependencies. Actual generation requires a later approved PRD or slice.
- Non-time bars and derived datasets are visual/exploratory only. Strategy, backtest, and training launch/gating belongs to #688 or another separately approved PRD and must coordinate with adversarial work.
- Synthetic, fair-price, and global derived series must never be presented as executable venue truth or execution prices.
- Default chart behavior and routes remain canonical OHLCV. Derived chart selection is explicit and opt-in.
- Derived options must render disabled/unavailable with clear copy unless required input capability and lineage metadata exist.
- Provider capability and lineage metadata drive derived dataset availability. Generic behavior must include a synthetic non-Hyperliquid provider fixture.
- Do not touch adversarial backtest readiness, training handoff, strategy gating, Genesis workflow surfaces, promotion/readiness decisions, or execution semantics.
- #682 parent and #686 catalog/quality are approved; #810 is approved as raw-event foundation but does not authorize raw capture or derived generation in #687.

---

## 1. Problem

Future derived datasets such as tick bars, volume bars, dollar bars, and fair-price series must coexist with standard OHLCV charts. If non-time bars look like uniform time candles, users may misread indicators, timestamps, and strategy behavior.

## 2. Product goal

Let users intentionally select registered derived datasets for visual exploration while preserving default OHLCV charts and clearly labeling non-time sampling. This PRD defines registration and selection semantics, not generation.

## 3. Scope

### In scope

- Derived dataset registration metadata and lineage requirements.
- Initial derived dataset types visible in catalog/chart selection when existing, fixture-backed, or registered.
- Chart dataset selector for source, sampling, granularity/threshold, and display mode.
- Disabled/unavailable states when lineage or required input capabilities are missing.
- Non-time-bar labeling, hover details, and compatibility warnings.
- Default charts remain unchanged.

### Out of scope

- Derived dataset generation jobs.
- Production-scale raw event ingestion.
- Raw-event storage.
- High-volume storage dependencies or ClickHouse/provider decisions.
- Full DSP research workbench.
- Strategy, training, or backtest launch compatibility gates.
- Execution-price semantics for synthetic, fair-price, or global derived series.
- Default chart route changes.
- Approving VPIN/order-flow toxicity as production signal input.
- Adversarial/Genesis readiness state mutation.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Derived metadata

Each derived dataset records:

- input dataset ids
- derivation type
- parameters
- code version/hash
- causality mode
- warmup/boundary behavior
- quality gates
- output dataset id and storage location

### 4.2 Initial derived outputs

Support registration and display for existing, fixture-backed, or registered datasets of these types:

- reconstructed OHLCV
- tick bars
- volume bars
- dollar/notional bars
- global VWAP or fair-price series where source data supports it, labeled as analytic/non-executable

### 4.3 Chart selector

Add explicit selection for:

- source: exchange/provider/global derived
- sampling: time, tick, volume, dollar, imbalance
- granularity/threshold
- display mode: candles, line, volume profile, depth, spread/dispersion overlay where supported

### 4.4 Non-time-bar safety

For non-time bars:

- X-axis must not imply uniform clock time.
- Hover shows start/end timestamp range.
- UI warns when time-based indicators or comparisons are not aligned.
- Synthetic, fair-price, or global series must be labeled as analytic/non-executable.

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- Default chart behavior remains standard OHLCV.
- Users can select an existing, fixture-backed, or registered derived dataset without changing the default path.
- Non-time bars are visibly labeled as non-time sampled.
- Derived datasets show lineage back to inputs, and unavailable derived options explain missing lineage or input capability.
- Tests cover selector labels, non-time-axis copy, lineage display, unavailable/missing-lineage states, synthetic price labeling, provider capability gating, and default chart preservation.

## 6. Verifier checkpoints

- Checkpoint 1: Derived metadata, lineage contract, and missing-input/unavailable-state review.
- Checkpoint 2: Chart UI review for non-time-bar labeling, synthetic/fair-price non-executable copy, and default OHLCV preservation.
- Checkpoint 3: Provider-neutral fixture review with Hyperliquid and synthetic non-Hyperliquid provider behavior.
- Final bug-check after scoped implementation is complete.

## 7. Suggested validation

- `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/services/datafeed -q`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run frontend/src/components/datafeed frontend/src/pages/datafeed`
- Add targeted tests for chart selector copy, non-time hover labels, unavailable derived options when lineage/input capability is missing, synthetic/fair-price labeling, provider capability gating, and default chart behavior.
- `git diff --check`

## 8. Human gates

Escalate before:

- using synthetic/global prices for execution decisions,
- launching strategies, backtests, or training jobs directly from non-time bars without separately approved compatibility checks,
- adding derived generation jobs,
- adding raw-event ingestion/storage,
- adding production high-volume storage dependencies,
- changing default chart routes,
- mutating adversarial/Genesis readiness or promotion state,
- expanding into a full DSP research workbench.



---

## 9. Cross-asset provider update

Derived dataset and chart-selection behavior must respect asset class and provider fidelity from #689. Non-time bars should only be offered when the selected provider supplies the required raw events or when an approved vendor-derived dataset includes the needed lineage. Otherwise options must render unavailable with clear copy.

Forex broker bid/ask streams, stock broker quote feeds, and crypto exchange trades/books may produce different derived datasets and must be labeled accordingly.



---

## Provider-neutral implementation requirement

The system must be provider-neutral by default. Implementation code should not hardcode a specific exchange, broker, or vendor as the default path for multi-provider behavior.

Requirements:

- Provider behavior must be driven by the provider/capability registry, configuration, adapter contracts, or explicit provider plugin metadata.
- Generic services must not branch on one provider slug when the behavior should apply to crypto exchanges, forex brokers, stock brokers, or market-data vendors.
- Provider-specific code is acceptable inside provider adapter/plugin modules, provider-specific fixtures, provider-specific tests, migration compatibility shims, and documentation examples.
- Existing provider-specific v1 paths may remain temporarily for backward compatibility, but new generalized work should wrap or migrate them behind provider-neutral interfaces.
- Default UI copy and API responses should describe provider capabilities, not imply that one crypto exchange is the canonical model for all future providers.
- Tests should include at least one non-Hyperliquid provider fixture or synthetic provider fixture for generalized services so provider-neutral behavior is proven.

Acceptance criteria addition:

- No new generic backfill, verifier, dataset registry, quality, strategy gate, or UI service hardcodes Hyperliquid, Binance, Kraken, IG, Interactive Brokers, or any other provider as a special default unless the code lives inside that provider's adapter or is explicitly marked as a temporary compatibility shim.



---

## 10. Codex `/goal` card for #687

Objective: register derived datasets and add chart selection that preserves default OHLCV behavior while making non-time sampling explicit.

Context to read: #684, #686, #691, #681 raw-event pilot decisions, and chart/datafeed UI code.

Constraints: no derived generation jobs; no full DSP workbench; no strategy/backtest/training launches from non-time bars without #688 gates; no synthetic/global prices for execution decisions; no default chart route changes.

Done when registered derived datasets have lineage and parameters, unavailable options fail closed, default charts remain OHLCV, synthetic/fair-price series are non-executable, and non-time bars show event/bar semantics with timestamp ranges.

Verification/evidence: backend tests for derived metadata/lineage and frontend tests for selector labels, non-time axis copy, hover ranges, and default chart preservation.

Stop/escalate if: required raw inputs are unavailable, lineage cannot be proven, or chart copy could mislead users about time uniformity.

## DATA parallel-work boundary

This PRD may run in parallel with adversarial-debate PRDs only while it remains limited to derived dataset registration and chart-selection display semantics. Shared backtest readiness, training handoff, strategy compatibility enforcement, Genesis workflow copy, portfolio/evidence artifacts, execution-price semantics, and promotion/readiness surfaces are explicitly out of scope.

# [PRD] Strategy and training data compatibility gate

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.  
> Parent PRD: #682 Datafeed multi-resolution extension and UI coexistence.  
> Depends on: child PRD 1, Dataset registry and capability contract; child PRD 3, Dataset catalog and stream-specific quality surfaces.  
> Related research PRD: #681 DSP-ready market data foundation for algorithmic trading research.  
> Requested by: CEO split of #682 into implementation-sized child PRDs.  
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.  
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.  
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2.  
> Status: PRD draft; not approved for implementation.

---

## 1. Problem

Strategies and model-training jobs can become invalid if they run against datasets that lack required capabilities, coverage, freshness, license permissions, or quality. Candle-only strategies should remain easy, but microstructure and derived-data strategies must fail closed before execution.

## 2. Product goal

Add a compatibility gate to strategy and training launch flows so jobs declare data requirements, show compatible datasets, and block runs with missing, stale, low-quality, or license-blocked data.

## 3. Scope

### In scope

- Data requirement declarations for strategies and model jobs.
- Dataset compatibility checks before launch.
- UI step showing compatible datasets, missing requirements, quality blockers, and license blockers.
- OHLCV remains the default for candle-only strategies.
- Fail-closed launch behavior for unsupported microstructure requirements.

### Out of scope

- Building new strategies.
- Raw event ingestion.
- Derived bar generation.
- Model performance claims.
- Vendor/license procurement.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Requirement declarations

Support profiles such as:

- candle-only
- candle + funding
- trades + derived bars
- order book L2 + quotes
- custom capability requirements where needed

### 4.2 Compatibility checks

Before launch, validate:

- required data kind/capability exists
- coverage window is sufficient
- freshness/staleness is acceptable
- quality tier/status meets the job threshold
- license/export restrictions allow the job use case
- derived dataset lineage satisfies requirements

### 4.3 UI behavior

Launch flow shows:

- strategy input profile
- compatible datasets
- selected dataset
- missing requirements
- quality blockers
- license blockers
- safe default selection for candle-only strategies

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- Candle-only strategies remain one-click compatible with current OHLCV defaults.
- Microstructure strategies cannot launch against OHLCV-only datasets.
- Launch flow explains missing data and quality blockers before execution.
- License-blocked datasets are not selectable for unsupported job modes.
- Tests cover requirement declarations, compatibility matching, fail-closed behavior, and UI blocker states.

## 6. Verifier checkpoints

- Checkpoint 1: Requirement contract and compatibility matching review.
- Checkpoint 2: Launch-flow fail-closed and default-OHLCV behavior review.

## 7. Suggested validation

- `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/services/datafeed tests/services/training tests/api -q`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run frontend/src/components/datafeed frontend/src/pages/datafeed frontend/src/pages/training`
- Add targeted tests for dataset compatibility, missing requirement blockers, and candle-only defaults.
- `git diff --check`

## 8. Human gates

Escalate before:

- changing default behavior for candle-only strategy launches,
- allowing non-time bars to drive launches without explicit compatibility checks,
- exposing paid/licensed datasets to unsupported workflows,
- expanding scope into strategy implementation or model claims.



---

## 9. Cross-asset provider update

Strategy and training compatibility checks must account for provider class from #689. A strategy requiring raw trades, order-book depth, NBBO, corporate actions, funding, open interest, or account-specific broker prices must only launch when the selected provider and dataset explicitly satisfy those requirements.

Candle-only workflows remain the default when a strategy does not require richer data.



---

## 10. Reuse-first quality/backfill note

Strategy and training compatibility gates should consume existing candle quality/backfill status for OHLCV datasets where available. New blockers for trades, quotes, order books, corporate actions, broker prices, or derived datasets should be added separately when the existing candle-gap state does not apply.



---

## 11. Backtest and app-feature preflight update

This compatibility gate applies to future backtests and historical app features, not only strategy/training launches.

Before a backtest runs, the selected dataset must be checked against the requested provider, instrument, data kind, timeframe/sampling, and date window. A backtest from `2025-01-01` to `2026-01-01` must verify that the full requested window is clean enough for the strategy's declared requirements.

If data is unclean, the user should see the issue before execution and be offered a safe action such as "clean data first". That action should trigger the approved verifier/backfill workflow from #690, then rerun validation before launch.

"Force clean" means force repair and verification. It must not mean bypass quality checks or silently accept incomplete data.

Acceptance criteria additions:

- Backtest launch checks verified coverage for the full requested window.
- Backtest launch blocks missing, degraded, repairing, unknown, stale, or license-blocked data unless an explicit degraded/experimental run mode is approved.
- The user can trigger a bounded clean/backfill workflow for the selected dataset/window.
- Backtest results record dataset ids, quality state, coverage, accepted exceptions, and repair provenance.



---

## Provider-neutral implementation requirement

The system must be provider-neutral by default. Implementation code should not hardcode a specific exchange, broker, or vendor as the default path for multi-provider behavior.

Requirements:

- Provider behavior must be driven by the provider/capability registry, configuration, adapter contracts, or explicit provider plugin metadata.
- Generic services must not branch on one provider slug when the behavior should apply to crypto exchanges, forex brokers, stock brokers, or market-data vendors.
- Provider-specific code is acceptable inside provider adapter/plugin modules, provider-specific fixtures, provider-specific tests, migration compatibility shims, and documentation examples.
- Existing provider-specific v1 paths may remain temporarily for backward compatibility, but new generalized work should wrap or migrate them behind provider-neutral interfaces.
- Default UI copy and API responses should describe provider capabilities, not imply that one crypto exchange is the canonical model for all future providers.
- Tests should include at least one non-Hyperliquid provider fixture or synthetic provider fixture for generalized services so provider-neutral behavior is proven.

Acceptance criteria addition:

- No new generic backfill, verifier, dataset registry, quality, strategy gate, or UI service hardcodes Hyperliquid, Binance, Kraken, IG, Interactive Brokers, or any other provider as a special default unless the code lives inside that provider's adapter or is explicitly marked as a temporary compatibility shim.



---

## 12. Codex `/goal` card for #688

Objective: block strategies, training jobs, backtests, and historical app features from running on incompatible or unclean datasets.

Context to read: #684, #686, #690, #691, future backtester plans, strategy/training launch flows, and dataset quality contracts.

Constraints: candle-only defaults remain simple; degraded/experimental runs must be explicit; "force clean" means repair and verify, not bypass quality checks.

Done when: launch/preflight checks validate provider, instrument, data kind, sampling, date window, coverage, quality, license, and lineage before execution.

Verification/evidence: tests for requirement declarations, dataset matching, backtest-window preflight, fail-closed blockers, clean/backfill actions, and result provenance.

Stop/escalate if: launch blocking policy would break existing candle-only flows, licensed data rules are unclear, or quality state is insufficient to decide safely.

# [Research PRD] Cross-asset provider capability audit for crypto, forex, and stock-broker data

> Canonical PRD source: this GitHub issue.  
> Parent research PRD: #681 DSP-ready market data foundation for algorithmic trading research.  
> Related coexistence PRD: #682 Datafeed multi-resolution extension and UI coexistence.  
> Requested by: CEO clarification that the software is intended for crypto exchanges, forex brokers, and stock brokers.  
> Assigned agent: Evonome-data agent.  
> Worktree: `/mnt/hyperliquid-data/projects/worktrees/Evonome-data`.  
> GitHub Project: https://github.com/users/hyperbotsx/projects/2.  
> Status: done; research/audit complete; final verifier approved; PR opened: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/692.
> Approval state: CEO approved.
> CEO approved at: 2026-05-12.

---

## 1. Problem

The platform is intended to support crypto exchanges, forex brokers, and stock brokers. These provider classes do not expose the same data. Crypto venues often expose trades, candles, funding, open interest, BBO, and L2 order books. Forex brokers often expose account-specific bid/ask prices and candles rather than a universal last-trade tape. Stock brokers and equity data vendors may expose trades, quotes, NBBO, market depth, reference data, corporate actions, and historical bars, but access is constrained by subscriptions, exchange agreements, redistribution limits, and rate limits.

Before selecting storage, ingestion, or UI defaults, we need a provider capability audit that answers what data can be obtained, at what fidelity, under what license, and whether it is suitable for DSP, non-time bars, strategy launch, and model training.

## 2. Product goal

Create a cross-asset provider capability matrix and recommendation package for integrating crypto exchanges, forex brokers, and stock-broker/market-data providers into the Evonome datafeed model.

## 3. Providers to audit

### 3.1 Crypto exchange/provider candidates

Initial required providers:

- Hyperliquid
- Binance
- Kraken

Optional benchmark candidates if needed:

- Coinbase
- OKX
- Tardis.dev
- Kaiko
- CoinAPI
- Coin Metrics / CCData
- Amberdata

### 3.2 Forex broker/provider candidates

Initial required providers:

- IG Markets
- Interactive Brokers

Recommended additions for comparison:

- OANDA
- Dukascopy
- TrueFX
- dxFeed / Cboe FX or similar composite FX feeds
- Polygon forex data where licensing and quality fit

### 3.3 Stock broker/provider candidates

Initial required providers:

- Interactive Brokers

Recommended additions for comparison:

- Alpaca
- Polygon
- Databento
- dxFeed
- AlgoSeek
- Intrinio

## 4. Capability matrix requirements

For each provider, record whether the provider supports:

- Asset classes: crypto spot, crypto perps/futures, forex, equities, futures, options, indices, CFDs.
- Historical OHLCV/candles.
- Live candles or live aggregate bars.
- Raw trades or time-and-sales.
- Quote/BBO data.
- L1 top-of-book.
- L2 market-by-price / depth.
- L3 market-by-order where available.
- Historical tick data.
- Historical depth data.
- Funding, open interest, mark/index prices for derivatives.
- Corporate actions, splits, dividends, reference data, sessions, and calendars.
- Account-specific broker prices versus exchange/consolidated market data.
- Replay or bulk export formats.
- Timestamp precision and semantics: exchange event time, receive time, provider time, sequence ids.
- Backfill depth and completeness claims.
- Rate limits and connection limits.
- Authentication, subscription, exchange agreement, and account requirements.
- License/export restrictions and redistribution constraints.

## 5. Provider-fit scoring

Score each provider from 1 to 5 for:

- Data fidelity for DSP and non-time bars.
- Historical backfill quality.
- Live capture quality.
- Timestamp and sequence quality.
- Order-book suitability.
- Cross-asset coverage.
- API maturity and SDK fit.
- Cost and licensing practicality.
- Suitability as canonical data source.
- Suitability as benchmark or secondary source.

## 6. Initial hypotheses to validate

- Hyperliquid is a strong crypto-native source for trades, BBO, L2 book, candles, funding/perp context, and owned live capture.
- Binance is a strong CEX benchmark for high-liquidity crypto trades, candles, and depth streams.
- Kraken is a useful secondary CEX source for crypto trades, OHLC, ticker/BBO, and L2 order book data.
- IG Markets is likely useful for broker/CFD/forex/indices price feeds and historical bars, but may be weaker for raw exchange-level microstructure.
- Interactive Brokers is strategically important for stocks, futures, options, and FX, but access depends on subscriptions, exchange permissions, pacing limits, and licensing.
- OANDA may be a practical forex-first benchmark for candles and account-specific bid/ask price streams.
- Databento/dxFeed/AlgoSeek/Polygon-style vendors may be better canonical or benchmark sources for equities than broker APIs alone.

## 7. Audit outputs

The audit should produce:

1. Provider capability matrix.
2. Asset-class coverage map.
3. Data-fidelity scorecard.
4. Licensing and redistribution risk summary.
5. API/rate-limit/subscription summary.
6. Recommended first provider per asset class:
   - crypto exchange source,
   - crypto benchmark source,
   - forex broker/source,
   - stock broker/source,
   - institutional market-data vendor if broker APIs are insufficient.
7. Recommended implementation sequencing for #681 and #682 child PRDs.
8. Explicit blockers that require CEO approval before spend, licensed data ingestion, or production collectors.

## 8. Acceptance criteria

- Hyperliquid, Binance, Kraken, IG Markets, and Interactive Brokers are audited with source links to official docs or vendor terms.
- At least one forex-specific alternative and two stock-market-data alternatives are compared against broker APIs.
- The final matrix distinguishes exchange data, broker/account-specific prices, and third-party market-data vendor feeds.
- The audit states which providers can support raw trades, quotes, L2/L3 books, historical ticks, and historical depth.
- The audit identifies which providers can support current OHLCV-only workflows and which can support DSP/non-time-bar research.
- Licensing, redistribution, and subscription constraints are captured before any production ingestion work is approved.
- The audit recommends whether IG should be included in the first production data roadmap or treated as secondary/limited-fidelity.
- The audit recommends whether Interactive Brokers should be canonical, benchmark, execution-adjacent, or research-only for each asset class.

## 9. Suggested validation/evidence

- Official API documentation links for every provider capability claim.
- Trial/sample payloads where available.
- Small authenticated probe only after CEO approves credentials/subscriptions.
- No production collectors and no paid commitments during this audit.
- `gh issue view <audit-issue> --json labels,projectItems` to confirm project/label wiring.

## 10. Human gates

Escalate before:

- spending money on vendor trials or subscriptions,
- accepting exchange agreements or redistribution terms,
- ingesting licensed equities/forex data into shared infrastructure,
- using broker/account-specific prices as canonical exchange truth,
- building production collectors,
- adding high-volume storage dependencies,
- expanding beyond the providers listed in this audit without CEO approval.



---

## 11. Provider-neutral architecture requirement

The provider audit should explicitly identify which capabilities can be modeled generically and which require provider-specific adapter policy. The resulting implementation guidance must avoid making any audited provider the hardcoded default for crypto, forex, or stock-broker behavior.

The audit should recommend provider-neutral capability names and provider-specific policy fields for rate limits, auth, licensing, sequence/checksum handling, timestamp semantics, and backfill support.



---

## 12. Codex `/goal` card for #689

Objective: audit provider capabilities for crypto exchanges, forex brokers, stock brokers, and market-data vendors and recommend first integrations.

Context to read: #681, #682, #684, #690, #691, official provider docs, and vendor/license notes.

Constraints: no paid commitments, no credentials, no production collectors, and no unsupported claims without source links.

Done when: Hyperliquid, Binance, Kraken, IG Markets, Interactive Brokers, plus comparison forex/equities providers have source-linked capability, fidelity, licensing, and integration scores.

Verification/evidence: matrix with official docs links, capability scores, subscription/license risks, and recommended first provider per asset class.

Stop/escalate if: provider terms require legal review, access needs paid subscriptions, or official docs conflict with implementation assumptions.




---

## 13. Completion evidence

- Research artifacts: `dev-plans/agentops/coder-verifier-workflow/runs/session-1778573803849/`.
- Final verifier decision: approved; open findings 0; bug-check passed.
- PR: https://github.com/hyperbotsx/SoldierOne/pull/692.
- Master execution plan updated in #681 with #689-driven sequencing and provider decisions.
